recipe.title: Chicken fried rice
recipe.summary: A quick weeknight fried rice with chicken thigh, scrambled egg, peas and spring onion, made with cold cooked rice so the grains stay separate.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 1.5 cm pieces
4 spring onions, thinly sliced, whites and greens separated
4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice (from about 1½ cups raw)
method: Toss the chicken pieces with the salt and white pepper, then prep the spring onions, garlic, ginger and rice, and mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil.
Cook the chicken in 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over high heat for 4 minutes, until golden and cooked through, then set aside.
Scramble the eggs in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 30 seconds until just set, and add them to the chicken.
Fry the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil over high heat for 30 seconds, then stir-fry the cold rice and peas for 3 minutes until hot and the peas are tender.
Add the sauce mix and toss for 1 minute until evenly coloured, then return the chicken and egg for 1 minute until steaming, and stir through the spring onion greens.

stages.title: Prepare everything
steps: Cut the chicken thigh fillets into 1.5 cm pieces and toss with 1 tsp of the salt and the white pepper in a bowl.
Slice the spring onions, keeping the whites and greens in separate piles, then chop the garlic and grate the ginger.

Break up any clumps in the cold cooked rice with your fingers so the grains are loose, and mix the light soy sauce, oyster sauce and sesame oil in a small cup. Do not use freshly cooked rice, as it turns mushy in the pan.

stages.title: Cook the chicken and egg
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat until it shimmers, about 1 minute.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and no pink remains in the centre of the largest piece. Tip it onto a plate.
Return the pan to medium-high heat with 1 tbsp of the oil, pour in the beaten eggs and stir for 30 seconds until just set but still soft, then slide them onto the plate with the chicken.

stages.title: Fry the rice
steps: Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the same pan over high heat, then add the spring onion whites, garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the cold rice and the frozen peas and stir-fry for 3 minutes, pressing the rice against the pan, until the grains are hot, bouncing around and the peas are tender.

Pour the soy sauce mixture around the edge of the pan, toss for 1 minute until the rice is evenly coloured, then return the chicken and egg and toss for 1 minute until steaming hot, breaking the egg into small pieces.
Turn off the heat, stir through the spring onion greens, taste and add a little more soy sauce if needed, then serve straight away.

tips: Cook the rice the day before and spread it on a tray to cool before chilling, so the grains dry out and fry rather than steam.
Keep the pan very hot and don't crowd it; cook in two batches if your pan is smaller than 30 cm.
Swap the oyster sauce for an extra 1 tbsp light soy sauce if you want to keep it simpler.
variations: Use prawns instead of chicken and cook them for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian by using firm tofu or extra eggs, and use vegetarian mushroom stir-fry sauce in place of oyster sauce.
Add 1 tbsp chilli oil or a sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
recipe.storage: Cool quickly and refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 1 day. Reheat in a hot pan or the microwave until steaming hot all the way through; don't freeze.

recipe.title: Chicken schnitzel with slaw
recipe.summary: Crumbed chicken breast pan-fried until golden and crisp, served with a creamy, crunchy cabbage slaw and lemon.
ingredients: 1/2 cup (125 ml) vegetable oil, for frying
1/4 small green cabbage (about 300 g), finely shredded
1 lemon, half juiced, half cut into wedges
method: Whisk the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, some salt and pepper, then toss through the cabbage, carrots and spring onions and chill.
Halve the chicken breasts horizontally and pound the cutlets to 1 cm thick.
Coat each cutlet in the seasoned flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, pressing firmly.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a breadcrumb sizzles.
Fry 2 schnitzels at a time for 3–4 minutes per side, until deep golden and white through the centre, then rest 2–3 minutes.
Serve with the slaw and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Make the slaw
steps: In a large bowl, stir the mayonnaise, Dijon mustard, juice of half the lemon, 1/2 tsp of the salt and a pinch of the black pepper until smooth.
Add the cabbage, carrots and spring onions and toss until every shred is lightly coated in the dressing, then cover and refrigerate while you cook so the cabbage stays crunchy.

stages.title: Crumb the chicken
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thin cutlets, then place them between sheets of baking paper and pound with a rolling pin until an even 1 cm thick, which helps them cook through before the crumb burns.
Set up three shallow dishes: the flour mixed with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the remaining black pepper in the first, the beaten eggs in the second and the breadcrumbs in the third.
Coat each cutlet in the flour and shake off the excess, dip it in the egg and let the extra drip off, then press it firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides until completely covered.

stages.title: Fry the schnitzels
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for about 2 minutes, until a pinch of breadcrumb sizzles straight away when dropped in.
Cook 2 schnitzels at a time for 3–4 minutes per side, until deep golden and the chicken is white all the way through with no pink in the centre; do not crowd the pan, or the crumb will turn soggy.
Transfer each batch to a plate lined with paper towel and rest for 2–3 minutes so the juices settle, then serve with the slaw and the lemon wedges.

tips: Pounding the chicken to an even thickness is the key to crumb that browns at the same time as the chicken cooks through.
Press the crumbs on firmly and don't move the schnitzel around in the pan, so the coating stays put.
Make the slaw up to 4 hours ahead and keep it covered in the fridge, but add the dressing no earlier than 30 minutes before serving if you like it extra crunchy.
variations: Use pork loin steaks or veal instead of chicken, pounded to the same thickness.
Make it a parmigiana by topping each cooked schnitzel with napoli sauce and grated mozzarella, then grilling for 3–4 minutes until bubbling.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in separate containers; reheat schnitzels on a tray in a 200°C fan-forced oven for 10 minutes until hot and crisp, and serve the slaw cold.

recipe.title: Chicken satay stir-fry
recipe.summary: Chicken and crisp vegetables tossed in a peanut butter, soy and coconut satay sauce, served over jasmine rice in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
1 head broccoli (about 300 g), cut into small florets
method: Cook the rice with the water and salt: boil, then cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
While it cooks, prep the chicken, capsicum, broccoli, carrot, garlic, ginger and spring onions, and whisk the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy, sweet chilli, lime juice and pepper.
Sear the chicken in the oil in a large pan over high heat for 5 minutes, until golden and white through. Set aside.
In the same pan over medium-high heat, stir-fry the carrot and broccoli for 3 minutes, then the capsicum for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken, add the sauce and stir for 2 minutes, until bubbling. Serve on the rice with spring onions, peanuts and lime.

stages.title: Start the rice and prep
steps: Put the rice, water and salt in a medium saucepan over high heat and bring to the boil, about 3 minutes, until the surface is bubbling.
Cover with a tight lid, turn the heat to low and cook for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Do not lift the lid, as the steam is what cooks the rice.
While the rice cooks, cut the chicken, slice the capsicum and carrot, cut the broccoli into florets, chop the garlic and ginger, and slice the spring onions.
Whisk the peanut butter, coconut milk, soy sauce, sweet chilli sauce, lime juice and black pepper in a bowl until smooth and pourable.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden. Do not crowd the pan or the chicken will steam instead of browning.
Cut one piece open to check it is white all the way through with no pink, then move the chicken to a plate.

stages.title: Stir-fry and finish
steps: Return the same pan to medium-high heat, add the carrot and broccoli, and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green.
Add the capsicum and cook for 2 minutes, until just tender but still crisp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Do not let the garlic brown or it turns bitter.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan, pour in the sauce and stir for 2 minutes, until bubbling and coating everything. Add a splash of water if it is too thick.
Fluff the rested rice with a fork and divide it among bowls. Top with the satay chicken, spring onions and peanuts, with lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Use thigh fillets rather than breast, as they stay juicy and forgive a minute of overcooking.
Whisk the sauce before you start cooking, because the stir-fry moves quickly once the pan is hot.
If the sauce thickens too much, loosen it with a splash of water or coconut milk.
variations: Swap the chicken for firm tofu, pressed and cubed, and use tamari for a vegetarian, gluten-free version.
Add 1 sliced red chilli or a teaspoon of sambal oelek to the sauce for more heat.
Use beef strips or raw prawns instead of chicken, cooking prawns for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for 3 days. Reheat in a pan or microwave with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Chicken laksa
recipe.summary: A Malaysian-style curry noodle soup made with store-bought laksa paste, coconut milk, chicken, rice noodles and tofu puffs, ready in 35 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, thinly sliced
method: Fry the laksa paste in the oil over medium heat for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add the chicken with the salt and black pepper and cook 4–5 minutes, until no longer pink outside.
Pour in the stock and coconut milk, then add the fish sauce and brown sugar. Add the tofu puffs and simmer gently 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 5 minutes until soft, then drain.
Ladle the soup over the noodles in bowls. Top with the bean sprouts, coriander and chilli, and serve with the lime wedges.

stages.title: Fry the paste
steps: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat, then add the laksa paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until it smells fragrant and the oil starts to separate.

Add the chicken, sprinkle with the salt and black pepper, and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the outside is no longer pink. Don't let the paste catch and burn on the base of the pan; add a splash of stock if it sticks.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Pour in the chicken stock and coconut milk, then stir in the fish sauce and brown sugar.

Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then add the tofu puffs and cook for 10 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the centre and the tofu has soaked up the broth. Keep it at a gentle simmer, as boiling hard can make the coconut milk split.

stages.title: Cook the noodles and serve
steps: While the soup simmers, place the rice vermicelli in a large heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and leave for 5 minutes, until soft and no longer brittle, then drain well.
Divide the noodles among 4 bowls and ladle the hot soup, chicken and tofu puffs over the top.
Top with the bean sprouts and coriander, and add the sliced chilli if using. Serve straight away with the lime wedges for squeezing over.

tips: Use chicken thighs rather than breast, as they stay tender in the simmering broth.
Laksa pastes vary in heat, so start with less if yours is hot and add more at the end to taste.
Soak the noodles separately rather than in the soup so they don't turn soft and swell up in the leftovers.
variations: Swap the chicken for peeled raw prawns and add them in the last 3 minutes, until pink and curled.
For a vegetarian version, use vegetable stock, leave out the chicken and fish sauce, and use soy sauce instead, adding extra tofu and green beans.
recipe.storage: Keep the soup and noodles separately in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the soup gently on the stove until steaming, and pour over the noodles. Not recommended for freezing, as the coconut milk can split.

recipe.title: Honey soy chicken stir-fry
recipe.summary: Tender chicken thigh, broccoli and capsicum in a sticky honey soy garlic sauce, served over steamed rice in about 25 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into small florets
method: Cook the rice in water in a covered pan on low heat for 12–15 minutes, until tender, and toss the chicken in the cornflour, salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large pan on high. Cook the chicken 5–6 minutes, until golden and white through, then set aside.
Add 1 tbsp oil to the pan on medium-high and stir-fry the broccoli and capsicum 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then add the soy sauce, honey, vinegar and water and simmer 2 minutes, until thickened.
Return the chicken, toss 1 minute until glossy, then stir through the sesame oil and spring onions and serve over rice with sesame seeds.

stages.title: Prep and cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it with 1 1/2 cups water in a covered saucepan over low heat for 12–15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
While the rice cooks, toss the chicken in a bowl with the cornflour, salt and black pepper until every piece is lightly coated.
Whisk the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar and water together in a jug, and have the garlic, ginger, broccoli, capsicum and spring onions ready by the stove, because the cooking moves quickly.

stages.title: Sear the chicken
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers.

Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on the outside and white all the way through with no pink in the centre. Avoid crowding the pan, or the chicken will steam instead of browning; cook in two batches if needed.
Transfer the chicken to a plate.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and finish
steps: Return the pan to medium-high heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil, then add the broccoli and capsicum and stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and just tender with a slight bite.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.
Pour in the sauce and bring it to a simmer, then cook for 2 minutes, until it thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan and toss for 1 minute, until everything is glossy and heated through. Remove from the heat and stir through the sesame oil and spring onions.
Serve over the rice, scattered with sesame seeds if using.

tips: Cut the chicken into even pieces so it cooks at the same rate and stays juicy.
Get the pan properly hot before adding the chicken so it browns rather than stews.
Use chicken breast if you prefer, but cook it a minute less to avoid drying it out.
Whisk the sauce before you start so nothing is rushed once the pan is hot.
variations: Swap the chicken for sliced beef rump or firm tofu, cooking the beef for 2–3 minutes only.
Add 1 sliced red chilli or 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for more heat.
Use snow peas, carrot or baby corn in place of the capsicum.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan or microwave with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Japanese chicken curry
recipe.summary: Tender chicken, potato and carrot in a thick, mild Japanese curry sauce made from roux blocks, served over steamed rice.
ingredients: 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
3 medium potatoes (about 450 g), cut into 3 cm chunks
2 large carrots (about 300 g), cut into 2 cm chunks
100 g Japanese curry roux blocks, roughly chopped
method: Brown the seasoned chicken in the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes, until golden. Add the onions and cook 3 minutes, until softened.
Add the potatoes, carrots, water and soy sauce. Bring to the boil, then simmer covered on medium-low for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Meanwhile, boil the rinsed rice in its water, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes, then rest 8 minutes until fluffy.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the roux until dissolved, then simmer on low for 3 minutes until thick, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes.
Check the chicken is white through with no pink, then serve over the rice.

stages.title: Prep the ingredients
steps: Cut the chicken thigh fillets into 3 cm pieces and season them with the salt and black pepper.
Slice the onions, then cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks and the carrots into 2 cm chunks so they cook at the same pace.
Chop the curry roux blocks roughly so they melt quickly later, and rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.

stages.title: Brown the chicken and onion
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the chicken in a single layer and cook for 4–5 minutes, turning once or twice, until golden on the outside. It will finish cooking in the sauce, so don't worry that it isn't cooked through yet.
Add the sliced onions and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until softened and starting to turn translucent.

stages.title: Simmer the curry and cook the rice
steps: Put the rinsed rice and the 2 1/4 cups of water in a medium saucepan over high heat and bring to the boil. Cover with a tight lid, reduce to the lowest heat and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid.

Meanwhile, add the potatoes, carrots, the 600 ml of water and the soy sauce to the chicken pot. Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer, covered, for 12 minutes, until a knife slides easily into a potato chunk.
Turn off the rice and leave it covered for 8 minutes, until the grains are tender and fluffy.
Take the curry pot off the heat and add the chopped roux, stirring for 2 minutes until fully dissolved. Adding the roux to boiling liquid makes it clump, so always take the pot off the heat first.

Return the pot to low heat and simmer for 3 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Stir in the frozen peas for the last 2 minutes, until bright green and hot. Cut open a piece of chicken to check it's white all the way through with no pink, then serve the curry over the rice.

tips: Use thigh fillets rather than breast, as they stay juicy through the simmer and are harder to overcook.
For a deeper, slightly sweet flavour, grate half an apple into the pot with the water.
Let the curry sit for 5 minutes off the heat before serving, as it thickens a little as it cools.
Most roux blocks come in mild, medium and hot, so pick the heat level your family likes.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g of firm tofu or a can of drained chickpeas, and use a vegetable roux.
Serve it as katsu curry by topping the rice with a crumbed chicken schnitzel and ladling the sauce over.
Add 1 tsp of chilli flakes or use hot roux for extra heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 2 months, though potato can go a little grainy once frozen. Reheat gently in a saucepan with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Lemon and garlic chicken tray bake
recipe.summary: Chicken thighs, potatoes, red onion and zucchini roasted together on one tray with lemon, garlic and oregano for an easy weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 2 zucchini (about 400 g), cut into 2 cm chunks
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Whisk the lemon zest and juice, olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Toss the chicken thighs and potatoes in the marinade, then spread on a lined tray in a single layer.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the potatoes start to turn golden at the edges.
Add the red onion, zucchini and lemon wedges and toss in the juices.
Roast 15 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through with no pink and the potatoes are tender.
Rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then top with parsley if using.

stages.title: Prepare the tray
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line a large, deep baking tray with baking paper.
Zest one lemon into a large bowl, then squeeze in its juice and add the olive oil, garlic, oregano, salt and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the chicken thighs and the potatoes to the bowl and toss well so everything is coated in the marinade.
Cut the second lemon into wedges and set aside.

stages.title: Roast the potatoes and chicken
steps: Tip the chicken and potatoes onto the tray, spreading them in a single layer with the potatoes cut side down and the chicken skin side up if it has skin; use two trays if crowded, as crowding makes them steam instead of brown.
Roast for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are starting to turn golden at the edges and the chicken is lightly browned.

stages.title: Add the vegetables and finish
steps: Take the tray out, scatter the red onion wedges, zucchini chunks and lemon wedges around the chicken, and toss the vegetables in the pan juices.

Roast for another 15 minutes, until the zucchini is tender and golden, the potatoes are easily pierced with a knife, and the chicken is deep golden and cooked through with no pink in the centre of the thickest piece (75°C on a meat thermometer).
Rest on the tray for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then sprinkle with parsley if using and squeeze over the roasted lemon wedges to serve.

tips: Cut the potatoes small and place them cut side down so they brown and cook in the same time as the chicken.
Use two trays rather than one crowded tray, otherwise the food steams and won't colour.
Marinate the chicken in the lemon and garlic mixture for up to 8 hours in the fridge for more flavour.
variations: Swap the zucchini for broccoli florets or capsicum chunks.
Add 150 g crumbled feta and a handful of Kalamata olives over the tray for the last 5 minutes for a Greek-style version.
Use bone-in chicken drumsticks and roast an extra 10 minutes.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a 180°C oven for 12–15 minutes until piping hot, or microwave until steaming throughout.

recipe.title: Apricot chicken
recipe.summary: Chicken thigh fillets baked in a sweet and savoury apricot and French onion sauce, served over fluffy rice.
ingredients: 1 x 35 g packet French onion soup mix
1 x 410 g can apricot halves in juice, drained
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into florets
2 tbsp chopped flat-leaf parsley, to serve (optional)
method: Heat the oven to 180°C fan-forced. Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown in the olive oil over medium-high heat, 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Soften the onion in the same pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, then put it in a baking dish with the chicken.
Whisk the soup mix, apricot nectar and water, pour over the chicken, add the apricots and bake 25 minutes, until bubbling and the chicken has no pink inside.
Meanwhile, boil the rice for 12 minutes until tender, adding the broccoli for the last 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Stir the cornflour and extra water into the sauce and bake 5 minutes until glossy. Serve over the rice and broccoli with parsley.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan-forced and pat the chicken thighs dry with paper towel, then season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in two batches for 3 minutes per side, until golden; don't crowd the pan or it will steam instead of browning.
Transfer the chicken to a baking dish and add the sliced onion to the same pan over medium heat, cooking it for 3 minutes until softened.

stages.title: Bake in the apricot sauce
steps: Whisk the French onion soup mix, apricot nectar and water together in a jug, then pour it over the chicken and onion in the baking dish.
Scatter the drained apricot halves around the chicken and bake for 25 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling and the chicken is cooked through with no pink in the middle (75°C on a meat thermometer).

stages.title: Cook the rice and thicken the sauce
steps: While the chicken bakes, rinse the rice and cook it in a saucepan of boiling water over medium heat for 12 minutes until tender, then drain well. Add the broccoli for the final 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender, and drain with the rice.
Mix the cornflour with the extra water until smooth. Stir it into the sauce in the baking dish and return to the oven for 5 minutes, until the sauce is glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Serve the chicken and sauce over the rice and broccoli, scattered with parsley if you like.

tips: Thighs stay juicy in the long bake, so don't swap in breast unless you cut the baking time and check it's cooked through.
Browning the chicken first adds deeper flavour; skip it on a busy night and just bake a few minutes longer.
Use apricot nectar, not apricot juice with added water, for a sauce that is properly sweet and thick.
Serve with extra steamed greens or a green salad to balance the sweetness.
variations: Use chicken drumsticks instead of thighs and bake for 40 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Stir in 1 tbsp Dijon mustard with the soup mix for a tangier sauce.
Swap the rice for mashed potato for a comforting winter version.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 2 months. Reheat in a covered pan or microwave until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Chicken Kiev
recipe.summary: Crumbed chicken breast stuffed with garlic and herb butter, browned in a pan and finished in the oven, so it's crisp outside and juicy inside.
method: Mash the butter with the garlic, parsley, dill, lemon zest and 1/2 tsp salt, roll into a log and freeze for 10 minutes until firm. Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced.
Cut a pocket in each chicken breast, season with the remaining salt and the pepper, and tuck in the butter.
Coat each breast in flour, egg and panko, repeating the egg and panko if any bare patches show.
Heat the oil in a large ovenproof pan over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 3 minutes per side, until deep golden.
Bake on a tray for 14 minutes, until crisp and 75°C in the middle. Rest 5 minutes and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the garlic butter
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, mash the softened butter with the garlic, parsley, dill, lemon zest and 1/2 tsp of the salt until evenly combined and speckled with green.
Spoon the butter onto a piece of baking paper, roll it into a log about 12 cm long and twist the ends tight. Freeze for 10 minutes until firm, which stops it leaking out later.

stages.title: Stuff and crumb the chicken
steps: Lay each chicken breast on a board and use a small sharp knife to cut a deep pocket into the thick side, taking care not to cut all the way through.
Season the chicken inside and out with the remaining salt and the black pepper.
Unwrap the butter, cut it into 4 equal pieces and push one into each pocket. Press the opening closed and, if it gapes, secure it with a toothpick.

Put the flour, eggs and panko in three separate shallow dishes. Coat each chicken breast in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in egg, then press it firmly into the panko until fully covered. Double-dip in egg and panko if any bare patches show.

stages.title: Brown the kievs
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large ovenproof frying pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, until a breadcrumb sizzles straight away.
Cook the chicken for 3 minutes per side, until the crumb is deep golden. Don't turn them too early or the crumb will tear, and don't crowd the pan.
Transfer the chicken to the lined baking tray, using tongs and handling it gently so the pockets stay sealed.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Bake the chicken for 14 minutes, until the crumb is crisp and the thickest part reaches 75°C on a meat thermometer, or the juices run clear when you pierce it.
Rest the kievs for 5 minutes so the juices settle and the butter cools slightly. Remove any toothpicks and serve with lemon wedges if you like, cutting in carefully as the butter will be hot.

tips: Freeze the butter until properly firm, otherwise it melts and leaks out in the pan before the chicken sets.
Press the crumb on firmly and double-coat in egg and panko for a sealed, extra-crisp crust.
Use a meat thermometer: 75°C in the thickest part means the chicken is cooked through without drying out.
You can stuff and crumb the kievs up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge, then brown and bake as directed.
variations: Swap the dill for chives or tarragon, or add a pinch of chilli flakes to the butter for some heat.
Fill each pocket with a slice of ham and a little grated mozzarella along with the butter for a cheesy version.
Use thinly sliced mushrooms and extra herbs in place of the chicken for a vegetarian version, shaping the filling into crumbed mushroom caps.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat on a tray in a 180°C fan-forced oven for 15 minutes until hot through and crisp; the microwave makes the crumb soggy.

recipe.title: Chicken and leek pie
recipe.summary: A creamy chicken, leek and mushroom filling under a golden puff pastry lid, a comforting British classic for a cold evening.
ingredients: 700 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Cook the leeks in the olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the mushrooms for 5 minutes until golden. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until no longer pink outside.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the chicken stock gradually. Add the cream and mustard and simmer 6 minutes until thick and the chicken is white inside.
Tip into a pie dish and cool for 10 minutes. Top with one pastry sheet, cut a cross, then add pastry strips around the rim and brush with egg.
Bake at 200°C fan-forced for 30 minutes until puffed and deep golden, then rest 5 minutes.

stages.title: Cook the filling base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the leeks and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and bright green with no browning.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, until they have released their liquid and turned golden. Stir in the garlic and thyme and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Push the vegetables to one side, add the chicken and season with the salt and black pepper. Cook for 5 minutes, turning, until the outside is no longer pink.

stages.title: Make the sauce
steps: Sprinkle the flour over the chicken and vegetables and stir for 1 minute so there are no dry patches. Pour in the chicken stock gradually, stirring, to avoid lumps.

Add the cream and mustard, then simmer over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Cut a piece of chicken open to check it is white right through with no pink.
Tip the filling into a 1.5 litre pie dish and let it cool for 10 minutes. Hot filling will melt the pastry, so don't skip this.

stages.title: Top and bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Lay one pastry sheet over the filling, trim the overhang and cut a small cross in the centre so steam can escape.
Cut the second sheet into strips and press them around the dish rim. Brush the top and rim with the beaten egg.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the pastry is puffed and deep golden and the filling bubbles at the edges.
Rest the pie for 5 minutes so the filling settles before serving.

tips: Wash the sliced leeks in a bowl of water to remove grit, then drain well so the filling isn't watery.
Cool the filling before adding the pastry, or the base will turn gummy and the lid won't puff.
Make the filling a day ahead and chill it, then top with pastry and bake just before serving.
variations: Use leftover roast chicken or turkey, stirring it in with the stock instead of browning raw chicken.
Swap the mustard for a splash of dry white wine added before the stock.
Add a cup of frozen peas to the sauce for a bit of sweetness and colour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days. Reheat portions in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 15 to 20 minutes until hot through, so the pastry stays crisp.

recipe.title: Chicken korma
recipe.summary: A mild, creamy chicken curry thickened with cashews and yoghurt, served over basmati rice, with gentle flavours that suit kids.
ingredients: 700 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Cook the onions in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 6 to 7 minutes, until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger, korma paste and garam masala for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Blitz the cashews with the chicken stock until smooth. Start the rice with the water and a pinch of salt: boil on high, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, and rest 5 minutes.
Add the chicken to the onions and stir for 3 minutes, until no longer pink outside. Pour in the cashew mixture and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and the chicken has no pink inside.
Reduce to low, stir in the yoghurt and cream for 2 minutes, until smooth and hot, without boiling. Season with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Fluff the rice with a fork and serve the korma over it, topped with coriander if you like.

stages.title: Prepare
steps: Dice the onions, grate the garlic and ginger, and cut the chicken thigh fillets into 3 cm pieces so they cook evenly.
Blitz the cashews and chicken stock in a blender for about 1 minute, until completely smooth with no gritty bits, then set aside.
Stir the yoghurt and cream together in a small bowl and leave it at room temperature so it is less likely to split in the hot pan.

stages.title: Cook the base
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat, then add the onions and cook for 6 to 7 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, korma paste and garam masala and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown or it will taste bitter.

stages.title: Simmer the korma and cook the rice
steps: Put the rice and water in a medium saucepan with a pinch of the salt, bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Rest, covered, for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
While the rice cooks, add the chicken to the pan over medium heat and stir for 3 minutes, until the outside is no longer pink.

Pour in the cashew and stock mixture, scraping up any bits from the base of the pan, and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is white through the centre with no pink when you cut a piece open.
Reduce the heat to low, stir in the yoghurt and cream mixture and cook for 2 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and hot. Do not boil it or the yoghurt may split.
Season with the remaining salt and the black pepper, and taste. Serve over the rice, topped with coriander leaves if you like.

tips: Use thigh fillets rather than breast, as they stay tender and juicy in the sauce.
Bring the yoghurt and cream to room temperature and keep the heat low when adding them so the sauce stays smooth.
Blend the cashews really well for a silky sauce; soaking them in hot water for 10 minutes first helps if your blender is weak.
Use a mild korma paste for kids and add a pinch of chilli for adults at the table.
variations: Swap the chicken for 800 g of cauliflower florets and a 400 g can of chickpeas for a vegetarian version, simmering for 15 minutes.
Use lamb leg steaks cut into pieces and simmer for 30 minutes, until tender.
Stir in 2 handfuls of baby spinach at the end for extra greens.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days or frozen for 2 months. Thaw overnight and reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water, until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Chicken adobo
recipe.summary: Filipino chicken braised in soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and bay leaves until tender and glazed in a sticky, tangy sauce.
ingredients: 6 chicken thigh cutlets, skin on (about 1 kg)
1 head garlic, cloves peeled and lightly crushed
method: Marinate the chicken in the soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns for 10 minutes, and rinse the rice.
Pat the chicken dry, then brown it in the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, 4-5 minutes skin-side down and 2-3 minutes on the other side.
Return the chicken to the pan with the marinade, vinegar, water and brown sugar, boil for 2 minutes, then cover and simmer on medium-low for 15 minutes, until cooked through.
Cook the rice on medium heat for 12-15 minutes, until tender.
Uncover and simmer on medium-high for 8-10 minutes until the sauce is glossy and thick. Season with salt and pepper and serve with rice and green beans if using.

stages.title: Marinate and prep
steps: Combine the chicken, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a large bowl and turn the chicken to coat.
Leave it to marinate for 10 minutes while you rinse the jasmine rice and measure out the vinegar, water and brown sugar.

stages.title: Brown the chicken
steps: Lift the chicken out of the marinade, keeping the marinade, and pat the pieces dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep frying pan or casserole over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Cook the chicken skin-side down for 4-5 minutes, until the skin is deep golden, then turn and cook the other side for 2-3 minutes. Do not crowd the pan; work in two batches if needed.

stages.title: Braise until sticky
steps: Pour off any excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp in the pan, and return all the chicken to the pan skin-side up.

Pour in the reserved marinade with the garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns, then add the white vinegar, water and brown sugar. Bring to a boil over high heat without stirring, about 2 minutes, so the vinegar mellows.
Reduce to medium-low, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until the chicken is tender and an instant-read thermometer reads 75°C or the juices run clear when pierced near the bone.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in a saucepan of water over medium heat according to the packet, usually about 12-15 minutes, until tender and fluffy.
Remove the lid, increase to medium-high heat and simmer for 8-10 minutes, spooning the sauce over the chicken, until the sauce is thick and glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper if needed, then serve the chicken and sauce over the rice with steamed green beans if using.

tips: Do not stir the sauce while the vinegar comes to the boil; this takes the harsh edge off the vinegar.
Patting the chicken dry before browning gives crisper, deeper golden skin.
Adobo tastes even better the next day, so make it ahead and reheat gently.
Use a little less sugar if your soy sauce is already on the sweet side.
variations: Use chicken drumsticks or pork belly pieces instead, simmering pork for about 40 minutes until tender.
Stir in 1/2 cup coconut milk at the final reduction stage for a creamy adobo sa gata.
Add 2 sliced red chillies with the garlic for some heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water until piping hot.

recipe.title: Massaman chicken curry
recipe.summary: A rich, mild Thai curry of chicken, potato and peanuts simmered in coconut milk and massaman paste, good over rice.
ingredients: 1 large brown onion (about 200 g), cut into wedges
600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
2 medium potatoes (about 400 g), cut into 3 cm chunks
1 large carrot (about 180 g), sliced into 1 cm rounds
method: Cut the onion, chicken, potatoes and carrot into even pieces.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat and cook the onion 3 minutes until soft, then stir in the paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir 4–5 minutes until no longer pink outside.
Add the coconut milk, potatoes, carrot, fish sauce, sugar and tamarind, then simmer gently over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until the potato is tender.
Stir in the peanuts, simmer 2 minutes until the chicken is white through, then season with salt. Serve with rice and lime if you like.

stages.title: Prep the ingredients
steps: Cut the onion into wedges, the chicken into 3 cm pieces, the potatoes into 3 cm chunks and the carrot into 1 cm rounds.
Keep the pieces of potato and carrot a similar size so they cook through at the same rate.

stages.title: Fry the paste and brown the chicken
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium-high heat, then cook the onion for 3 minutes, until it softens and the edges start to colour.
Add the massaman paste and stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant and the oil begins to separate.
Add the chicken and stir for 4–5 minutes, until the outside is no longer pink and is coated in paste.

stages.title: Simmer the curry
steps: Pour in both cans of coconut milk, scraping the base of the pan to lift any paste stuck to it, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Add the potatoes, carrot, fish sauce, brown sugar and tamarind puree, then reduce the heat to medium-low.

Simmer, partly covered, for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the potato is tender when pierced with a knife and the sauce has thickened slightly. Avoid a hard boil, which can make the coconut milk split.
Stir in the peanuts and cut a piece of the largest chicken open to check it is white through the middle with no pink, then simmer 2 minutes more.
Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed, then adjust with a little more sugar or tamarind to balance sweet and sour.
Serve over steamed jasmine rice, with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Use thigh fillets rather than breast, as they stay tender through the long simmer.
Don't let the curry boil hard, or the coconut milk can split and turn greasy.
Taste at the end and balance with fish sauce for salt, sugar for sweetness and tamarind for tang.
The flavour deepens overnight, so it can be made a day ahead.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g beef chuck cut into chunks and simmer for about 1.5 hours until tender.
For a vegetarian version, use firm tofu and extra vegetables, and replace the fish sauce with soy sauce.
Add a sliced red chilli or an extra spoonful of paste for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat gently on the stove until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

recipe.title: Pollo a la brasa
recipe.summary: Peruvian roast chicken with a garlic, cumin, paprika and lime marinade, crisp golden skin and a creamy green chilli sauce for dipping.
method: Heat the oven to 210°C fan-forced. Spatchcock the chicken by cutting out the backbone and pressing it flat.
Mix the garlic, juice of 2 limes, soy sauce, olive oil, cumin, paprika, oregano, 1 tsp salt and pepper, then rub it all over the chicken.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the juices run clear at the thigh.
Blend the chillies, coriander, spring onion, extra garlic, mayonnaise, yoghurt, juice of the last lime and 1/2 tsp salt for 30 seconds, until smooth.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then carve and serve with the sauce.

stages.title: Spatchcock and marinate
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C fan-forced and place a rack in the middle, so it is hot by the time the chicken goes in.

Place the chicken breast-side down and use kitchen scissors to cut along both sides of the backbone, then discard the backbone. Flip the chicken over and press firmly on the breastbone until it lies flat.
Juice 2 of the limes into a bowl, then stir in the crushed garlic, soy sauce, olive oil, cumin, paprika, oregano, 1 tsp of the salt and the black pepper until it forms a loose paste.

Rub the marinade over the chicken and under the skin of the breasts and thighs. Place it skin-side up in a roasting tray and leave it for 10 minutes while the oven finishes heating. Do not skip patting the skin with the marinade evenly, as bare patches will not colour well.

stages.title: Roast the chicken
steps: Roast the chicken at 210°C fan-forced for 40 to 45 minutes, until the skin is deep golden and the juices run clear when you pierce the thickest part of the thigh.

If you have a thermometer, the thickest part of the thigh should read 75°C. If the skin darkens too quickly before the time is up, cover the tray loosely with foil, but remove it for the last 10 minutes so the skin stays crisp.

stages.title: Make the green chilli sauce
steps: While the chicken roasts, or as it rests, put the green chillies, coriander, spring onion, the remaining garlic clove, the mayonnaise, yoghurt, the juice of the last lime and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt into a small blender or food processor.
Blend for about 30 seconds, until the sauce is smooth and pale green, then taste and add a pinch more salt if needed. Keep the seeds in the chillies for more heat, or remove them for a milder sauce.

stages.title: Rest and carve
steps: Move the chicken to a board and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle back into the meat and do not run out when you cut it.
Carve the chicken into pieces and serve with the green chilli sauce for dipping.

tips: For deeper flavour, marinate the chicken in the fridge for 6 to 24 hours and bring it out 30 minutes before roasting.
Pat the chicken dry with paper towel before rubbing in the marinade for crisper skin.
Serve with hot chips, rice or a simple tomato and red onion salad to round out the meal.
Spoon any tray juices over the carved chicken for extra flavour.
variations: Use 1.2 kg of chicken marylands instead of a whole bird and roast for 35 to 40 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Add 1 tbsp of aji amarillo paste or an extra chilli to the sauce for more heat and a more traditional flavour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days in an airtight container; the sauce keeps for 3 days. Reheat the chicken in a 180°C fan-forced oven for 10 to 15 minutes, until piping hot.

recipe.title: Korean fried chicken
recipe.summary: Double-fried chicken wings tossed in a sticky, sweet and spicy gochujang glaze, with a shatteringly crisp coating that holds up to the sauce.
ingredients: 1 kg chicken wings, split into drumettes and flats
method: Dry the wings, season with salt and pepper, then toss in the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder. Rest 10 minutes so the coating sets.
Warm the garlic, ginger, gochujang, tomato sauce, honey, soy sauce and vinegar in a saucepan over low heat for 2–3 minutes until bubbling, then stir in the sesame oil.
Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat to 160°C. Fry the wings in 2 batches for 10 minutes each until pale golden and cooked through.
Raise the heat to high, bring the oil to 190°C and fry all the wings for 3–4 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Toss the hot wings in the glaze for 30 seconds until glossy, then top with sesame seeds and spring onions.

stages.title: Prepare the chicken
steps: Pat the wings very dry with paper towel, then toss them in a large bowl with the salt and black pepper.
Mix the cornflour, plain flour and baking powder in a second bowl, then add the wings and toss until every piece is evenly coated in a thin, dry layer.
Rest the coated wings on a rack or tray for 10 minutes so the coating sets, which helps it stay crisp and stops it falling off in the oil.

stages.title: Make the glaze
steps: Place a small saucepan over low heat and add the garlic, ginger, gochujang, tomato sauce, honey, soy sauce and rice wine vinegar.
Stir for 2–3 minutes until the glaze is bubbling gently and smells fragrant, then remove from the heat and stir through the sesame oil. Don't let it boil hard, as the honey can catch and turn bitter.

stages.title: Double-fry the chicken
steps: Pour the vegetable oil into a large heavy-based pot to a depth of about 5 cm and heat over medium-high heat to 160°C, or until a pinch of flour sizzles steadily when dropped in.

Fry the wings in 2 batches for 10 minutes each, until pale golden and cooked through, turning occasionally, then lift onto a rack. Don't crowd the pot, as the oil temperature will drop and the chicken will turn greasy.

Raise the heat to high and bring the oil to 190°C, then fry all the wings together for 3–4 minutes, until deep golden and very crisp. Cut one open to check there is no pink near the bone and the juices run clear.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Put the hot wings in a large bowl, pour over the warm glaze and toss for about 30 seconds until every wing is glossy and evenly coated.
Pile onto a platter and scatter with the toasted sesame seeds and sliced spring onions. Serve straight away while the coating is still crunchy.

tips: Pat the wings completely dry before coating, as any surface moisture makes the crust soggy.
Use a thermometer if you can, because the oil temperature is what makes the double fry work.
Toss in the glaze just before serving, since the crust softens the longer it sits in the sauce.
Swap the wings for boneless thigh pieces cut into 4 cm chunks and fry for 6 minutes at 160°C, then 3 minutes at 190°C.
variations: Make it spicier by adding 1 tbsp of gochugaru or a pinch of chilli flakes to the glaze.
Use cauliflower florets instead of chicken for a vegetarian version, frying for 4 minutes then 2 minutes.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the crisp coating softens once glazed. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat on a tray in a 200°C oven for 10–12 minutes until hot and crisp again.

recipe.title: Chicken burrito bowls
recipe.summary: Spiced chicken breast over brown rice with black beans, corn, fresh tomato salsa, lettuce and avocado, ready in 30 minutes and high in protein.
ingredients: 2 x 250 g microwave brown rice pouches
400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
method: Mix the tomatoes, red onion, lime juice, coriander and some of the salt for the salsa. Halve the chicken breasts into thin steaks and rub with the oil, spices, remaining salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a large pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until golden. Flip and cook 4–5 minutes, until white through with clear juices.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice. Microwave the rice for 2 minutes until steaming.
Heat the beans and corn in the pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until hot. Build bowls with rice, beans and corn, lettuce, chicken, salsa and avocado, with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the salsa and spice the chicken
steps: Stir the tomatoes, red onion, lime juice, coriander and 1/4 tsp of the salt together in a bowl, then set aside so the flavours mingle.
Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thinner steaks, which cook quickly and evenly.
Mix the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper in a small bowl, then rub it over the chicken with the olive oil until evenly coated.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.
Cook the chicken for 5 minutes on the first side, until deep golden and it releases easily from the pan. Don't move it around, or it won't brown.
Flip and cook another 4–5 minutes, until the centre is white with no pink and the juices run clear (75°C if you have a thermometer).
Transfer to a board and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice across the grain.

stages.title: Warm the sides and assemble
steps: Microwave the rice pouches for about 2 minutes, until steaming hot, following the packet directions.
Meanwhile, put the same pan over medium heat and add the black beans and corn with a splash of water. Stir for 3 minutes, until the corn is thawed and everything is hot.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top with the beans and corn, lettuce, sliced chicken, salsa and avocado. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Slicing the breasts in half keeps them juicy because they cook through before they dry out.
Cook the rice from scratch ahead of time if you prefer; 1 cup of uncooked brown rice takes about 30 minutes, so start it first.
Make the spice mix in bulk and keep it in a jar for quick weeknight chicken.
Add the avocado last so it stays green and doesn't turn brown.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g lean beef strips or raw prawns, cooked for 2–3 minutes per side.
Make it vegetarian by using a second can of beans or a pan-fried sweet potato instead of the chicken.
Add 1 tsp chipotle in adobo or a pinch of chilli flakes to the spice rub for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keep the chicken, rice, beans and salsa in separate containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken, rice and beans in the microwave until steaming hot, and add the lettuce, salsa and avocado fresh.

recipe.title: Vietnamese lemongrass chicken
recipe.summary: Chicken thigh pieces marinated in lemongrass, garlic and fish sauce, seared until caramelised and served with rice, fresh herbs and quick pickled carrot.
ingredients: 800 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces
3 lemongrass stalks, white part finely chopped
method: Mix the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, 1 tbsp oil and pepper, then toss through the chicken. Pickle the carrot in the vinegar, caster sugar and 1/2 tsp salt.
Rinse the rice, then boil it in water with the remaining salt over high heat. Cover, cook on low for 12 minutes, then rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook half the chicken 7–8 minutes, turning once, until golden and no pink inside.
Cook the second batch in the remaining oil the same way, using any leftover marinade only if it bubbles for 2 minutes.
Serve the chicken over rice with carrot, cucumber, mint, coriander, chilli and lime wedges if using.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken and pickle the carrot
steps: In a large bowl, mix the lemongrass, garlic, fish sauce, brown sugar, soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the oil and the black pepper until the sugar mostly dissolves, about 1 minute.
Add the chicken and toss well so every piece is coated, then leave it to marinate while you do the carrot. Chop the lemongrass very finely, because big pieces turn tough and woody.
In a small bowl, stir the rice wine vinegar, caster sugar and 1/2 tsp of the salt until the sugar dissolves, about 1 minute. Add the carrot, toss, and leave it to soften and pickle until needed.
Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water for about 1 minute, until the water runs mostly clear.

stages.title: Cook the rice and chicken
steps: Put the rice in a medium saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Bring to the boil over high heat, about 3 minutes, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Turn off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes to steam.

While the rice cooks, heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until shimmering. Add half the chicken in a single layer and cook for 4 minutes without moving it, until deep golden and caramelised underneath.
Turn the pieces and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes, until golden all over and cooked through. Cut the biggest piece open to check there is no pink and the juices run clear. Move to a plate.

Wipe out any burnt bits, heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat, and cook the second batch the same way. Don't crowd the pan, or the chicken steams and turns pale instead of caramelising. Stir in any marinade left in the bowl only if you cook it for a full 2 minutes, until bubbling and sticky, then pour it over the chicken.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Fluff the rice with a fork and divide it among four bowls.
Top with the chicken, drained pickled carrot, cucumber slices, mint and coriander, and the chilli if you like heat.
Serve with lime wedges on the side if you like, squeezing the lime over just before eating.

tips: Marinate the chicken for up to 24 hours in the fridge for deeper flavour; cook it straight from the bowl after 10 minutes if you're short of time.
Use only the pale, tender lower part of the lemongrass and bash the stalk first to release more fragrance.
Cook in two batches so the chicken browns and caramelises instead of steaming.
Thighs stay juicy; if using breast, cut it a little larger and cook it just until no pink remains.
variations: Swap the chicken for pork shoulder slices or firm tofu cubes, cooking tofu until crisp and golden.
Serve in rice paper rolls or a vermicelli noodle bowl with lettuce and peanuts.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes to the marinade for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keep the chicken, rice and pickle in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat the chicken in a hot pan or microwave until steaming hot, and eat the herbs fresh.

recipe.title: Greek chicken tray bake
recipe.summary: Chicken breast, capsicum, zucchini and chickpeas roasted on trays with lemon and oregano, served with tzatziki for a high-protein, low-fuss dinner.
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts (about 600 g), cut into 3 cm pieces
1 large red capsicum (about 250 g), cut into 3 cm pieces
2 zucchini (about 400 g), cut into 2 cm half-moons
1 large red onion (about 200 g), cut into wedges
400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line two trays. Whisk the oil, lemon zest, 2 tbsp lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Toss the chicken in some of the marinade, and the capsicum, zucchini, onion and chickpeas in the rest. Spread in a single layer over both trays.
Roast for 25 minutes, stirring once at 12 minutes, until the chicken has no pink and the juices run clear and the vegetables are browned.
Rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, squeeze over the remaining lemon juice and serve with tzatziki and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep and marinate
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, lemon zest, 2 tbsp of the lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and black pepper.
Add the chicken pieces to the bowl and toss until every piece is coated, then lift them out onto one tray, leaving as much marinade behind as you can.
Add the capsicum, zucchini, red onion and chickpeas to the same bowl and toss in the remaining marinade.
Spread the vegetables and chickpeas over both trays around the chicken, keeping everything in a single layer with a little space between pieces, because crowded trays steam instead of roast.

stages.title: Roast
steps: Roast on the middle and upper racks for 25 minutes, swapping the trays and stirring everything once at the 12-minute mark.

Check that the chicken has no pink in the centre of the thickest piece and the juices run clear (75°C on a thermometer), and that the vegetable edges are browned and tender and the chickpeas look crisp at the edges.
If the chicken is still pink, return it to the oven for 3-5 minutes and check again.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Rest the trays on the bench for 5 minutes so the chicken juices settle.
Squeeze the remaining lemon juice over the trays and toss gently.
Divide among four plates and serve with the tzatziki and lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Cut the chicken into even 3 cm pieces so it all cooks at the same time and stays juicy.
Use two trays rather than one; overcrowding gives soggy vegetables instead of browned edges.
Marinate the chicken for up to 8 hours in the fridge for more flavour, adding the vegetables just before roasting.
Swap the tzatziki for hummus if you prefer, or use plain Greek yoghurt with a squeeze of lemon.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets instead of breast and roast 5 minutes longer, until cooked through.
Add 200 g cherry tomatoes and 60 g crumbled feta for the last 10 minutes of roasting.
Make it vegetarian by swapping the chicken for two 400 g cans of chickpeas and 250 g halloumi, cut into slices.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days, with the tzatziki stored separately. Reheat in a 180°C fan-forced oven for 10-12 minutes, or in the microwave until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Beef tacos
recipe.summary: Spiced beef mince piled into crunchy taco shells with lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream, ready in 20 minutes.
method: Cook the onion in the oil in a pan over medium heat for 3 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Turn the heat to high and cook the beef mince for 4 minutes, until no pink remains and it is browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the water and simmer on medium for 2 minutes until thick.
Warm the taco shells in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 2 minutes until crisp.
Fill with beef, lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Prep the toppings
steps: Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and grate the cheese, then put each in a small bowl.
Finely dice the onion and crush the garlic so they are ready to go, as the cooking moves quickly.
Spoon the sour cream into a bowl and cut the lime into wedges if using.

stages.title: Cook the beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to let it brown and turn bitter.
Turn the heat to high, add the beef mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 4 minutes, until no pink remains and the edges are browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until the spices smell fragrant. Season with salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Simmer the filling
steps: Pour in the water and simmer over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring, until the liquid thickens and clings to the mince. Don't let it dry out; add a splash more water if it looks dry.

stages.title: Warm the shells and serve
steps: Warm the taco shells on a tray in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 2 minutes, until crisp and hot to the touch.
Fill each shell with beef, then top with lettuce, tomato, cheese and sour cream. Serve straight away with lime wedges, if using, so the shells stay crunchy.

tips: Drain any excess fat from the pan after browning the mince if it looks greasy, so the filling isn't oily.
Use a hot pan and don't stir the mince constantly, so it browns instead of steaming.
Stand the shells upright in a loaf tin to keep them steady while you fill them.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken mince or pork mince, cooking until no pink remains.
Use soft flour tortillas warmed in a dry pan for 20 seconds each side instead of hard shells.
Add a drained can of black beans with the water for extra fibre and a more filling taco.
recipe.storage: Keep the cooked beef in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat in a pan over medium heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of water.

recipe.title: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry with brown rice
recipe.summary: A quick Chinese-style stir-fry of lean chicken breast and plenty of greens in a ginger, garlic and soy sauce, served on brown rice.
ingredients: 3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into small florets
method: Boil the brown rice over medium heat for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew. Meanwhile, slice the chicken and toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tsp cornflour, salt and pepper.
Whisk the remaining soy sauce, cornflour, honey, sesame oil and water. Prep the capsicum, carrots, broccoli, snow peas, ginger and garlic.
Heat half the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the chicken in two batches, 3 minutes each, until golden and white through.
Stir-fry the broccoli, carrots and capsicum over medium-high heat for 4 minutes. Add the snow peas, garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Return the chicken, add the sauce and toss 2 minutes, until glossy. Drain the rice, serve topped with the stir-fry, spring onions and sesame seeds.

stages.title: Start the rice and prep
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat, add the brown rice, then reduce to medium so it simmers steadily. Cook for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew; it will finish while you stir-fry.
Slice the chicken breasts across the grain into strips about 1 cm thick. Toss with 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, 2 tsp of the cornflour, a pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper.
In a small jug, whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, the honey, sesame oil, water and the remaining 1 tsp cornflour until smooth, so the cornflour doesn't clump later.

Slice the capsicum and carrots, cut the broccoli into small florets, trim the snow peas, and finely grate the ginger and chop the garlic. Keep everything within reach of the stove, because the stir-fry moves fast.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large wok or frying pan over high heat for 1 minute, until a drop of water sizzles at once. Add 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil and swirl to coat.
Cook half the chicken in a single layer for 3 minutes, turning once, until golden outside and white right through. Cut the thickest piece open to check there is no pink, then move it to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining vegetable oil and chicken. Cooking in two batches keeps the pan hot so the chicken browns rather than stews.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and sauce
steps: Return the empty pan to medium-high heat. Add the broccoli, carrots and capsicum and stir-fry for 4 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and the carrot is just tender but still crisp.
Add the snow peas, garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Take care not to let the garlic brown, as it turns bitter.
Return the chicken and any juices to the pan. Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss for 2 minutes, until it thickens to a glossy coating and the chicken is hot through.

stages.title: Drain the rice and serve
steps: Drain the rice in a colander and let it steam-dry for 2 minutes so it isn't wet or gluey.
Divide the rice among four bowls, top with the stir-fry, then scatter over the spring onions and the sesame seeds, if using. Serve straight away while the vegetables are crisp.

tips: Cook the chicken in two batches so the pan stays hot and the meat browns instead of steaming.
Slice the chicken across the grain and keep the strips thin so they stay tender and cook quickly.
Swap the vegetables for whatever is in the fridge: bok choy, zucchini, green beans or mushrooms all work.
For a faster dinner, use two 250 g pouches of microwave brown rice instead of boiling your own.
variations: Use 600 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed, instead of chicken for a vegetarian version, browning it well before adding the vegetables.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic and ginger for more heat.
Use 600 g raw peeled prawns instead of chicken, cooking them for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Steak sandwich
recipe.summary: A classic Aussie steak sandwich of thin-cut steak, sweet caramelised onion, beetroot and salad on toasted Turkish bread, ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 2 large brown onions (about 400 g), thinly sliced
1 loaf Turkish bread (about 450 g), cut into 4 pieces
method: Cook the onions in 1 tbsp oil in a pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the brown sugar and cook 2 minutes until deep golden and sticky.
Season the dried steaks with the salt and pepper. Cook in the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a pan over high heat for 1–2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Rest the steaks for 2 minutes so the juices settle.
Butter the cut sides of the Turkish bread and toast them in a pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes until golden.
Layer barbecue sauce, lettuce, tomato, beetroot, steak and onions on the bread, then top and serve.

stages.title: Caramelise the onions
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the sliced onions and cook, stirring often, for 5 minutes until soft and starting to colour.

Sprinkle in the brown sugar and cook for 2 more minutes, stirring, until the onions are deep golden and sticky, then tip them into a bowl and wipe out the pan. Don't walk away, as the sugar can catch and burn quickly.

stages.title: Cook the steak
steps: Pat the steaks dry with paper towel and season both sides with the salt and black pepper, because wet steak will steam instead of browning.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in the same pan over high heat until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.

Cook the steaks in two batches for 1–2 minutes per side, until deeply browned and just cooked through with no pink raw patches in the centre, then move them to a plate and rest for 2 minutes so the juices settle. Don't crowd the pan or overcook, as thin steak turns tough fast.

stages.title: Toast and assemble
steps: Split the Turkish bread pieces in half horizontally and spread the cut sides with the softened butter.
Toast the bread buttered-side down in a clean frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until golden and crisp, working in batches if needed.
Spread barbecue sauce over the bottom halves, then layer on the lettuce, tomato, beetroot, steak and caramelised onions, and press the tops on. Serve straight away while the bread is warm and crisp.

tips: Use minute steaks or slice a rump or sirloin steak thinly and bash it flat so it cooks in a couple of minutes and stays tender.
Make the caramelised onions up to 3 days ahead and reheat them in the pan or microwave.
Dry the lettuce well so the bread doesn't go soggy.
variations: Add 4 slices of cheddar on the hot steaks and a fried egg per sandwich for a loaded version.
Swap the steak for 600 g chicken thigh fillets, flattened and cooked 3–4 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Use chilli jam or tomato relish instead of barbecue sauce.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the bread goes soggy. Keep leftover cooked steak and onions separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat gently in a hot pan.

recipe.title: Homemade beef burgers
recipe.summary: Juicy beef patties with melted cheese, beetroot, pickles, lettuce and tomato on toasted buns, a classic Aussie burger that's ready in 30 minutes.
method: Mix the mince, onion, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper, then shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick.
Mix the tomato sauce and mayonnaise, drain the beetroot and pickles, and slice the tomato. Butter the cut sides of the buns.
Cook the patties in the oil in a pan over medium-high heat for 4 minutes per side, until browned and no pink remains.
Top with cheddar, cover for 1 minute until melted, then rest 2 minutes.
Toast the buns over medium heat for 1 minute until golden, then stack with sauce, lettuce, tomato, patties, beetroot and pickles.

stages.title: Make the patties
steps: Combine the beef mince, grated onion, egg, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, salt and black pepper in a large bowl and mix with your hands for about 1 minute, just until it holds together.
Divide the mixture into 4 equal portions and shape each into a patty about 11 cm wide and 2 cm thick, pressing a shallow dip into the centre of each so they stay flat as they cook.
Avoid overworking the mince, as it makes the patties tough and dense.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Wash and dry the lettuce leaves, slice the tomato, and drain the beetroot slices and pickle slices on paper towel so the buns don't go soggy.
Mix the tomato sauce and mayonnaise together in a small bowl, then spread the softened butter over the cut sides of the buns.

stages.title: Cook the patties
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until the oil shimmers.
Cook the patties for 4 minutes without moving them, until a dark brown crust forms and they release easily from the pan, then flip and cook another 4 minutes.

Lay a cheddar slice on each patty, cover the pan with a lid or tray and cook 1 minute, until the cheese is melted and the patties are cooked through with no pink in the centre and juices running clear.
Move the patties to a plate and rest them for 2 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Toast the buns and assemble
steps: Wipe the pan, then toast the buns buttered side down over medium heat for 1 minute, until golden.
Spread the sauce mixture on the bun bases, then layer on the lettuce, tomato, patty with cheese, beetroot and pickles, and finish with the bun tops. Serve straight away.

tips: Grating the onion keeps the patties moist and avoids chunks that make them fall apart.
Chill the shaped patties for 15 minutes if you have time, as they hold their shape better in the pan.
Don't press down on the patties while they cook or you'll squeeze out the juices.
Add a fried egg or a slice of bacon for the full Aussie burger with the lot.
variations: Use chicken or turkey mince and cook 5 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Swap the beef patties for a store-bought plant-based patty and cook to the packet directions.
Add sliced pineapple rings, grilled for 2 minutes each side, for a burger with the lot.
recipe.storage: Cooked patties keep in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days or frozen for 2 months; reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes per side until hot through. Assemble the burgers fresh so the buns stay crisp.

recipe.title: Beef nachos
recipe.summary: Corn chips baked under chilli beef mince, kidney beans and melted cheese, then topped with guacamole and sour cream for an easy family dinner.
ingredients: 400 g can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
method: Cook the onion in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 3–4 minutes until soft, add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the mince on high for 5–6 minutes until browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning and cumin until fragrant, then add the tomatoes, beans, salt and pepper and simmer on medium-low for 5 minutes until thick.
Layer the corn chips, beef and cheese on a lined tray and bake at 200°C fan-forced for 6–8 minutes until the cheese bubbles.
Mash the avocado with the lime juice, then dollop it over the nachos with the sour cream.
Top with the coriander and the pickled jalapeños if using, and serve straight away.

stages.title: Cook the chilli beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then cook the onion for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the beef mince and turn the heat to high.
Break the mince up with a wooden spoon and cook for 5–6 minutes until browned all over with no pink left; don't crowd it or it will stew rather than brown.
Stir in the taco seasoning and cumin for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the crushed tomatoes, salt and black pepper.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the kidney beans and simmer for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and no longer watery.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: While the beef simmers, preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Spread half the corn chips over the tray, spoon over half the beef mixture and sprinkle with a third of the cheese, then repeat with the remaining chips and beef.
Top with the remaining cheese and bake for 6–8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges; watch the edges of the chips so they don't burn.

stages.title: Make the guacamole and serve
steps: Mash the avocado with the lime juice in a bowl until mostly smooth with a few small chunks, then season with a pinch of extra salt if needed.
Take the nachos out of the oven and dollop over the guacamole and sour cream.
Scatter with the coriander and the pickled jalapeños if using, and serve straight away while the chips are still crisp.

tips: Drain any excess fat from the mince after browning so the chips don't turn soggy.
Layer the chips, beef and cheese twice so more chips get a topping, not just the top ones.
Make the beef mixture up to 2 days ahead and reheat it before assembling.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken mince or a second can of beans and a diced capsicum for a vegetarian version.
Add a diced fresh chilli or a spoonful of chipotle paste to the beef for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh as the chips go soggy. Keep leftover beef mixture in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a pan or microwave until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Mongolian beef
recipe.summary: Thin strips of beef stir-fried with spring onions in a sticky sweet soy and garlic sauce, served over steamed rice in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g beef rump steak, thinly sliced against the grain
½ cup (125 ml) water, for the sauce
6 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
2¼ cups (560 ml) cold water, for the rice
method: Slice the beef thinly, toss with cornflour, salt and pepper, and stir the soy sauce, brown sugar, water and oyster sauce together.
Cook the rice with its water: boil on high, then cover and cook on low for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed.
Sear the beef in 2 tbsp oil in batches over high heat, 1–2 minutes each, until browned with no pink left.
On medium heat, fry the garlic and ginger in 1 tbsp oil for 30 seconds, then simmer the sauce 2–3 minutes until glossy and thick.
Return the beef, add the spring onions and toss 1 minute until coated. Serve over rice with sesame seeds if you like.

stages.title: Prep the beef and sauce
steps: Slice the beef across the grain into strips about 5 mm thick, which keeps it tender; slicing is easier if the steak is chilled for 10 minutes first.
Toss the beef in a bowl with the cornflour, salt and black pepper until every strip has a light, even coating.
