In a jug, stir together the soy sauce, brown sugar, the ½ cup of water and the oyster sauce until the sugar mostly dissolves.
Cut the spring onions, chop the garlic and grate the ginger, then keep them close to the stove because the cooking moves quickly.

stages.title: Start the rice
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then tip it into a medium saucepan with the 2¼ cups of cold water.

Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 12 minutes without lifting the lid, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender; leave it covered off the heat while you cook the beef.

stages.title: Sear the beef
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for about 1 minute, until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.
Add half the beef in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes, until deeply browned underneath, then toss for 30 seconds until no pink remains; transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining beef, adding a little more oil if the pan looks dry. Do not crowd the pan, or the beef will steam and turn grey instead of browning.

stages.title: Make the sauce and finish
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp of oil, then the garlic and ginger, stirring for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the sauce and simmer for 2–3 minutes, until it turns glossy and thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the beef and any juices to the pan, add the spring onions and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce clings to the beef and the spring onions are just wilted and still bright green.
Fluff the rice with a fork, divide it among bowls, spoon the beef over the top and scatter with sesame seeds if using.

tips: Slice the beef across the grain and partly freeze it for 15 minutes beforehand to get thin, even strips.
Cook the beef in two batches so it browns rather than stews; a hot pan is the key to the caramelised edges.
If the sauce gets too thick, loosen it with a splash of water; if it's too thin, simmer it for another minute before adding the beef.
Flank, skirt or sirloin steak all work in place of rump.
variations: Swap the beef for chicken thigh fillets cut into thin strips, cooking for 4–5 minutes until golden and white all the way through.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or a sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
Serve with steamed broccoli or bok choy alongside the rice for extra greens.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes, until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Chilli con carne
recipe.summary: Beef mince and kidney beans simmered in a smoky cumin and chilli tomato sauce, served over rice with sour cream.
ingredients: 400 g can kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1/2 cup (120 g) sour cream, to serve
method: Cook the onion in the olive oil over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and capsicum for 3–4 minutes until fragrant.
Turn the heat to high and brown the beef mince for 5–6 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Stir in the cumin, paprika, chilli flakes, oregano and tomato paste for 1 minute until toasty, then add the tomatoes, beef stock, salt and pepper.
Simmer on low for 20 minutes until thick, then add the kidney beans for 5 minutes until heated through.
Boil the rice for 12 minutes until tender, then drain.
Serve the chilli over the rice with sour cream and coriander, if using.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan or pot over medium heat, then cook the diced onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and diced capsicum and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the capsicum starts to soften and the garlic smells fragrant.

Turn the heat to high, add the beef mince and break it up with a wooden spoon. Cook for 5–6 minutes, until no pink remains and the mince is browned in places; avoid stirring constantly so it can brown rather than steam.

stages.title: Simmer the chilli
steps: Stir in the cumin, smoked paprika, chilli flakes, oregano and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens slightly and the spices smell toasty.
Pour in the diced tomatoes and beef stock, add the salt and black pepper, and scrape up any browned bits from the base of the pan.
Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thick and no longer watery.
Add the kidney beans and simmer for 5 minutes more, until the beans are heated through. Taste and add more salt if needed.

stages.title: Cook the rice and serve
steps: While the chilli simmers, cook the rice in a saucepan of boiling water over medium heat for 12 minutes, until tender with no hard centre, then drain well and keep covered.
Spoon the rice into bowls, top with the chilli, add a dollop of sour cream and scatter with coriander leaves if using.

tips: Brown the mince over high heat without stirring too much; the browned bits add a lot of flavour.
Taste at the end and adjust salt and chilli, as canned tomatoes and stock vary in saltiness.
Make it a day ahead: the flavours deepen overnight and it reheats well.
Add a square of dark chocolate or a pinch of sugar if the sauce tastes sharp from the tomatoes.
variations: Swap the beef mince for turkey or chicken mince, and add an extra 1 tbsp olive oil as these are leaner.
Make it vegetarian by using two 400 g cans of mixed beans and a diced zucchini instead of the mince, with vegetable stock.
Add 1–2 chopped fresh red chillies or a tsp of chipotle paste for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium-low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Cottage pie
recipe.summary: Beef mince and vegetables in a rich gravy under a golden, cheesy mashed potato top, a hearty family favourite.
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
method: Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat then simmer on medium for 15 minutes until tender. Drain, then mash with the butter, milk, half the cheese, salt and pepper.
Fry the onion, carrots and celery in the olive oil over medium heat for 6–7 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Brown the mince over high heat for 6–8 minutes until no pink remains. Stir in the tomato paste, flour and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the stock and Worcestershire sauce and simmer 8–10 minutes until thick, then stir in the peas, salt and pepper.
Spoon the filling into a dish, top with the mash and remaining cheese. Bake at 200°C (180°C fan-forced) for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling, then rest 5 minutes.

stages.title: Make the mash
steps: Put the potatoes in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, add a good pinch of salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium and simmer for 15 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.
Drain well and return the potatoes to the hot pot for 1 minute so the steam escapes, which stops the mash going watery.
Add the butter, milk, 1/2 cup of the cheese, a pinch of salt and some black pepper, then mash for 2 minutes until smooth and creamy. Cover and set aside.

stages.title: Cook the filling
steps: While the potatoes simmer, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery for 6–7 minutes, stirring, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Increase to high heat, add the beef mince and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking up lumps with a wooden spoon, until no pink remains and it is lightly browned. Avoid overcrowding the pan or the mince will steam rather than brown.
Stir in the tomato paste, flour and thyme and cook for 1 minute, until the flour disappears into the mince.
Pour in the stock and Worcestershire sauce, stir well and bring to a simmer. Reduce to medium-low and cook for 8–10 minutes, until the gravy thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Stir through the peas, season with salt and black pepper, and cook 1 minute until the peas are hot.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) while the filling simmers.
Spoon the filling into a 2.5 litre ovenproof baking dish and spread it level.
Dollop the mash over the top, spread to the edges to seal in the gravy, then rough up the surface with a fork so it browns well.
Sprinkle over the remaining 1/2 cup of cheese and bake for 20 minutes, until the top is golden and the gravy bubbles at the edges.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving so the filling firms up and is easier to scoop.

tips: Rough up the mash with a fork before baking; the ridges crisp and brown beautifully.
Let the filling thicken properly, as a loose gravy will leak up through the mash.
Assemble up to a day ahead and refrigerate, then bake for about 30 minutes until hot through.
Swap the Worcestershire sauce for 1 tbsp of soy sauce if you run out.
variations: Make it a shepherd's pie by using lamb mince instead of beef.
Add 1 cup of finely diced mushrooms with the onion for extra depth.
Top with a mix of half potato and half sweet potato mash for a sweeter finish.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days in an airtight container or freezes for up to 3 months. Reheat covered in a 180°C oven for 20–25 minutes, or microwave single portions until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Rissoles with gravy
recipe.summary: Pan-fried beef and onion rissoles served with onion gravy, creamy mash and peas, a classic Aussie family dinner.
ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (about 800 g), peeled, cut into chunks
method: Boil the potatoes in salted water over medium heat for 12–15 minutes until tender. Mix the mince, grated onion, breadcrumbs, egg, tomato sauce, 1 tbsp Worcestershire, half the salt and pepper, and shape into 8 patties.
Fry the rissoles in the oil over medium-high heat, 5 minutes a side, until browned and no pink remains in the centre. Rest them on a plate.
Drain and mash the potatoes with the butter, milk and remaining salt until smooth.
In the same pan over medium heat, cook the sliced onion for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Stir in the stock, remaining Worcestershire and pepper, and simmer 4–5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Cook the peas for 3 minutes until bright green, then serve everything together.

stages.title: Shape the rissoles
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even chunks about 4 cm wide, then set aside in a pot of cold water. Peel the onions, finely grate one onion and thinly slice the other.

In a large bowl, combine the beef mince, grated onion, breadcrumbs, egg, tomato sauce, 1 tbsp of the Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp of the salt and half the black pepper. Mix with your hands for about 1 minute until it holds together, but don't overwork it or the rissoles will turn tough.
Divide the mixture into 8 portions and shape each into a flat patty about 2 cm thick, pressing the edges smooth so they don't crack while frying.

stages.title: Cook the rissoles and mash
steps: Add a pinch of salt to the pot of potatoes, bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and cook for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides into the chunks with no resistance.
While the potatoes cook, heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute until it shimmers. Cook the rissoles in two batches if needed so the pan isn't crowded.

Fry the rissoles for 5 minutes on the first side until deep brown, then flip and cook another 4–5 minutes until firm, browned all over and no pink remains in the centre when you cut one open. Move them to a plate and cover loosely with foil, leaving the browned bits in the pan for the gravy.
Drain the potatoes well and return them to the hot pot. Add the butter, milk and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and mash for about 1 minute until smooth and fluffy, then cover to keep warm.

stages.title: Make the gravy and peas
steps: Reduce the frying pan to medium heat and add the sliced onion. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, until soft and golden.
Sprinkle over the plain flour and stir for 1 minute until it coats the onion and smells toasty. Gradually pour in the beef stock, stirring constantly, to avoid lumps.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce and the remaining black pepper. Simmer for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until the gravy is glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Meanwhile, put the frozen peas in a small saucepan with 1/2 cup of water over medium heat and cook for 3 minutes until bright green and hot, then drain.
Serve the rissoles on the mash with the peas alongside, and spoon the gravy over the top.

tips: Grate the onion rather than chopping it so it melts into the mince and keeps the rissoles moist.
Chill the shaped patties for 15 minutes if you have time, as they hold together better in the pan.
Don't press the rissoles down while frying, as that squeezes out the juices.
Stir the flour into the onions for a full minute so the gravy doesn't taste floury.
variations: Use half beef and half pork mince for a softer, richer rissole.
Add 1 grated carrot or zucchini to the mixture for extra vegetables.
Stir a teaspoon of Dijon mustard into the gravy for a sharper flavour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days in airtight containers, or freeze the cooked rissoles and gravy for up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a covered pan or microwave until steaming hot all the way through.

recipe.title: Picadillo
recipe.summary: A Cuban beef mince stewed with tomato, green olives, raisins and cumin, served over rice with black beans for a sweet, salty and savoury weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander, to serve (optional)
method: Cook the rice with water and half the salt, covered on low for 12 minutes until tender, then rest 5 minutes. Warm the black beans over medium-low for 3–4 minutes until hot.
Soften the onion and capsicum in olive oil over medium heat for 5–6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beef mince over medium-high heat and cook 6–8 minutes until browned with no pink left. Season with the remaining salt and the pepper.
Stir in the tomatoes, paste, bay leaves, olives, raisins and vinegar. Simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes until thick and saucy.
Remove the bay leaves and serve over the rice with the beans, topped with coriander if using.

stages.title: Cook the rice and beans
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then add it to a medium saucepan with 3 cups of water and 1/2 tsp of the salt.

Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender. Rest it, covered and off the heat, for 5 minutes and do not lift the lid while it cooks.
Warm the black beans in a small saucepan over medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes, until hot and steaming, stirring so they don't catch on the base.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Add the onion and capsicum and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and the onion is translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and oregano and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, so the garlic doesn't burn and turn bitter.

stages.title: Brown the beef
steps: Turn the heat to medium-high and add the beef mince. Break it up with a wooden spoon and cook for 6–8 minutes, until no pink remains and the meat is browned in places.
Season with the remaining salt and the black pepper. If a lot of liquid pools in the pan, let it bubble away so the meat browns rather than steams.

stages.title: Simmer the picadillo
steps: Stir in the diced tomatoes, tomato paste, bay leaves, olives, raisins and vinegar, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pan.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce is thick and clings to the meat rather than pooling. Remove the bay leaves, taste and add more salt if needed.
Serve the picadillo over the rice with the black beans alongside, scattering over the coriander if using.

tips: Let the mince brown properly before adding the tomatoes; the browned bits give the dish its deep savoury flavour.
Taste before serving and balance with a splash more vinegar if it's too sweet or a few more raisins if it's too salty.
Use a deep frying pan so the mince has room to brown instead of steaming.
The flavour improves overnight, so it's a good make-ahead dish.
variations: Swap the beef for pork mince or a mix of beef and pork.
Add 1 diced potato with the tomatoes and simmer until tender for a more traditional, heartier version.
Top each serve with a fried egg for a classic Cuban 'a caballo' style.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 4 days or frozen for 3 months. Reheat in a pan over medium-low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Thai beef salad
recipe.summary: Seared lean steak sliced over a crunchy herb, cucumber and tomato salad with a sharp lime, fish sauce and chilli dressing.
ingredients: 600 g lean beef rump or sirloin steak
method: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chilli and garlic in a large bowl until the sugar dissolves, then prep the cucumber, tomato, onion, herbs and salad leaves.
Rub the dry steak with oil, salt and pepper, then sear in a very hot pan over high heat for 3–4 minutes a side, until browned and springy.
Rest the steak for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice thinly against the grain.
Toss the cucumber, tomato and onion in the dressing for 30 seconds, then gently add the herbs and salad leaves.
Top with the sliced beef and peanuts and serve straight away.

stages.title: Make the dressing and salad
steps: In a large bowl, stir the lime juice, fish sauce, brown sugar, chilli and garlic for 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves completely.
Add the cucumbers, cherry tomatoes and red onion to a separate large bowl, but do not toss them with the dressing yet, as the salt in it will make the vegetables watery.
Pick the mint and coriander leaves and keep them with the salad leaves in a third bowl or on a platter, ready to assemble.

stages.title: Sear the steak
steps: Take the steak out of the fridge, pat it very dry with paper towel, then rub it with the rice bran oil and season both sides with the salt and black pepper.
Heat a heavy frying pan or chargrill pan over high heat for 2 minutes, until it is very hot and the oil just starts to shimmer.

Cook the steak for 3–4 minutes on each side for medium-rare, until deeply browned and the centre feels springy, or until a thermometer reads 55°C in the thickest part; cook 1–2 minutes longer per side for medium. Avoid moving it around in the pan so it forms a good crust.
Transfer the steak to a board and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it thinly against the grain.

stages.title: Assemble and serve
steps: Add the cucumber, tomato and onion to the dressing and toss gently for 30 seconds, until everything is coated.
Add the mint, coriander and salad leaves and toss lightly so the herbs stay bright and do not wilt.
Pile the salad onto a platter, top with the sliced beef and any resting juices, and scatter over the chopped peanuts. Serve straight away while the beef is still slightly warm.

tips: Pat the steak very dry before searing; a dry surface browns well, while a wet one steams and turns grey.
Dress the salad just before serving so the cucumber and leaves stay crisp.
Taste the dressing before using it and add a little more sugar or lime to balance the salty, sour and sweet flavours.
Remove the chilli seeds for a milder dressing.
variations: Swap the beef for 600 g chicken breast fillets, cooked through until no pink remains and the juices run clear.
Add 100 g cooked rice vermicelli noodles for a more filling meal.
Use firm tofu, pan-fried until golden, and replace the fish sauce with soy sauce for a vegetarian version.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the dressed salad turns watery. Keep the sliced beef and undressed salad separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and dress just before serving.

recipe.title: Beef and Guinness stew
recipe.summary: Chuck steak slow-braised with Guinness, onions, carrots and thyme until the beef is tender and the gravy is rich and glossy.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into 4 cm pieces
4 carrots (about 500 g), cut into 3 cm chunks
method: Toss the beef in the flour, salt and pepper, then brown it in the olive oil in batches over medium-high heat, 4–5 minutes per batch, until deep golden.
Cook the onions over medium heat for 6–8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1–2 minutes until darkened.
Add the Guinness, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 3–4 minutes until reduced by a third.
Return the beef to the pot with the stock, carrots, celery, thyme, bay leaves, Worcestershire sauce and sugar, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and braise in a 160°C fan-forced oven for 1 hour 45 minutes, until the beef is fork-tender.
Rest for 10 minutes, remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves, and top with parsley if using.

stages.title: Brown the beef
steps: Pat the beef dry with paper towel, then toss it in a bowl with the flour, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering.

Brown a third of the beef for 4–5 minutes, turning occasionally, until deep golden on all sides, then transfer to a plate. Don't crowd the pot, or the beef will steam and turn grey instead of browning.
Add another 1 tbsp of oil and brown the second third for 4–5 minutes until deep golden, then move it to the plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp of olive oil and brown the rest of the beef for 4–5 minutes, until deep golden on all sides, then add it to the plate.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the onions to the same pot. Cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook for 1–2 minutes, until the paste darkens and smells sweet.
Pour in the Guinness and scrape the browned bits from the base of the pot with a wooden spoon. Simmer for 3–4 minutes, until reduced by about a third.

stages.title: Braise the stew
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C fan-forced.
Return the beef and any juices to the pot, then add the stock, carrots, celery, thyme, bay leaves, Worcestershire sauce and brown sugar. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Cover with a lid and transfer to the oven. Cook for 1 hour 45 minutes, stirring once halfway, until the beef is fork-tender and falls apart when pressed.

Remove the pot from the oven and rest it, uncovered, for 10 minutes so the gravy thickens slightly. Discard the thyme stalks and bay leaves, taste and adjust the salt, then scatter with parsley if using.

tips: Brown the beef in batches; crowding the pot makes it steam and costs you flavour.
If the gravy is thin after braising, simmer it uncovered on the stovetop over medium heat for 5–10 minutes until it coats a spoon.
The stew tastes better the next day, so make it ahead and reheat gently.
Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread to mop up the gravy.
variations: Add 300 g peeled potato chunks with the carrots for a one-pot meal.
Swap the chuck steak for lamb shoulder, cut into chunks, for an Irish-style lamb stew.
Top with a sheet of puff pastry and bake at 200°C fan-forced for 20 minutes for a stout pie.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat gently in a pot over medium-low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of stock if it's thick.

recipe.title: Lean beef burrito bowls
recipe.summary: Taco-spiced lean beef mince served over brown rice with black beans, corn, salsa and crisp lettuce for a high-protein, vegetable-packed weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 x 300 g can corn kernels, drained
method: Prep the lettuce, tomatoes, avocado and lime, and drain the black beans and corn.
Cook the onion in olive oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Turn the heat to medium-high and cook the beef mince for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains, then stir in the taco seasoning, tomato paste, salt and pepper for 1 minute.
Add the water and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until thick and glossy, then stir in the beans and corn for 3 to 4 minutes until hot.
Microwave the rice until steaming hot, then divide among bowls and top with the beef, lettuce, tomato, avocado, salsa, yoghurt, coriander and lime wedges.

stages.title: Prep the toppings
steps: Shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes, slice the avocado and cut the lime into wedges, then keep each in a separate pile or bowl.
Drain and rinse the black beans and drain the corn, then set both aside along with the salsa, Greek yoghurt and coriander leaves, if using.

stages.title: Cook the beef
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then cook the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to let it brown or it will turn bitter.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the beef mince and break it up with a wooden spoon, then cook for 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains and the edges are lightly browned.
Stir in the taco seasoning, tomato paste, salt and black pepper for 1 minute until the spices smell fragrant and the paste coats the meat.
Pour in the water, reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the liquid reduces to a thick, glossy sauce that coats the meat.

stages.title: Warm the rice, beans and corn
steps: Microwave the brown rice following the packet directions, usually about 2 minutes, until steaming hot, then fluff with a fork.
Stir the black beans and corn into the beef mixture and cook over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until both are heated through and the mixture is steaming.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.

tips: Choose beef mince labelled 5-star or under 10% fat so the bowls stay lean without needing to drain off oil.
Check the taco seasoning for salt, as some brands are very salty; add the extra pinch of salt at the end only if needed.
Cook the beef mixture up to 3 days ahead and reheat it, then add the fresh toppings just before serving so they stay crisp.
Swap the yoghurt for sour cream if you prefer, though it adds more fat.
variations: Use chicken or turkey mince instead of beef, cooking until no pink remains.
Make it vegetarian by replacing the beef with an extra can of beans and 1 cup of diced capsicum.
Add 1 tsp chipotle paste or sliced jalapeños with the taco seasoning for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keep the beef mixture and rice in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days, and reheat until steaming hot. Store the fresh toppings separately and add them just before serving.

recipe.title: Lamb cutlets with minted peas
recipe.summary: Pan-fried lamb cutlets served over crushed minted peas with lemon, a quick weeknight main that is on the table in 20 minutes.
method: Pat the cutlets dry, rub with half the oil, and season with the salt and black pepper.
Cook the cutlets in a very hot pan over high heat in the remaining oil, 2–3 minutes a side, until golden and pink in the centre.
Rest the lamb for 5 minutes so the juices settle.
Melt the butter over medium heat, cook the garlic for 30 seconds, then add the peas and water and cook covered for 3–4 minutes, until bright green.
Crush the peas, stir in the mint, lemon zest and juice, and serve under the cutlets with lemon wedges if using.

stages.title: Prepare the lamb
steps: Take the lamb cutlets out of the fridge and pat them dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Rub the cutlets with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, then season both sides with the salt and black pepper.
Zest the lemon, then juice it, and chop the mint leaves and finely chop the garlic so everything is ready before you start cooking.

stages.title: Cook the lamb
steps: Heat a large frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes until very hot, then add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Add the cutlets in a single layer, working in two batches if the pan is crowded, and cook for 2–3 minutes without moving them, until deeply golden underneath.
Turn the cutlets and cook for another 2 minutes for medium-rare, or 3 minutes for medium, until the meat feels springy when pressed and is pink in the centre.
Transfer the lamb to a plate and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle; do not skip this or the juices will run out when you cut.

stages.title: Make the minted peas
steps: While the lamb rests, melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the frozen peas and the water, cover, and cook for 3–4 minutes, until the peas are bright green and tender.
Take the pan off the heat and roughly crush the peas with a potato masher or fork, leaving some whole for texture.
Stir through the chopped mint, lemon zest and 1 tablespoon of lemon juice, then taste and add more lemon juice if you like.
Spoon the peas onto plates, top with the lamb cutlets and serve with lemon wedges if using.

tips: Dry cutlets and a really hot pan give you a proper crust; crowding the pan makes them grey and steamy.
Ask the butcher for French-trimmed cutlets if you want them neat, or leave the fat on for extra flavour and crisp it up on its edge for 1 minute.
Use the leftover pan juices: spoon a little over the peas for extra flavour.
Crush the peas just before serving, as they lose their bright colour if left to sit.
variations: Swap the lamb for 4 chicken thigh fillets, cooked for 5–6 minutes a side until no pink remains.
Add 100 g crumbled feta to the peas for a salty, creamy finish.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the garlic for a little heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in separate airtight containers; reheat the lamb gently in a pan for 1–2 minutes and the peas in the microwave until hot. Not suitable for freezing as the lamb turns dry.

recipe.title: Steak with salsa verde and sweet potato
recipe.summary: Seared rump steak with roasted sweet potato wedges, green beans and a fresh herb salsa verde, a lean and filling weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 2 large sweet potatoes (about 900 g), cut into wedges
2 tbsp olive oil, for the wedges
600 g lean rump steak (2 steaks, about 3 cm thick)
1 tbsp olive oil, for the steak
1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, firmly packed
method: Roast the sweet potato wedges tossed in olive oil, salt and pepper at 220°C fan-forced for 25 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender.
Finely chop the parsley, basil, capers and garlic, then stir in the mustard, vinegar, extra virgin olive oil and salt.
Boil the green beans in salted water over high heat for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Rub the steaks with oil, salt and pepper and sear in a very hot pan over high heat for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, until browned and springy.
Rest the steaks for 5 minutes so the juices settle, slice, and serve with the wedges, beans, salsa verde and lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Roast the sweet potato
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line a large tray with baking paper.
Toss the sweet potato wedges with 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper, then spread them in a single layer with space between them so they roast rather than steam.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges are golden and a knife slides in easily.

stages.title: Make the salsa verde
steps: While the wedges roast, finely chop the parsley, basil, capers and garlic together until very fine.
Scrape into a bowl and stir in the Dijon mustard, red wine vinegar, 80 ml extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Taste and add a little more vinegar if it needs sharpness. Avoid using a food processor, which turns it to a dull paste.

stages.title: Cook the steak and beans
steps: Take the steaks out of the fridge, pat them dry with paper towel and rub with 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and plenty of black pepper.
Bring a small pot of salted water to the boil over high heat, add the green beans and cook for 3 minutes until bright green and just tender, then drain.
Heat a large frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes until very hot and just smoking, then add the steaks.
Cook for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare, until deeply browned and the steak feels springy when pressed; add 1 minute per side for medium.
Rest the steaks on a board for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice against the grain.
Serve the sliced steak with the wedges and beans, spoon over the salsa verde and add lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the steak very dry so it browns instead of steaming in the pan.
Slice the steak against the grain to keep each slice tender.
Make the salsa verde up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge, stirring in a splash of oil before serving.
Use a thermometer if you have one: 52–55°C in the centre is medium-rare.
variations: Swap the rump for chicken thigh fillets and cook 5–6 minutes per side until no longer pink inside.
Add 1 finely chopped red chilli to the salsa verde for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days, with the salsa verde stored separately. Reheat the wedges in a 200°C oven for 10 minutes and eat the steak cold or warm it gently in a pan.

recipe.title: Beef and black bean stir-fry
recipe.summary: Tender strips of rump steak, capsicum and onion tossed in a salty, savoury black bean sauce and served over steamed rice.
ingredients: 1 large red onion (about 200 g), cut into wedges
method: Cook the rice in water on low heat, covered, for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest 5 minutes.
Toss the sliced rump steak with the cornflour, 1 tbsp soy sauce, rice wine, salt and pepper. Mix the black bean sauce, remaining soy, sugar and water.
Sear the beef in 1 tbsp oil in a hot pan over high heat in two batches, 2–3 minutes each, until browned but still pink inside.
Stir-fry the onion and capsicum in the remaining oil for 3–4 minutes until charred at the edges, then add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the sauce and bubble 1–2 minutes until thickened, return the beef for 1 minute, then top with spring onions and serve over the rice.

stages.title: Prepare the beef, sauce and rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it in a saucepan with 3 cups of water, covered, on low heat for 12 minutes after it first boils, until the water is absorbed. Rest it, covered, for 5 minutes.
Toss the sliced rump steak in a bowl with the cornflour, 1 tbsp of the soy sauce, the Shaoxing rice wine, a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper, so every strip is lightly coated.
Stir the black bean sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp soy sauce, the sugar and the water together in a small jug, then set it aside with the garlic, ginger and spring onions.

stages.title: Sear the beef
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers and just starts to smoke.

Add half the beef in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes without moving it, until browned underneath, then toss for 30 seconds until just browned all over but still pink inside. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining beef, adding more oil only if the pan looks dry. Do not crowd the pan or the beef will stew and turn grey.

stages.title: Stir-fry the vegetables and finish
steps: Return the pan to high heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, then the onion wedges and capsicum. Stir-fry for 3–4 minutes, until the edges are lightly charred and the capsicum is tender but still crisp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.

Pour in the sauce and bubble for 1–2 minutes, until it thickens slightly and coats the vegetables. Return the beef and its juices to the pan and toss for 1 minute, until the beef is hot and cooked to medium. Scatter over the spring onions and serve over the rice.

tips: Slice the beef across the grain as thinly as you can; freezing it for 15 minutes first makes this much easier.
Get the pan very hot before the beef goes in, and cook it in batches so it sears rather than steams.
Black bean sauce is salty, so taste before adding extra soy sauce.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets instead of beef and cook for 4–5 minutes until no pink remains.
Add 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
Swap the beef for firm tofu, pan-fried until golden, for a vegetarian version.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot pan or the microwave until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Lamb rogan josh
recipe.summary: A Kashmiri-style lamb curry simmered until tender in a yoghurt, paprika and warm spice sauce, good with rice and naan.
ingredients: 1 kg boneless lamb shoulder, cut into 3 cm pieces
method: Mix the lamb with the yoghurt, salt and black pepper, and set aside while you slice the onions and crush the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat, then fry the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Cook the onions for 10–12 minutes until deep golden, then stir in the garlic, ginger, paprika, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric, chilli and tomato paste for 1–2 minutes.
Add the lamb and yoghurt over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, pour in the water, then simmer on low, partly covered, for 40–45 minutes until very tender.
Stir through the garam masala, then serve with coriander leaves and steamed basmati rice.

stages.title: Marinate the lamb
steps: Place the lamb in a large bowl with the yoghurt, salt and black pepper, then stir well until every piece is coated.
Set aside at room temperature while you prepare the onions, garlic and ginger, and slice, crush and grate them as listed.
Mix the paprika, ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder in a small bowl so they are ready to add all at once.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and bay leaves and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the onions and cook, stirring often, for 10–12 minutes until deep golden brown; lower the heat if they darken too fast, as burnt onion makes the curry bitter.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until you can smell them, then add the spice mix and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute until the paste darkens slightly.

stages.title: Simmer the curry
steps: Add the lamb and all the yoghurt marinade, turn the heat to medium-high and stir for 5 minutes until the yoghurt looks thick and the lamb is no longer pink on the outside.
Pour in the water, scrape up any bits stuck to the base, and bring to a gentle bubble.

Reduce the heat to low, cover with the lid slightly ajar and simmer for 40–45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until the lamb is very tender and breaks easily with a spoon and the oil rises to the surface of the sauce.
Stir in the garam masala, cook for 1 minute, then taste and add more salt if needed. Scatter with coriander leaves and serve with steamed basmati rice.

tips: Use lamb shoulder rather than leg, as the extra fat and connective tissue turn silky during the long simmer.
Take the yoghurt out of the fridge for 15 minutes first and use full-fat, which is much less likely to split in the heat.
Rogan josh tastes even better the next day, so make it ahead and reheat gently.
Sweet paprika gives the classic red colour without much heat; add more chilli powder only if you want it spicier.
variations: Swap the lamb for 1 kg beef chuck and simmer for about 1 hour longer, until tender.
Use 800 g chicken thigh fillets and cut the simmering time to 25 minutes, until cooked through with no pink inside.
For more heat, add 2 sliced green chillies with the garlic and ginger.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the fridge and reheat in a pot over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Roast lamb with rosemary
recipe.summary: A bone-in leg of lamb studded with garlic and rosemary, roasted until pink in the middle and served with crisp potatoes, sweet pumpkin and gravy.
ingredients: 6 medium potatoes (about 1.2 kg), peeled and quartered
1 Kent pumpkin (about 1 kg), cut into 5 cm wedges
2 brown onions, cut into thick wedges
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Stud the lamb with garlic and rosemary, rub with oil, salt and pepper, and sit it on the onion in a tray.
Parboil the potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes, drain and shake them rough. Roast the lamb 20 minutes at 200°C, then 170°C for 10 minutes.
Heat oil in a second tray, add the potatoes, and roast. After 15 minutes add the oiled pumpkin; roast 35 more minutes until the lamb reads 60°C.
Rest the lamb under foil for 20 minutes. Crisp the potatoes and pumpkin at 220°C until golden and the edges caramelise.
Cook the flour in the tray on medium for 1 minute, whisk in the stock and redcurrant jelly, and simmer 5 minutes until thick. Strain, carve and serve.

stages.title: Prepare the lamb and vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and take the lamb out of the fridge so it isn't fridge-cold when it goes in.
Use a small sharp knife to cut about 20 deep slits all over the lamb, then push a slice of garlic and a few rosemary leaves into each one until they sit snug below the surface.
Scatter the onion wedges over the base of a large roasting tray, sit the lamb on top, then rub with 2 tbsp of the olive oil, 1 tsp of the salt and half the pepper.

Put the potatoes in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, add a pinch of the salt and bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 8 minutes, until the edges of the potatoes look slightly fluffy but they still hold their shape.
Drain the potatoes in a colander, then shake them hard for 10 seconds to roughen the edges, which is what makes them crisp.

stages.title: Roast the lamb
steps: Slide the tray into the oven and roast the lamb at 200°C fan-forced for 20 minutes, until the surface is sizzling and starting to brown.
Reduce the oven to 170°C fan-forced and roast for another 10 minutes, keeping the door closed as much as you can so the oven doesn't lose heat.

stages.title: Roast the potatoes and pumpkin
steps: Pour 3 tbsp of the olive oil into a second large baking tray and heat it in the oven for 3 minutes, until the oil is shimmering.
Carefully add the potatoes, turn them in the hot oil with half the remaining salt and any leftover pepper, then return the tray to the oven beside the lamb.

After 15 minutes, toss the pumpkin wedges with the last of the olive oil and the remaining salt, then add them to the potato tray, spreading everything out in a single layer so it browns instead of steaming.

Keep roasting everything at 170°C fan-forced for another 35 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until a meat thermometer pushed into the thickest part of the lamb (away from the bone) reads 60°C for medium, and the potatoes are golden.

stages.title: Rest the lamb and make the gravy
steps: Lift the lamb onto a board, cover loosely with foil and rest for 20 minutes so the juices settle; slicing too early lets them run out and leaves the meat dry.
Raise the oven to 220°C fan-forced and return the potatoes and pumpkin for the 20 minutes the lamb rests, until the potatoes are deeply golden and crisp and the pumpkin edges are caramelised.
Meanwhile, tip off all but 2 tbsp of the fat from the roasting tray, then set the tray over medium heat on the stovetop, scraping up the browned bits and softened onion with a wooden spoon.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, until it forms a paste and smells nutty, then slowly pour in the stock a splash at a time, stirring so it doesn't go lumpy.
Add the redcurrant jelly and simmer for 5 minutes, until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, then strain it into a jug.
Carve the lamb into thick slices and serve with the potatoes, pumpkin and gravy.

tips: Use a meat thermometer: 55°C is rare, 60°C medium and 65°C well done, all before resting, as the temperature rises a few degrees while it rests.
Shaking the parboiled potatoes in the colander is the secret to crunchy edges, so don't skip it.
Salt the lamb up to a day ahead and leave it uncovered in the fridge for a drier surface and better browning.
If the gravy is too pale, add a splash of soy sauce for colour and depth.
variations: Swap the pumpkin for sweet potato or carrots, cut into similar-sized pieces.
Use a boneless rolled lamb leg and cut about 20 minutes off the roasting time, checking with a thermometer.
Add 4 anchovy fillets to the slits with the garlic for a deeper, savoury flavour that doesn't taste fishy.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days in an airtight container; reheat the lamb gently covered in the oven at 150°C, and crisp the potatoes uncovered at 200°C. Leftover gravy freezes for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Lamb souvlaki
recipe.summary: Lemon, garlic and oregano marinated lamb skewers, grilled until charred and tucked into warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and red onion.
ingredients: 800 g boneless lamb leg, cut into 3 cm cubes
method: Mix the oil, lemon zest and juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper and toss through the lamb. Marinate 15 minutes while the skewers soak, then thread on.
Slice the tomatoes and red onion, and get the salad leaves ready.
Heat a chargrill pan over medium-high heat. Cook the skewers 8–10 minutes, turning, until browned and just cooked through, then rest 3 minutes.
Warm the pita in a pan over medium heat, 30 seconds per side, until soft.
Fill the pita with tzatziki, tomato, onion and lamb. Serve with the salad leaves and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Marinate the lamb
steps: Soak the skewers in cold water for 15 minutes so they don't burn on the grill.
In a large bowl, mix the olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and black pepper.
Add the lamb and toss until every piece is coated, then leave it to marinate while the skewers soak.
Thread the lamb onto the drained skewers, leaving a small gap between pieces so the heat reaches all sides.

stages.title: Prep the toppings
steps: Slice the tomatoes and thinly slice the red onion, then set them out with the tzatziki.
Wash and dry the salad leaves now so everything reaches the table together.

stages.title: Grill the skewers
steps: Heat a large chargrill pan or barbecue plate over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.
Cook the skewers in batches for 8–10 minutes, turning every 2–3 minutes, until deeply browned with charred edges. Don't crowd the pan or the lamb will steam instead of char.
Cut into a piece to check: the centre should be just barely pink for juicy lamb, or no pink if you prefer it well done.
Rest the skewers on a plate for 3 minutes so the juices settle back into the meat.

stages.title: Warm the pita and serve
steps: Wipe out the pan and heat it over medium heat, then warm each pita for 30 seconds per side, until soft, pliable and lightly marked.
Spread each pita with tzatziki, then add the tomato, red onion and the lamb pulled off the skewers.
Fold or roll the pita and serve straight away with the salad leaves and lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Cut the lamb into even 3 cm cubes so the pieces cook at the same speed.
Don't marinate much longer than an hour, as the lemon juice can make the lamb mealy.
For even more flavour, marinate the lamb in the fridge for several hours or overnight, using only half the lemon juice and adding the rest after cooking.
Use metal skewers instead of wooden ones to skip the soaking.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets cut into 3 cm pieces and cook for 10–12 minutes, until no pink remains in the centre.
Make it vegetarian with thick halloumi slices and capsicum chunks on the skewers, grilled until golden.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the marinade for a little heat.
recipe.storage: Keep leftover lamb in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2–3 minutes, until hot through. Assemble the pita fresh.

recipe.title: Harissa lamb meatballs
recipe.summary: Spiced lamb mince meatballs simmered in a smoky harissa tomato sauce, served over fluffy couscous with cool yoghurt.
method: Mix the lamb mince, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, spices, chopped mint, salt and pepper until just combined, then roll into 20 balls.
Brown the meatballs in 1 tbsp of the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, 4 minutes a batch, until deep golden. Set aside.
Over medium heat, cook the onion in the remaining oil for 4 minutes until soft, then stir in the remaining garlic, harissa and tomato paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes and honey, return the meatballs, and simmer partly covered over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until no pink remains inside.
Soak the couscous in the boiling water, covered, for 5 minutes until absorbed, then fluff. Serve topped with meatballs, yoghurt, mint leaves and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Make the meatballs
steps: In a large bowl, combine the lamb mince, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, cumin, coriander, chopped mint, salt and pepper.
Mix with your hands for about 1 minute until just combined and sticky, as overmixing makes the meatballs tough.
Roll the mixture into 20 balls about the size of a golf ball and place them on a plate.

stages.title: Brown the meatballs and build the sauce
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat.
Brown the meatballs in two batches for 4 minutes per batch, turning occasionally, until deep golden on most sides, then move them to a plate; they will finish cooking in the sauce.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and the onion, and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Stir in the remaining garlic, harissa and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly.

stages.title: Simmer the meatballs
steps: Pour in the crushed tomatoes and honey, stir, and bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the base of the pan.

Return the meatballs to the pan, reduce the heat to medium-low, partly cover and simmer for 10 minutes, turning once, until the sauce thickens slightly and a meatball cut open is brown with no pink inside.
Meanwhile, put the couscous in a heatproof bowl, pour over the boiling water, cover and stand for 5 minutes until the water is absorbed, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Divide the couscous among four plates and top with the meatballs and sauce.
Add a spoonful of Greek yoghurt, scatter over the mint leaves and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Wet your hands with cold water when rolling so the mince doesn't stick.
Harissa brands vary a lot in heat, so start with 1 tbsp if yours is hot and add more at the end.
Make the meatballs a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge, then brown them just before cooking.
variations: Swap the lamb for beef or chicken mince for a milder meatball.
Add a 400 g tin of drained chickpeas to the sauce with the meatballs for extra body.
Serve with warm flatbread instead of couscous.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat the meatballs and sauce gently in a covered pan with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Lamb shanks
recipe.summary: Lamb shanks slowly braised in red wine and tomato until the meat falls off the bone, served with creamy mashed potato.
ingredients: 1 kg Desiree potatoes, peeled, cut into chunks
method: Heat the oven to 170°C fan-forced. Season the shanks with salt and pepper, then brown in the olive oil in a casserole over medium-high heat, 8–10 minutes per batch, until deep golden.
Reduce to medium and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6–7 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1–2 minutes until darkened.
Add the red wine and simmer 4–5 minutes until reduced by half. Add the tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary and bay leaves, then return the shanks.
Cover and braise in the oven for 1 hour 20 minutes, then uncover and turn the shanks. Cook 20 minutes more until the meat pulls from the bone.
Boil the potatoes over high then medium heat for 15 minutes until tender, then mash with the butter and warm milk.
Simmer the sauce over medium heat for 5 minutes until it coats a spoon, then serve over the shanks and mash.

stages.title: Prep and brown the shanks
steps: Heat the oven to 170°C fan-forced and dice the onion, carrots and celery, and crush the garlic.
Pat the lamb shanks dry with paper towel, then season all over with 1 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large flameproof casserole dish over medium-high heat until it shimmers.

Brown the shanks in two batches for 8–10 minutes per batch, turning every few minutes, until deep golden on all sides. Don't crowd the pan or they will steam instead of browning, then move them to a plate.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the onion, carrot and celery to the same dish. Cook for 6–7 minutes, stirring, until softened and lightly coloured.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 1–2 minutes until the paste darkens and smells sweet.
Pour in the red wine and scrape up the browned bits from the base. Simmer for 4–5 minutes until reduced by about half and the sharp alcohol smell fades.
Stir in the diced tomatoes, beef stock, rosemary and bay leaves, and bring to a simmer, then return the shanks to the dish so they are mostly submerged.

stages.title: Braise in the oven
steps: Cover the dish with a tight-fitting lid and braise in the oven for 1 hour 20 minutes.

Remove the lid, turn the shanks over and braise for another 20 minutes, until the meat is very tender, pulls away from the bone and a fork slides in with no resistance. If the meat still feels firm, return it for 15 minutes more.

stages.title: Make the mash and finish
steps: While the lamb finishes, put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, add the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce to medium and cook for 15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well, return to the pot off the heat and mash with the butter and warm milk until smooth and creamy.

Lift the shanks onto a plate and discard the rosemary stalks and bay leaves. Simmer the sauce in the dish over medium heat for 5 minutes until it coats the back of a spoon, then taste and adjust the seasoning.
Serve the shanks on the mash with plenty of sauce spooned over.

tips: Browning the shanks well builds most of the flavour, so take your time and don't crowd the pan.
Make it a day ahead: the flavour improves overnight and you can lift off the set fat from the top before reheating.
If the sauce is thin at the end, simmer it a few minutes longer rather than adding any thickener.
Desiree or Sebago potatoes give the creamiest mash.
variations: Swap the lamb shanks for 1.2 kg beef cheeks and braise for the same time until tender.
Add a strip of orange peel and a handful of Kalamata olives to the sauce for a Mediterranean twist.
Serve over creamy polenta or with steamed green beans instead of mash.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 3 days or frozen for 3 months in the sauce. Reheat gently, covered, in a 160°C fan-forced oven or in a pot over low heat until hot through.

recipe.title: Lamb backstrap with Greek salad
recipe.summary: Seared lean lamb backstrap sliced over a crisp Greek salad with feta and olives, ready in 25 minutes and high in protein.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, for the lamb
3 large tomatoes (about 500 g), cut into wedges
2 Lebanese cucumbers (about 250 g), sliced into half-moons
1 small green capsicum (about 150 g), thinly sliced
2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, for the dressing
method: Rub the dried lamb with olive oil, half the oregano, garlic, half the salt and the pepper.
Toss the tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, capsicum and olives with a dressing of vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, the remaining oregano and salt. Top with feta.
Sear the lamb in a very hot pan over high heat, 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and springy.
Rest the lamb under foil for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice across the grain over the salad. Serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Season the lamb
steps: Pat the lamb backstraps dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Rub them all over with the olive oil, 1 tsp of the oregano, the crushed garlic, half the salt and all the black pepper, then leave on the bench while you make the salad.

stages.title: Make the salad
steps: Put the tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, capsicum and olives in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, whisk the red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil, lemon juice, the remaining 1 tsp oregano and the remaining salt until combined.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss gently until everything is glossy, then scatter the feta on top without mixing it through so it stays in chunks.

stages.title: Sear the lamb
steps: Heat a large frying pan over high heat for 2 minutes until very hot and a drop of water sizzles at once.
Add the lamb and cook 3–4 minutes per side, until deeply browned and the meat feels springy when pressed, which is medium-rare (about 55°C in the centre). Cook 1–2 minutes longer per side for medium.
Avoid moving the lamb around in the pan, as it needs to sit still to build a crust.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Transfer the lamb to a board, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle back into the meat.
Slice the lamb across the grain into 1 cm slices, then arrange over the salad and spoon over any juices from the board.
Serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Slice the lamb across the grain for tender pieces, and don't skip the rest or the juices will run onto the board.
Use a meat thermometer if you have one: 55°C is medium-rare, 60°C is medium.
Cut the salad vegetables into similar-sized chunks so each forkful has a bit of everything.
Buy olives with pits in for better flavour, and warn the family to watch for them.
variations: Swap the lamb for 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cooked 5–6 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Make it vegetarian by replacing the lamb with thick slices of haloumi, fried 2 minutes per side until golden.
Serve with wholemeal pita or a small scoop of tzatziki for more bulk.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days, with the lamb and salad stored separately. Eat the lamb cold over the salad or reheat gently in a pan for 1 minute so it doesn't overcook. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Sweet and sour pork
recipe.summary: Crisp fried pork pieces tossed with capsicum, onion and pineapple in a tangy tomato-vinegar sauce, ready in 35 minutes.
ingredients: 2 pork loin steaks (about 600 g), cut into 2 cm pieces
1 large red capsicum (about 250 g), cut into 3 cm pieces
1 large green capsicum (about 250 g), cut into 3 cm pieces
1 large brown onion (about 200 g), cut into wedges
440 g can pineapple pieces in juice, drained
1/4 cup (60 ml) pineapple juice, from the can
method: Toss the pork with the salt, pepper and egg, then coat it in the 1/2 cup of cornflour. Whisk the pineapple juice, tomato sauce, vinegar, sugar, soy and the 2 tsp cornflour.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat. Fry the pork in two batches for 3–4 minutes each, until golden, crisp and no longer pink inside.
Pour off all but 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion and both capsicums over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, until the edges colour but the pieces keep a bite.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the sauce and simmer 2 minutes, until thick and glossy.
Toss through the pineapple and pork for 1 minute to coat. Serve straight away over steamed jasmine rice.

stages.title: Prepare the pork and sauce
steps: Season the pork with the salt and black pepper, then toss it in the beaten egg until every piece is coated.
Tip the 1/2 cup of cornflour onto a plate and press the egg-coated pork into it, shaking off the excess so the coating is thin and even. Thick, clumpy coating turns doughy instead of crisp.
In a small bowl, whisk the pineapple juice, tomato sauce, vinegar, brown sugar, soy sauce and the 2 tsp of cornflour until the sugar and cornflour dissolve and no lumps remain.

Cut the red and green capsicum and the onion, drain the pineapple, and chop the garlic and ginger, then set everything near the stove. If you are serving rice, start cooking the steamed jasmine rice now.

stages.title: Fry the pork
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large wok or deep frying pan over medium-high heat for about 2 minutes, until a pinch of cornflour sizzles straight away.
Fry half the pork for 3–4 minutes, turning once or twice, until golden and crisp. Cut one piece open to check there is no pink inside.
Lift the pork onto a paper towel-lined plate, then fry the second batch the same way. Crowding the pan drops the heat and makes the pork greasy, so keep to two batches.

stages.title: Cook the sauce and combine
steps: Carefully pour off all but 1 tbsp of oil from the wok and return it to medium-high heat.
Stir-fry the onion and the red and green capsicum for 3 minutes, until the edges start to colour but the pieces still have a bite.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Whisk the sauce again, then pour it in and simmer for 2 minutes, stirring, until it thickens, turns glossy and coats the back of a spoon.
Add the pineapple and the crisp pork and toss for 1 minute, just to coat and heat through. Serve straight away over the steamed jasmine rice, because the pork softens the longer it sits in the sauce.

tips: Pat the pork dry before coating, as wet meat makes the cornflour paste and the crumb won't crisp.
Keep the sauce separate until serving if you're not eating straight away, so the pork stays crunchy.
Use chicken thigh fillets instead of pork if you prefer, and fry them for 4–5 minutes per batch until cooked through.
Mix the sauce and cut the vegetables up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge.
variations: Swap the pork for 600 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 2 cm pieces.
For a vegetarian version, use 400 g firm tofu, pressed and cubed, and fry it until golden.
Add 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic for some heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in an airtight container, though the pork will soften. Reheat in a hot frying pan for 3–4 minutes until steaming, or on a tray in a 200°C oven for 10 minutes to help re-crisp the pork.

recipe.title: Curried sausages
recipe.summary: Beef sausages simmered in a mild curry gravy with potato, carrot and peas, served over rice for a cheap, filling family dinner.
ingredients: 2 medium potatoes (about 400 g), cut into 2 cm chunks
1 1/2 cups long-grain white rice, to serve
method: Brown the sausages in oil in a large pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes until golden, then slice and set aside.
Cook the onion over medium heat for 4 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, curry powder and flour and stir for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the stock, tomato paste, chutney and soy sauce until smooth.
Add the sausages, carrots and potatoes, cover and simmer on low for 15 minutes until the potato is tender. Cook the rice for 12 minutes meanwhile.
Stir in the peas, simmer 3 minutes until the gravy is thick and sausages have no pink inside, season with salt and pepper, and serve over rice.

stages.title: Brown the sausages
steps: Prick the sausages lightly and slice the onion, crush the garlic, slice the carrots and cut the potatoes into 2 cm chunks.

Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Brown the sausages for 5 minutes, turning, until golden all over, then move them to a plate. Don't worry that they are not cooked through yet.
Cut the sausages into thirds on an angle once they are cool enough to handle, about 2 minutes.

stages.title: Make the gravy
steps: Reduce the heat to medium and add the onion to the same pan with the sausage fat. Cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic, curry powder and a pinch of salt and cook for 1 minute until fragrant, then stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute so it loses its raw smell.
Pour in the stock a little at a time, stirring well so no lumps form, then stir in the tomato paste, chutney and soy sauce until smooth.

stages.title: Simmer the sausages and vegetables
steps: Return the sausages to the pan with the carrots and potatoes. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce to low, cover and cook for 15 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks, until the potato is tender when pierced with a knife.
Meanwhile, cook the rice in a pot of boiling water over medium-high heat for 12 minutes, until tender, then drain.
Stir the peas into the pan and simmer uncovered for 3 minutes, until the gravy is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon and the sausages are cooked through with no pink inside.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste, then serve over the rice.

tips: Don't skip browning the sausages, as the caramelised bits give the gravy its depth.
Add the stock gradually while stirring to keep the gravy smooth and lump-free.
Swap the rice for creamy mashed potato if you prefer, and leave the potato out of the pan.
variations: Use chicken or lamb sausages instead of beef.
Add a diced apple with the onion for a sweeter, old-fashioned gravy.
Stir in 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the curry powder for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if the gravy has thickened.

recipe.title: San choy bow
recipe.summary: Pork mince stir-fried with water chestnuts, ginger and oyster sauce, spooned into crisp lettuce cups for a quick, fresh dinner.
ingredients: 227 g tin water chestnuts, drained and finely chopped
1 iceberg lettuce, leaves separated into cups
1 tbsp crispy fried shallots, to serve
method: Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat, then brown the pork mince for 4–5 minutes, until no pink remains, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Reduce to medium-high and stir-fry the garlic, ginger, carrot and spring onion whites for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the water chestnuts and the mixed oyster sauce, soy sauce, cooking wine and sesame oil, and cook 2–3 minutes until glossy and coating the pork.
Stir through the spring onion greens, spoon into the lettuce cups, and top with crispy shallots and chilli.

stages.title: Prep the filling
steps: Finely chop the garlic and water chestnuts, grate the ginger, dice the carrot into 5 mm pieces and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts separate.
Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, Chinese cooking wine and sesame oil in a small bowl so the sauce is ready to pour in.
Peel the lettuce leaves off the head gently, choosing the roundest, deepest ones, then wash and pat them dry so the filling doesn't turn watery.

stages.title: Cook the pork
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.

Add the pork mince and break it up with a wooden spoon, then cook for 4–5 minutes, until browned with no pink left and any liquid has cooked off. Avoid crowding or stirring too early, or the pork will steam instead of browning.
Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Add the flavours
steps: Reduce the heat to medium-high, add the garlic, ginger, carrot and spring onion whites, and stir-fry for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the water chestnuts and pour in the sauce, then cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats the pork and the carrot is just tender but still crunchy.
Stir through the spring onion greens and take the pan off the heat.
Spoon the filling into the lettuce cups and top with the crispy fried shallots and the chilli, if using.

tips: Chop the water chestnuts finely so they stay crunchy without making the filling clumsy to eat.
Keep the lettuce cups cold and dry; soak the leaves in cold water for 10 minutes, then dry well, for extra crispness.
Let the pan get properly hot before adding the pork so it browns rather than stews.
Serve the filling and lettuce separately at the table so everyone fills their own cups and the lettuce stays crisp.
variations: Swap the pork for chicken mince or finely chopped chicken thigh fillets.
For a vegetarian version, use finely chopped shiitake mushrooms and firm tofu with a vegetarian oyster sauce.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or a spoonful of chilli oil to the sauce for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keep the cooked filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a hot pan until steaming, and add fresh lettuce cups only when serving.

recipe.title: Sausages with mash and onion gravy
recipe.summary: Pan-cooked beef or pork sausages with creamy mashed potato, peas and a rich onion gravy, a classic Aussie weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 kg potatoes, peeled and cut into 4 cm chunks
2 large brown onions (about 400 g), thinly sliced
method: Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Brown the sausages in the olive oil over medium heat for 10–12 minutes, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside. Set aside.

Cook the onions in the same pan over medium heat for 6–8 minutes, until soft and golden. Stir in the flour, Worcestershire sauce and beef stock, return the sausages, and simmer 4–5 minutes, until thickened.
Mash the drained potatoes with the butter, milk, salt and pepper until smooth and creamy.
Heat the peas with a little water over medium heat for 3 minutes, until bright green, then serve everything together.

stages.title: Cook the potatoes
steps: Put the potatoes in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, add a good pinch of salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium and simmer for 12–15 minutes, until a knife slides into a chunk with no resistance.

stages.title: Brown the sausages and onions
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the sausages and cook for 10–12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until deep golden and no pink remains in the centre when you cut into one.
Lift the sausages onto a plate and cover loosely with foil, leaving the browned bits and fat in the pan.

Add the sliced onions to the same pan over medium heat with a pinch of salt and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden brown. Don't let them blacken, as burnt onion makes the gravy bitter.

stages.title: Make the gravy
steps: Sprinkle the flour over the onions and stir for 1 minute, until no dry flour is visible and it smells slightly toasty.
Add the Worcestershire sauce, then pour in the beef stock a little at a time, stirring so no lumps form.
Return the sausages to the pan, then simmer over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes, until the gravy coats the back of a spoon. Season with black pepper.

stages.title: Mash and finish
steps: Drain the potatoes well and return them to the hot pan for 1 minute to steam off any water, which keeps the mash from going watery.
Add the butter and milk and mash until smooth and creamy, then season with salt and black pepper. Avoid using a food processor, which turns potato gluey.
Put the frozen peas in a small saucepan with 2 tbsp water over medium heat and cook for 3 minutes, until bright green and hot through, then drain.
Serve the sausages on the mash with the peas and plenty of onion gravy.

tips: Prick the sausages once or twice with a fork only if they're splitting; otherwise keep the juices in for better flavour in the gravy.
Warm the milk before adding it to the mash so the potato stays hot and fluffy.
Scrape up the browned bits from the pan when you add the stock, as they give the gravy its depth.
For a smoother gravy, whisk the stock in gradually rather than all at once.
variations: Use chicken or lamb sausages instead of beef or pork.
Swap the potato for sweet potato mash or a half potato, half cauliflower mash.
Add a tablespoon of wholegrain mustard to the gravy for extra tang.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in airtight containers for up to 3 days. Reheat the sausages, mash and gravy in the microwave or a covered pan over low heat until steaming hot, adding a splash of milk or stock if needed. The gravy freezes well for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Pork chops with apple
recipe.summary: Pan-fried pork chops with caramelised apple and a creamy mustard pan sauce, served with buttery greens, ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 4 pork loin chops (about 1 kg), bone in
2 Granny Smith apples (about 360 g), cut into wedges
method: Season the pork chops with the salt and pepper, then sear in hot olive oil over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes, then 3–4 minutes on the other side, until golden and 63°C inside. Rest 5 minutes.
Melt the butter in the pan over medium heat and cook the apple and onion for 4–5 minutes, until golden and soft.
Stir in the mustard and thyme for 30 seconds, then add the chicken stock and simmer 2 minutes, scraping up the browned bits.
Stir in the cream and simmer 1 minute until it coats a spoon.
Boil the green beans and broccolini for 3–4 minutes until bright and tender, then drain.
Return the chops to the sauce for 1 minute and serve with the greens.

stages.title: Prep and sear the chops
steps: Pat the pork chops dry with paper towel and season both sides with the salt and black pepper; dry meat browns better than damp meat.
Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes, until it shimmers.
Cook the chops for 4–5 minutes on one side, until deep golden and they release easily from the pan, then turn and cook 3–4 minutes more.
The pork is cooked when the thickest part reads 63°C or the juices run clear with only a hint of pink; transfer to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Caramelise the apple and make the sauce
steps: Reduce the pan to medium heat and add the butter, leaving the browned bits in the pan for flavour.
Add the apple wedges and onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 4–5 minutes, until the apple is golden at the edges and the onion is soft.
Stir in the mustard and thyme for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the chicken stock, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer for 2 minutes until reduced by about a third, then stir in the cream and simmer 1 minute until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Do not boil hard or the cream may split.

stages.title: Cook the greens and serve
steps: While the sauce simmers, bring a medium saucepan of salted water to the boil over high heat.
Cook the green beans and broccolini for 3–4 minutes, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife, then drain well.
Return the chops and any resting juices to the pan for 1 minute to warm through in the sauce, then serve with the greens.

tips: Choose chops at least 2 cm thick so they stay juicy while the outside browns.
Use a pan big enough to fit all four chops without crowding, or sear in two batches.
Granny Smith apples hold their shape; softer apples turn to mush in the pan.
Swap the cream for extra stock and a splash of milk for a lighter sauce.
variations: Use chicken thigh fillets instead of pork, cooking until 75°C inside.
Replace the stock with dry cider for a sharper, more traditional sauce.
Add a tablespoon of sage instead of thyme for a classic British flavour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan over low heat with a splash of stock or water until hot through; the chops freeze poorly once sauced.

recipe.title: Singapore noodles
recipe.summary: Rice vermicelli stir-fried with curry powder, prawns, char siu, egg and crisp vegetables, ready in 25 minutes in one wok.
ingredients: 300 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined
200 g char siu pork, thinly sliced
method: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4 minutes until soft, drain and toss with a little oil. Slice the vegetables, char siu and garlic, and mix the curry powder, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar.
Cook the prawns in a hot wok over high heat for 2 minutes until pink, seasoned with salt and pepper, then set aside. Scramble the eggs for 30-40 seconds until just set and set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic, carrots and capsicum over high heat for 2 minutes until tender-crisp. Add the char siu and sauce and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Toss in the noodles for 2-3 minutes until evenly yellow and hot, then return the prawns and egg with the bean sprouts and half the spring onions for 1 minute until the sprouts wilt.
Top with the remaining spring onions and serve with lemon wedges, if using.

stages.title: Prep the noodles and vegetables
steps: Place the vermicelli in a large heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and soak for 4 minutes, until soft but still slightly springy, then drain well and toss with 1 tsp of the oil so the strands don't stick.

While the noodles soak, slice the capsicum, cut the carrots into matchsticks, slice the spring onions and char siu, and chop the garlic, taking 5-6 minutes in total and keeping the pieces thin and even so they cook fast.
Stir the curry powder, soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves and you have a smooth, dark paste.

stages.title: Cook the prawns and egg
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large wok over high heat until it shimmers, then add the prawns, season with a pinch of salt and pepper and cook for 2 minutes, until pink and curled, then tip onto a plate.
Add 1 tbsp of the oil to the wok, pour in the eggs and cook for 30-40 seconds, until just set, then break into small pieces with your spoon and move to the plate with the prawns.

stages.title: Stir-fry and combine
steps: Heat the remaining oil in the wok over high heat, add the garlic, carrots and capsicum and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until the carrot is bright and just tender-crisp.
Add the char siu and the sauce mixture and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant and the curry powder smells toasted, but don't let it scorch.
Add the noodles and toss with tongs for 2-3 minutes, until evenly yellow and heated through, lifting from the bottom so they don't break up or stick.

Return the prawns and egg to the wok, add the bean sprouts and half the spring onions, and toss for 1 minute, until the sprouts just wilt and the prawns are hot, then season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve straight away, topped with the remaining spring onions and with lemon wedges on the side, if using.
