tips: Don't over-soak the vermicelli, as it keeps softening in the wok and turns mushy if it starts out too soft.
Cook in a very hot wok and keep the ingredients moving so the noodles fry rather than steam.
Use a Madras-style curry powder for the classic yellow colour and mild heat.
Have everything sliced and the sauce mixed before you turn on the heat, because the stir-fry moves fast.
variations: Swap the prawns for sliced chicken thigh, cooking it for 4-5 minutes until no pink remains in the centre.
For a vegetarian version, leave out the prawns and char siu and use fried firm tofu and mushrooms, with extra soy sauce in place of the oyster sauce.
Add 1 sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat in a hot wok or microwave with a splash of water until steaming hot throughout; not suitable for freezing as the noodles go soft.

recipe.title: Honey mustard pork fillet with roast vegetables
recipe.summary: Lean pork fillet glazed with honey and wholegrain mustard, roasted on one tray with pumpkin, carrots and broccolini for an easy, high-protein weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 600 g pumpkin, peeled and cut into 3 cm pieces
3 carrots (about 300 g), cut into 2 cm chunks
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Roast the pumpkin and carrots with half the oil, salt and pepper for 10 minutes, until the edges start to colour.
Mix the mustard, honey, garlic and lemon juice. Brush half over the pork, add the thyme, and season.
Roast the pork for 10 minutes, then brush with the remaining glaze.
Toss the broccolini with the remaining oil and add to the vegetables. Roast 8–10 minutes, until the pork reaches 63°C with a hint of pink and the broccolini is charred.
Rest the pork for 5 minutes, then slice and serve with the vegetables and lemon wedges, if using.

stages.title: Prep and start the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin and carrots on one tray with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, half the salt and half the pepper, then spread them in a single layer so they roast rather than steam.
Mix the wholegrain mustard, honey, garlic and lemon juice in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Pat the pork fillets dry with paper towel, trim off any silver skin, and tuck the thin tail ends under so the fillets are an even thickness.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables and pork
steps: Put the vegetable tray in the oven and roast for 10 minutes, until the edges are just starting to colour.
Place the pork on the second tray, brush it all over with half the glaze, scatter with the thyme, and season with the remaining salt and pepper.
Move the vegetables to the lower shelf if needed, put the pork tray in the oven, and roast both for 10 minutes.
Brush the pork with the remaining glaze and toss the broccolini with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, then add it to the vegetable tray.

Roast for another 8–10 minutes, until the pork is golden and reads 63°C in the thickest part (or the juices run clear with only a hint of pink in the centre) and the broccolini is tender with charred tips. Avoid overcooking, as lean pork dries out quickly.

stages.title: Rest and serve
steps: Cover the pork loosely with foil and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle; slicing too soon will leave the meat dry.
Slice the pork into 1.5 cm thick pieces and spoon over any juices from the tray.
Serve with the roast vegetables and lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Use a meat thermometer if you have one; pulling the pork at 63°C and resting it keeps it juicy and safely cooked.
Cut the pumpkin and carrots to the same size so they finish cooking together.
Trim the silver skin from the pork, as it stays chewy when cooked.
Swap the thyme for rosemary if that's what you have.
variations: Use chicken breast fillets or thighs instead of pork and roast until the centre reaches 75°C.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the glaze for a bit of heat.
Swap the pumpkin for sweet potato or the broccolini for green beans.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a covered dish in a 160°C oven or microwave on medium until hot through; the pork can also be served cold in sandwiches.

recipe.title: Pork and fennel sausage pasta
recipe.summary: Pork and fennel sausage meat is browned with chilli and garlic, simmered in tomato and tossed through penne with spinach for a quick, hearty dinner.
ingredients: 1/2 cup finely grated parmesan, plus extra to serve
method: Boil the penne in a large pot of well-salted water over high heat for 10–11 minutes, until al dente. Drain, saving a little of the water.
Squeeze the sausage meat from the casings and brown it in the olive oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until no pink remains.
Add the onion for 3 minutes until soft, then the garlic and chilli flakes for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the crushed tomatoes and water and simmer for 4 minutes, until thickened slightly.
Toss in the pasta and spinach for 1–2 minutes, until the spinach wilts, then stir through the parmesan, salt and pepper.

stages.title: Start the pasta and prep
steps: Fill a large pot with water, add a generous pinch of salt and bring to the boil over high heat, about 5 minutes, until at a rolling boil.
While it heats, dice the onion and finely chop the garlic.
Slit each sausage casing lengthways with a knife and squeeze the meat out into a bowl, discarding the casings, then break the meat into rough chunks with your hands.

stages.title: Cook the sausage sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat, then add the sausage meat and cook for 5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned with no pink remaining. Avoid stirring constantly, as leaving it to sit for short stretches gives better browning.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion and a pinch of salt and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and water.
Simmer for 4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and combine
steps: Add the penne to the boiling water and cook for 10–11 minutes, or according to the packet, until al dente, tender with a slight bite. This runs alongside the sauce stage, so start it as soon as the sausage goes into the pan.
Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta.
Add the pasta and spinach to the sauce over low heat and toss for 1–2 minutes, until the spinach wilts and the sauce clings to the pasta, loosening with a splash of pasta water if it looks dry.
Stir through the parmesan, then season with salt and black pepper to taste and serve with extra parmesan.

tips: Squeezing the meat from the casings is quickest if you slit each sausage along its length first.
Let the sausage meat sit undisturbed for a minute or two at a time so it browns instead of steaming.
Pasta water has starch that helps the sauce cling, so always keep a little back before draining.
Swap penne for rigatoni or orecchiette, as the sauce catches nicely in their shapes.
variations: Use chicken and sage sausages instead of pork and fennel for a milder flavour.
Stir in 1/2 cup of cream with the tomatoes for a richer, creamier sauce.
Add 1 tbsp of baby capers with the garlic for a salty, briny kick.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen for up to 2 months. Reheat in a pan over medium heat with a splash of water for 3–4 minutes, until steaming hot throughout.

recipe.title: Lemon herb crumbed basa
recipe.summary: Basa fillets baked under a lemon, parsley and parmesan panko crust, served with baby potatoes and steamed greens for a light, crunchy weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 1 lemon, zested, then cut into wedges
1 head broccoli (about 350 g), cut into florets
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Simmer the potatoes in salted water over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Mix the panko, parmesan, half the parsley, lemon zest, garlic, 1 tbsp oil, salt and pepper. Dry the basa, then coat in flour, egg and the crumb.
Bake the fish for 12 minutes, until golden and it flakes easily with a fork.
Steam the broccoli and beans over medium-high heat for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender, then drain.
Toss the drained potatoes with the remaining oil and parsley, then serve everything with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Start the potatoes and crumb the fish
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Put the potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold salted water and bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes, until a fork slides in easily. Don't let the water boil hard or the potatoes will break up.
In a bowl, mix the panko, parmesan, half the parsley, the lemon zest, the garlic, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper until it looks like damp sand.
Put the flour in one shallow dish and the beaten eggs in another. Pat the basa fillets very dry with paper towel, as wet fish makes the crumb slide off.
Season the fillets with the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, dust each one in flour and shake off the excess, dip in the egg, then press firmly into the crumb on both sides. Place on the tray.

stages.title: Bake the fish and cook the greens
steps: Bake the fish on the middle shelf for 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish turns white and opaque and flakes easily when pressed with a fork. Don't turn the fillets, as basa is delicate and will break.
When the potatoes are tender, drain them and return them to the warm pot with the lid on.

Add about 2 cm of water to a medium saucepan and bring to the boil over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli and green beans, cover and steam for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife, then drain.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Toss the potatoes with the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining parsley.
Divide the fish, potatoes, broccoli and beans among four plates and serve straight away with lemon wedges, if you like.

tips: Pat the fish very dry before flouring so the crumb sticks and crisps up.
Place the tray on the middle shelf, not the top, so the crumb browns without burning.
Make the crumb mix up to 2 days ahead and keep it in the fridge.
Use a squeeze of fresh lemon over the fish at the table for brightness without adding fat.
variations: Swap basa for firm white fish like hoki or barramundi fillets, adding 2 to 3 minutes if they are thicker.
Add 1/2 tsp smoked paprika or a pinch of chilli flakes to the crumb for more kick.
Use chicken breast cut into thin schnitzels and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until the juices run clear.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh while the crumb is crisp. Leftover fish keeps in the fridge for 1 day; reheat on a tray in a 200°C oven for 8 minutes, until hot through and the crumb crisps again.

recipe.title: Oven-baked fish and chips
recipe.summary: Crumbed basa fillets and potato chips baked until crisp, served with homemade tartare sauce and lemon for a lighter take on the classic.
ingredients: 4 large potatoes (about 1 kg), cut into 1 cm chips
Olive oil spray, for the fish
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Toss the potato chips with oil, paprika, salt and pepper, spread on a tray and bake 15 minutes, until the edges colour.
Dry the basa, season, then coat in flour, egg, and panko mixed with garlic powder. Spray the tops with oil on a second tray.
Turn the chips and bake with the fish for 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes and is opaque throughout.
Mix the mayonnaise, gherkins, capers, parsley and lemon juice for the tartare. Serve with the lemon wedges.

stages.title: Bake the chips
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Dry the potato chips well with a clean tea towel, then toss them in a large bowl with the olive oil, smoked paprika, half the salt and half the black pepper.
Spread the chips in a single layer across one tray, leaving space between them, as crowded chips steam instead of crisping.
Bake the chips for 15 minutes on the top shelf, until the edges are starting to colour, then leave them in while you crumb the fish.

stages.title: Crumb the fish
steps: Pat the basa fillets dry with paper towel and season them with the remaining salt and black pepper.
Put the flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with the garlic powder into three separate shallow dishes.
Coat each fillet in flour and shake off the excess, dip it in the egg, then press it firmly into the panko so it is covered all over.
Place the crumbed fillets on the second lined tray and spray the tops lightly with olive oil, which helps the crumb turn golden.

stages.title: Bake the fish and make the tartare
steps: Turn the chips over, slide the fish tray onto the lower shelf, and bake both for 12 minutes, until the crumb is golden and the fish flakes easily with a fork and is opaque all the way through.
While they bake, stir the mayonnaise, gherkins, capers, parsley and lemon juice together in a small bowl to make the tartare sauce.
Rest the fish for 2 minutes, then serve with the chips, tartare sauce and lemon wedges. Avoid turning the fish, as the underside crumb can lose its crunch.

tips: Dry the potato chips thoroughly before oiling so they crisp rather than steam.
Press the panko on firmly so the crumb stays on the fish while baking.
Use a hot oven and a single layer on each tray; crowding gives soggy chips.
Swap basa for any firm white fish, such as flathead or hoki, adjusting the time for thickness.
variations: Use sweet potato chips instead of regular potato for a sweeter side.
Add 1 tsp lemon zest and a pinch of chilli flakes to the panko for extra flavour.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the crumb and chips soften in the fridge. Leftover fish keeps 1 day refrigerated; reheat on a tray at 200°C for 8 minutes to re-crisp.

recipe.title: Goan fish curry
recipe.summary: White fish gently poached in a tangy coconut, tomato and tamarind sauce, served over rice for an easy weeknight curry.
ingredients: 600 g firm white fish fillets (basa), cut into 4 cm pieces
1 tsp salt, plus extra to taste
1 large brown onion (about 200 g), finely diced
3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
1 cup fresh coriander leaves, roughly chopped
method: Season the fish with the salt. Dice the onion and tomatoes, grate the garlic and ginger, and slit the chillies.
Cook the onion in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 5–6 minutes until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 3–4 minutes until pulpy.
Add the coconut milk, tamarind, sugar and green chillies. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes until slightly thickened, then season with salt and pepper.
Add the fish and cook on low for 4–5 minutes until opaque and flaking. Top with coriander and serve with rice and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep the fish
steps: Cut the fish into 4 cm pieces and toss with the 1 tsp salt and the turmeric from the spice list, if you like, or simply season it with the salt and set aside.
Dice the onion, grate the garlic and ginger, chop the tomatoes and coriander, and slit the green chillies lengthways so everything is ready before you start cooking.

stages.title: Build the sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat, add the onion and cook for 5–6 minutes, stirring often, until soft and light golden.

Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute until fragrant, then add the ground coriander, cumin, turmeric and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds until the spices smell toasty; don't let them scorch or the curry will taste bitter.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3–4 minutes, stirring and pressing down, until they break down into a thick paste.

stages.title: Simmer and finish
steps: Pour in the coconut milk, then stir in the tamarind paste, sugar and green chillies, and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat for 4–5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and looks glossy.
Taste and season with salt and black pepper, adding a little more tamarind if you want it tangier.

Slide in the fish pieces in a single layer and spoon sauce over them, then cook gently for 4–5 minutes until the fish turns opaque and flakes easily with a fork; stir very gently, as the fish breaks up if handled roughly, and keep the heat low so the coconut milk doesn't split.
Scatter over the fresh coriander and serve over steamed basmati rice with lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Use firm fish such as basa, barramundi or ling so the pieces hold together in the sauce.
Add tamarind a little at a time and taste, as brands vary a lot in sourness.
Make the sauce up to 2 days ahead and add the fish just before serving for the best texture.
Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer once the coconut milk is in, because a hard boil can make it split.
variations: Swap the fish for raw peeled prawns and cook for 3–4 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian with cubes of firm tofu or cooked chickpeas instead of fish.
Add another green chilli or 1 tsp more chilli powder for extra heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 days in an airtight container. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until just hot; don't freeze, as the fish turns mushy.

recipe.title: Crispy skin barramundi with greens
recipe.summary: Pan-fried skin-on barramundi with shatteringly crisp skin, served on garlicky greens with lemon for a light, protein-rich dinner.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, for the greens
1 lemon, zested and cut into wedges
method: Dry the barramundi well, score the skin, and season with salt and pepper. Trim the broccolini and beans, and zest the lemon.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fillets skin-side down, pressing flat, for 5–6 minutes until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip, add the butter, and cook 1–2 minutes until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Rest on a plate.
Heat the greens oil over medium-high. Cook the broccolini and beans with the water for 3–4 minutes until tender, then add garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the spinach, salt and lemon zest for 1 minute until wilted. Serve the fish on the greens with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep the fish and greens
steps: Pat the barramundi fillets very dry on both sides with paper towel, paying extra attention to the skin, because any moisture will stop it crisping.
Score the skin of each fillet lightly with a sharp knife, then season the skin side with the 1/2 tsp salt for the fish and the black pepper.
Halve the broccolini stems lengthways if they are thick, and zest the lemon, then cut the zested lemon into wedges.

stages.title: Cook the barramundi
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for about 1 minute, until the oil shimmers.
Lay the fillets in the pan skin-side down, pressing each one flat with a spatula for 20 seconds so the skin makes full contact and does not curl.
Cook for 5–6 minutes without moving them, until the skin is deep golden and crisp and the flesh has turned opaque about three-quarters of the way up the side.

Flip the fillets, add the butter, and cook for 1–2 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. Move to a plate, skin-side up, and avoid covering them or the skin will go soft.

stages.title: Cook the greens
steps: Wipe out the pan, then heat the 1 tbsp olive oil for the greens over medium-high heat for 30 seconds.
Add the broccolini and green beans with the 2 tbsp water, and cook for 3–4 minutes, tossing often, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, stirring, until fragrant but not browned, as burnt garlic turns bitter.
Stir through the baby spinach, the 1/2 tsp salt for the greens and the lemon zest for 1 minute, until the spinach has just wilted.
Divide the greens among four plates, top with the barramundi skin-side up and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Dry skin and a properly hot pan are what make the skin crisp, so never skip the paper towel step.
Don't move the fillets while the skin side cooks, or the skin will stick and tear.
Swap the broccolini for asparagus or zucchini ribbons depending on what looks good at the shops.
variations: Use skin-on salmon fillets instead, cooking the skin side for 4–5 minutes and the flesh side for 2 minutes.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for a spicy kick.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the skin loses its crunch once stored. Leftover greens keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat gently in a pan.

recipe.title: Cajun basa with corn salsa
recipe.summary: Cajun-spiced basa fillets pan-fried until golden, served on rice with a fresh corn, tomato and avocado salsa.
ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, for the fish
1 x 300 g can corn kernels, drained
1 tbsp olive oil, for the salsa
method: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered on low heat with water and a pinch of the salt for 10–12 minutes, until tender. Rest 5 minutes, then fluff.
Toss the corn kernels, tomatoes, avocado, red onion and coriander with the lime juice, salsa oil, remaining salt and pepper.
Pat the basa dry and coat it in the Cajun spice and flour mix.
Fry in the fish oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until golden, flip, then cook 2–3 minutes until opaque and flaking.
Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa and lime wedges if using.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then put it in a medium saucepan with 1 1/2 cups of water and 1/4 tsp of the salt.
Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and cook for 10–12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice is tender.
Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Don't lift the lid while it cooks or the steam escapes and the rice cooks unevenly.

stages.title: Make the corn salsa
steps: While the rice cooks, combine the drained corn kernels, cherry tomatoes, avocado, red onion and coriander in a bowl.

Add the lime juice, the olive oil for the salsa, the remaining salt and the black pepper, then toss gently until everything is coated. Fold the avocado in gently so it stays in chunks rather than turning mushy.

stages.title: Cook the basa
steps: Pat the basa fillets dry with paper towel, then mix the Cajun spice mix and flour on a plate and press each fillet into it to coat both sides lightly.
Heat the olive oil for the fish in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the fillets for 3 minutes without moving them, until the underside is deeply golden and releases easily from the pan.
Flip carefully and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh is opaque all the way through and flakes easily with a fork. Basa is delicate, so turn it only once to stop it breaking apart.
Serve the fish on the rice with the salsa spooned over and lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Pat the fillets very dry so the spice crust browns instead of steaming.
Check your Cajun mix for salt; some are very salty, so taste the salsa before adding extra salt.
Dice the salsa ingredients while the rice cooks, but add the avocado last so it doesn't brown.
variations: Swap the basa for chicken tenderloins, cooking them 4–5 minutes per side until no pink remains.
Add 1 finely chopped fresh chilli to the salsa for more heat.
Serve in warmed tortillas with shredded cabbage instead of rice for fish tacos.
recipe.storage: Keep the fish, rice and salsa in separate containers in the fridge for up to 1 day. Reheat the fish and rice in the microwave until steaming hot; the salsa is best fresh as the avocado browns.

recipe.title: Barramundi with Thai herb salad
recipe.summary: Seared barramundi fillets served on a crunchy salad of herbs, cucumber and carrot with a sharp lime and chilli dressing, light and high in protein.
ingredients: 1 cup coriander leaves and soft stems
method: Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, garlic and chilli until the sugar dissolves.
Dry the barramundi, rub with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Toss the cucumber, carrot, red onion, coriander, mint and Thai basil in a bowl.
Heat a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the fillets skin-side down for 5–6 minutes, until the skin is golden and crisp.
Flip and cook 2–3 minutes, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily. Rest for 2 minutes.
Toss the salad with most of the dressing, plate it with the fish, then add the rest of the dressing and the peanuts. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: In a small bowl, whisk the lime juice, fish sauce and brown sugar for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves and no grains remain.
Stir in the grated garlic and sliced chilli, then taste and adjust: it should be sharp, salty and a little sweet. Add more chilli only if you want extra heat.

stages.title: Prepare the salad
steps: Pat the barramundi fillets very dry with paper towel, rub them with the olive oil and season both sides with salt and black pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the cucumber, carrot, red onion, coriander, mint and Thai basil, but do not dress it yet, as the herbs wilt quickly once the dressing goes on.

stages.title: Cook the barramundi
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan or chargrill pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.

Lay the fillets in the pan skin-side down and press gently for 10 seconds so the skin stays flat. Cook for 5–6 minutes without moving them, until the skin is golden and crisp and the flesh is opaque about two-thirds of the way up the side.
Flip the fillets and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the flesh turns opaque all the way through and flakes easily when pressed with a fork. Rest on a plate for 2 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Pour about three-quarters of the dressing over the salad and toss gently for 20 seconds, until the leaves are lightly coated.
Divide the salad among four plates, top each with a barramundi fillet, then spoon over the remaining dressing and scatter with the chopped peanuts. Serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Dry skin is the secret to crisp skin: pat the fillets well and don't move them while the skin cooks.
Dress the salad just before serving, or the herbs and cucumber turn limp and watery.
Soak the sliced red onion in cold water for 5 minutes if you want a milder bite.
No Thai basil? Use regular basil, or just more mint and coriander.
variations: Swap the barramundi for salmon fillets or firm white fish, adjusting the cooking time to the thickness.
Make it vegetarian with pan-fried firm tofu and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes or a second chilli to the dressing for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the dressed herbs wilt. Keep leftover cooked fish and undressed salad separately in the fridge for up to 1 day, and eat the fish cold or reheat gently in a low oven for 5 minutes.

recipe.title: Miso salmon tray bake
recipe.summary: Salmon fillets glazed with sweet-salty miso and roasted on one tray with broccoli and edamame, served over brown rice for a balanced, high-protein dinner.
ingredients: 2 heads broccoli (about 600 g), cut into florets
2 x 250 g microwave brown rice pouches
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Whisk the miso, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, sesame oil and ginger until smooth, and pat the salmon dry.
Toss the broccoli and edamame with the olive oil, salt and pepper on a lined tray. Roast 10 minutes, until the broccoli edges start to brown.
Nestle the salmon in the middle of the tray and spoon the glaze over the fish and vegetables.
Roast 10 minutes, until the glaze is sticky and the salmon is opaque and flakes with a fork.
Microwave the rice pouches on high for 2 minutes, until steaming, then serve topped with the salmon, vegetables, spring onions, sesame seeds and lime wedges.

stages.title: Make the glaze and prep
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
In a small bowl, whisk the miso paste, soy sauce, honey, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil and ginger for about 1 minute, until smooth and runny with no lumps of miso.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towel so the glaze sticks, then set them aside on a plate.
Cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets and tip them onto the tray with the frozen edamame.

stages.title: Roast the vegetables
steps: Drizzle the olive oil over the broccoli and edamame, sprinkle with the salt and black pepper, and toss with your hands until everything is lightly coated.
Spread the vegetables out in a single layer, leaving a gap in the middle of the tray for the salmon, and roast on the middle shelf for 10 minutes, until the broccoli edges are just starting to brown.
Avoid overcrowding the tray, as piled-up broccoli steams instead of roasting.

stages.title: Glaze and roast the salmon
steps: Take the tray out, then push the vegetables to the sides and place the salmon fillets skin-side down in the middle.
Brush or spoon the miso glaze generously over the top of each fillet, and drizzle any leftover glaze over the vegetables.
Roast for 10 minutes, until the glaze is sticky and the salmon turns opaque and flakes easily when pressed with a fork in the thickest part.
Check the salmon at 8 minutes if your fillets are thin, because overcooked salmon turns dry and chalky.

stages.title: Heat the rice and serve
steps: While the salmon rests on the tray for 2 minutes, microwave the brown rice pouches on high for 2 minutes, until steaming hot, then squeeze the pouches to break up the grains.
Divide the rice among four bowls, top with the broccoli, edamame and a salmon fillet, then scatter over the spring onions and sesame seeds.
Serve with lime wedges on the side, if you like.

tips: Pat the salmon dry before glazing, otherwise the glaze slides off and pools on the tray.
Miso brands vary in saltiness, so use reduced-salt soy sauce and taste the glaze before using; add a little more honey if it's too salty.
Thin tail-end fillets cook faster, so choose similar-sized pieces or check the thinner ones a couple of minutes early.
Make the glaze up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge to speed up weeknight cooking.
variations: Swap the salmon for ocean trout or firm tofu slabs, pressed dry, and roast the tofu for 20 minutes.
Replace the broccoli with sliced zucchini, green beans or broccolini, and add a pinch of chilli flakes to the glaze for heat.
Use microwave quinoa or cooked brown rice mixed with cucumber for a cooler, fresher base.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in the microwave on medium for 1–2 minutes, until just warmed through, to avoid drying out the salmon.

recipe.title: Garlic prawn linguine
recipe.summary: Juicy prawns and linguine tossed in a quick garlic, chilli, white wine and lemon sauce, ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
1 small bunch flat-leaf parsley, leaves chopped
method: Boil the linguine in well-salted water for 9 minutes, until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Cook the seasoned prawns in hot olive oil over medium-high heat, 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and curled. Set aside.
Stir the garlic and chilli over medium heat for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add the wine and simmer 2 minutes, until reduced by half.
Toss in the linguine, butter, lemon zest and juice, and half the parsley for 1 minute.
Return the prawns, add a splash of pasta water and toss 1 minute, until glossy. Season with salt and pepper, top with the remaining parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Prep and boil the water
steps: Fill a large pot with water, add a generous pinch of salt and bring to a rolling boil over high heat, about 6 minutes.
While you wait, pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam, then season them with salt and black pepper.
Thinly slice the garlic, finely chop the chilli, pick and chop the parsley leaves, and zest then juice the lemon.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and prawns
steps: Add the linguine to the boiling water and cook for 9 minutes, stirring once in the first minute so it doesn't stick, until al dente with a little bite in the centre.
Meanwhile, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until they turn pink and curl into a loose C shape; a tight O means overcooked. Transfer them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic and chilli and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant and just pale golden. Don't let the garlic brown or it turns bitter.
Pour in the white wine and simmer for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits, until reduced by about half.
Scoop out 1 cup of the pasta cooking water, then drain the linguine.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the drained linguine to the frying pan along with the butter, lemon zest, lemon juice and half the parsley, and toss over medium heat for 1 minute.
Return the prawns and any juices to the pan, add a splash of the reserved pasta water and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce turns glossy and clings to the pasta. Add more water if it looks dry.
Taste and adjust with salt and black pepper, then serve straight away topped with the remaining parsley and lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the prawns very dry before cooking so they sear instead of stewing in their own liquid.
Pull the prawns out of the pan while you make the sauce; they cook in minutes and go rubbery if left in.
The starchy pasta water is what turns the oil, wine and butter into a silky sauce, so don't skip it.
Slice the garlic rather than crushing it; it's less likely to burn and gives milder, sweeter flavour.
variations: Swap the prawns for scallops or firm white fish pieces, cooking until just opaque.
Make it vegetarian with 400 g sautéed zucchini and a handful of baby spinach instead of prawns.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the garlic for more heat, or a handful of halved cherry tomatoes with the wine.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the prawns turn tough when reheated. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day; reheat gently in a pan over low heat with a splash of water.

recipe.title: Thai red prawn curry
recipe.summary: Prawns, capsicum and green beans simmered in a fragrant red curry and coconut sauce, served over jasmine rice in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 200 g green beans, trimmed and halved
800 g raw prawns, peeled and deveined, tails left on
method: Cook the jasmine rice with a pinch of salt following the packet directions, and prep the capsicum, beans and lime.
Fry the curry paste in the oil over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, fish sauce and sugar, then simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Simmer the capsicum and beans for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beans are bright green and just tender.
Add the prawns and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until pink, curled and opaque. Stir in the lime juice and season with salt and pepper.
Serve over the rice with the coriander and lime wedges, if using.

stages.title: Cook the rice and prep
steps: Rinse the jasmine rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear, then cook it following the packet directions with a pinch of salt in the water, so it is ready when the curry is done.
Slice the capsicum, trim and halve the green beans, and juice the lime, then keep the prawns, coriander and fish sauce within reach, because the curry cooks quickly.

stages.title: Build the curry sauce
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat, then add the red curry paste and stir for 1 minute, until it smells fragrant and darkens slightly.

Pour in both cans of coconut milk, add the fish sauce and brown sugar, and stir well. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is slightly thickened and glossy; avoid a hard boil, which can make the coconut milk split.

stages.title: Cook the vegetables and prawns
steps: Add the capsicum and green beans to the sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until the beans are bright green and just tender with a slight bite.

Add the prawns and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until they turn pink and curl into a loose C shape and are opaque all the way through. Do not overcook them, as they turn tough and rubbery.
Stir in the lime juice, then taste and season with salt and black pepper, adding a little more fish sauce if it needs more savoury depth.
Serve the curry over the rice, scattered with the coriander leaves and with lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Use prawns that are fully thawed and patted dry so they do not water down the sauce.
Red curry pastes vary in heat, so start with 2 tablespoons if yours is hot and add more at the end.
Cut the vegetables ahead and keep them in the fridge, which makes this a very quick weeknight dinner.
variations: Swap the prawns for 600 g chicken thigh fillets, sliced thinly, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked through.
Make it vegetarian with firm tofu and extra vegetables, and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Add a finely sliced red chilli or an extra tablespoon of curry paste for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a pan over low heat until just hot, as the prawns toughen if reheated for long. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: Prawn zucchini noodles
recipe.summary: Garlic and chilli prawns tossed through spiralised zucchini and blistered cherry tomatoes, a light, high-protein dinner ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 500 g raw king prawns, peeled and deveined
method: Pat the prawns dry and season with the salt and pepper. Sear in 1 tbsp olive oil in a hot pan over high heat for 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and curled. Set aside.
Lower to medium heat and add the remaining oil, garlic and chilli. Stir 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and cook 2–3 minutes until they burst.
Toss in the zucchini noodles for 1–2 minutes, until just tender but still with a little bite.
Return the prawns with the lemon zest and juice and toss 30 seconds until hot. Stir through the basil, top with parmesan and serve.

stages.title: Prepare the ingredients
steps: Pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they sear rather than steam, then season them with the salt and black pepper.
Spiralise the zucchini into noodles, halve the cherry tomatoes, slice the garlic and chilli, zest and juice the lemon, tear the basil and grate the parmesan.

stages.title: Cook the prawns
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large frying pan over high heat until it shimmers.

Add the prawns in a single layer and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and curled into a loose C shape with no grey flesh left. Do not overcook them or they turn rubbery; tip them onto a plate.

stages.title: Cook the tomatoes and zucchini
steps: Return the pan to medium heat and add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil, the garlic and the chilli. Stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant and the garlic is just pale gold; do not let it brown or it turns bitter.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook for 2–3 minutes, until they soften and start to burst.
Add the zucchini noodles and toss for 1–2 minutes, until just warmed and tender but still with a little bite. Cooking them any longer makes them watery.
Return the prawns and any juices to the pan, add the lemon zest and juice, and toss for 30 seconds until everything is hot.
Take the pan off the heat, then stir through the basil and serve topped with the parmesan.

tips: Salt draws water out of zucchini, so season the prawns, not the noodles, and serve straight away.
If you have no spiraliser, use a julienne peeler or buy ready-made zucchini noodles from the fresh produce section.
Make sure the pan is properly hot before the prawns go in so they sear quickly and stay juicy.
variations: Swap the prawns for 500 g chicken breast strips, cooked 4–5 minutes until no pink remains in the centre.
Use 400 g firm tofu, cubed and pan-fried until golden, for a vegetarian version, and skip the parmesan or use a vegetarian hard cheese.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the zucchini releases water and goes soft. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day; reheat briefly in a hot pan for 1 minute.

recipe.title: Tuna and tomato spaghetti
recipe.summary: A quick pantry pasta of spaghetti tossed in a garlicky chilli tomato sauce with canned tuna and capers.
ingredients: 2 x 185 g cans tuna in olive oil, drained
1 tsp salt, plus extra for the pasta water
method: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water over high heat for 9–10 minutes until just tender, then reserve 1/2 cup of the water and drain.
Fry the garlic and chilli flakes in the olive oil over medium heat for 30–60 seconds until fragrant and pale golden.
Add the tomatoes, capers, salt and pepper and simmer for 6–7 minutes until thickened.
Flake in the tuna and warm for 1 minute, then toss through the spaghetti with a splash of pasta water over low heat for 1 minute until glossy.
Stir through the parsley and serve with lemon wedges, if using.

stages.title: Cook the pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of water to the boil over high heat and stir in a generous pinch of salt so the water tastes like the sea.
Add the spaghetti and cook for 9–10 minutes, stirring in the first minute so it doesn't stick, until just tender with a little bite.
Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and leave it in the colander; don't rinse it, as the starch helps the sauce cling.

stages.title: Make the sauce
steps: While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 30–60 seconds, stirring, until the garlic is fragrant and pale golden; don't let it brown or it turns bitter.

Pour in the diced tomatoes, add the capers, 1 tsp salt and the black pepper, then simmer over medium heat for 6–7 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and no watery juice pools on the surface.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Flake the drained tuna into the sauce and stir gently for 1 minute, just until warmed through, as long cooking makes it dry.
Add the drained spaghetti and a splash of the reserved pasta water, then toss over low heat for 1 minute until the sauce coats every strand and looks glossy; add more water if it seems tight.
Stir through the parsley and serve straight away with lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Buy tuna in olive oil rather than springwater; it's more tender and flavoursome.
Salt the pasta water well, as it's the only chance to season the spaghetti itself.
Add the pasta water a splash at a time; it loosens the sauce and helps it cling.
Rinse the capers if they're very salty, and taste before adding extra salt.
variations: Add 1/2 cup pitted Kalamata olives with the capers for a puttanesca feel.
Swap the tuna for 2 cans of drained chickpeas for a vegetarian version.
Add 2 chopped anchovy fillets with the garlic for a deeper savoury flavour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat in a pan over low heat with a splash of water. Not ideal for freezing, as the pasta turns soft.

recipe.title: Prawn and chorizo pasta
recipe.summary: Spicy chorizo, juicy prawns and blistered cherry tomatoes tossed through spaghetti in a smoky paprika sauce, ready in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 500 g raw peeled prawns, tails on
method: Boil the spaghetti in salted water over high heat for 10 minutes, until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the pasta water, then drain.
Fry the chorizo in the olive oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes, until browned and the oil turns red.
Add the prawns with salt and black pepper and cook 1–2 minutes per side, until pink and curled.
Over medium heat, stir in the garlic and smoked paprika for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and chicken stock and simmer 3 minutes, until the tomatoes soften.
Toss through the spaghetti and a splash of pasta water for 1 minute until glossy. Top with parsley and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Prep and boil the pasta
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil over high heat, then cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes, or until al dente (tender with a slight bite).
While it cooks, slice the chorizo, halve the cherry tomatoes, chop the garlic and parsley, and pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Before draining, scoop out 1/2 cup (125 ml) of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and set it aside.

stages.title: Cook the chorizo and prawns
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat, then fry the chorizo for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until browned at the edges and the oil turns red.

Add the prawns in a single layer, season with salt and black pepper, and cook for 1–2 minutes per side, until they curl and turn pink and opaque. Don't overcook them or they turn rubbery; lift them out onto a plate if they finish before the sauce.

stages.title: Make the sauce and toss
steps: Reduce the heat to medium, add the garlic and smoked paprika, and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown or it will taste bitter.
Add the cherry tomatoes and chicken stock, then simmer for 3 minutes, scraping up the browned bits, until the tomatoes soften and the sauce reduces slightly.

Return the prawns to the pan, add the spaghetti and a splash of the reserved pasta water, and toss for 1 minute until the sauce coats the pasta. Scatter over the parsley and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the prawns dry before cooking so they sear instead of steaming.
Starchy pasta water helps the sauce cling to the spaghetti, so add it a splash at a time.
Use Spanish-style cured chorizo for the best smoky flavour; fresh chorizo needs a few more minutes of cooking.
Take the prawns out of the pan if the sauce needs longer, so they stay tender.
variations: Swap the prawns for 500 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 3 cm pieces and cooked for 5–6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the paprika for more heat.
Replace the spaghetti with short pasta such as penne or orecchiette.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as reheated prawns turn rubbery. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 1 day; reheat gently in a pan with a splash of water.

recipe.title: Lemon butter salmon with greens
recipe.summary: Pan-seared salmon with crisp skin, a light lemon butter sauce and tender green beans and broccolini, ready in 20 minutes.
method: Boil a pot of salted water on high. Cook the green beans and broccolini for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender, then drain.
Pat the salmon dry and season with salt and black pepper. Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Cook the salmon skin side down for 4 minutes until golden and crisp, then flip and cook 2 minutes until it flakes easily.
Turn the heat to low and melt the butter in the pan. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lemon juice, zest, parsley and water and simmer 30 seconds until glossy. Spoon over the salmon and greens.

stages.title: Prep
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil over high heat, and add a good pinch of salt once it is boiling.
Pat the salmon fillets very dry with paper towel, then season both sides with salt and black pepper. Dry skin is what gives you crisp skin.
Trim the green beans, cut the broccolini in half if the stems are thick, and finely chop the garlic and parsley.
Zest the lemon, then juice it into a small bowl and set both aside.

stages.title: Cook the greens
steps: Add the green beans and broccolini to the boiling water and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife.
Drain well and cover with a plate or foil to keep warm. Do not overcook them, as they will go dull and soft.

stages.title: Sear the salmon
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.

Place the salmon in the pan skin side down and press gently for 10 seconds so the skin stays flat. Cook for 4 minutes without moving, until the skin is golden and crisp and the flesh is opaque about two-thirds of the way up the sides.
Flip the fillets and cook for 2 minutes more. The salmon is cooked when the centre is just opaque and flakes easily with a fork. Move the fillets to a plate.

stages.title: Make the lemon butter sauce
steps: Turn the heat down to low and add the butter to the same pan. Once it melts, add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant but not browned.
Stir in the lemon juice, lemon zest, parsley and the water, and simmer for 30 seconds until the sauce looks glossy.
Divide the greens among four plates, top with the salmon, spoon over the sauce and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Dry the salmon skin thoroughly and don't move the fillets while they sear, or the skin won't crisp.
Take the salmon out of the fridge 10 minutes before cooking so it cooks more evenly.
Plunge the drained greens into cold water for 30 seconds if you want them extra bright, then drain again.
Add the garlic to the pan only once the heat is low, as burnt garlic turns the sauce bitter.
variations: Swap the salmon for ocean trout or barramundi fillets, and cook until the flesh flakes easily.
Add 1 tbsp of drained capers to the sauce for a salty, tangy kick.
Serve with steamed brown rice or baby potatoes for a more filling meal.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan over low heat or in the microwave on medium for 1 to 2 minutes, until just warmed through, so the salmon doesn't dry out.

recipe.title: Turkey lettuce cups
recipe.summary: Lean turkey mince stir-fried with ginger, garlic, carrot and water chestnuts, spooned into crisp lettuce cups for a light, high-protein dinner.
ingredients: 227 g can water chestnuts, drained and diced
method: Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat, then cook the turkey mince with the salt and pepper for 4 to 5 minutes, until no pink remains and it browns lightly.
Add the garlic, ginger, carrot and white spring onion and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the carrot softens slightly.
Stir in the water chestnuts and the mixed soy sauce, oyster sauce, vinegar, sesame oil and sriracha. Cook 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce bubbles and coats the mince.
Stir through the green spring onion, then spoon into the lettuce cups.
Top with coriander and peanuts, and serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Prep the filling and cups
steps: Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil and sriracha, if using, in a small bowl and set aside.
Finely chop the garlic, grate the ginger, dice the carrot and water chestnuts into 5 mm pieces, and slice the spring onions, keeping the white and green parts separate.
Peel 12 to 16 of the largest, most cup-shaped leaves from the lettuces, trimming the base so they sit flat, then pat them dry so the filling doesn't slide off.

stages.title: Cook the turkey
steps: Heat the peanut oil in a large frying pan or wok over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.

Add the turkey mince, salt and black pepper and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until no pink remains and the edges are lightly browned. Avoid stirring constantly, as the mince needs moments of contact with the pan to brown rather than steam.
Add the garlic, ginger, carrot and the white parts of the spring onions and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until fragrant and the carrot is just starting to soften.

Add the water chestnuts and the sauce mixture and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce bubbles and coats the mince with only a little liquid left in the pan. Take the pan off the heat and stir through the green spring onion tops.
To serve, spoon the filling into the lettuce cups and top with the coriander and chopped peanuts, with lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Dry the lettuce leaves well, as wet leaves go limp and make the cups soggy.
Don't crowd the pan. If your pan is small, brown the mince in two batches so it fries rather than steams.
Eat the cups straight away with your hands, as the hot filling will wilt the lettuce if it sits.
variations: Swap the turkey for chicken or pork mince, cooking it the same way until no pink remains.
For a vegetarian version, use crumbled firm tofu or finely chopped mushrooms, and replace the oyster sauce with hoisin.
recipe.storage: Keep the filling in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot pan or microwave until steaming hot. Assemble the lettuce cups fresh, as filled cups go soggy.

recipe.title: Tuna pasta bake
recipe.summary: A classic family bake of pasta, tuna, corn and peas in a creamy cheese sauce with a golden crumb top, made from pantry staples.
ingredients: 2 x 185 g cans tuna in springwater, drained
method: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced). Boil the penne in salted water for 8 minutes, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes until bright green, then drain.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4–5 minutes until soft. Stir in the flour for 1 minute until nutty.
Whisk in the milk and simmer 3–4 minutes until it coats a spoon. Off the heat, stir in the mustard and two-thirds of the cheese, with salt and pepper.
Fold the pasta, peas, tuna and corn through the sauce and tip into a baking dish. Top with the remaining cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 3 minutes, then top with parsley if using.

stages.title: Cook the pasta
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan-forced) and bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil over high heat.
Add the penne and cook for 8 minutes, stirring once or twice, until just tender with a little bite. Do not cook it fully, as it keeps softening in the oven.
Add the frozen peas for the final 2 minutes, then drain well once the peas are bright green and the pasta is al dente.

stages.title: Make the cheese sauce
steps: Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat, then add the onion and cook for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute until it forms a paste and smells slightly nutty.
Pour in the milk a little at a time, whisking constantly to avoid lumps. Simmer for 3–4 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the mustard and two-thirds of the cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Gently fold the drained pasta and peas, the tuna and the corn into the sauce, breaking the tuna into chunks, until everything is evenly coated.
Tip the mixture into a 2 litre baking dish and level the top. Scatter over the remaining cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 15 minutes, until the edges bubble and the top is golden brown.
Rest for 3 minutes so the sauce thickens slightly, then scatter with parsley if using and serve.

tips: Undercook the pasta by a minute so it doesn't turn mushy in the oven.
Add the milk slowly while whisking; pouring it in all at once is the usual cause of lumpy sauce.
Assemble the bake up to a day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge, then add 5–10 minutes to the baking time.
Use tuna in springwater and drain it well so the sauce doesn't turn thin or oily.
variations: Swap the tuna for shredded cooked chicken or a can of drained salmon.
Add 2 handfuls of baby spinach to the sauce along with the pasta for extra greens.
Stir in a pinch of chilli flakes and a diced red capsicum for more heat and colour.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days, or freeze portions for up to 2 months. Reheat in the microwave until steaming hot all the way through, or covered in a 180°C oven for about 15 minutes.

recipe.title: Pesto pasta with peas
recipe.summary: Spaghetti tossed with basil pesto, sweet peas, baby spinach and parmesan, a quick vegetarian dinner that comes together in 15 minutes.
ingredients: 1 tbsp salt, for the pasta water
method: Boil the spaghetti in salted water over high heat for 8 minutes, until al dente, adding the peas for the last 2 minutes until bright green.
Reserve 1/2 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and peas.
Warm the olive oil and spinach in the empty pot over low heat for 1 minute, until wilted.
Off the heat, toss in the pasta, pesto, parmesan, lemon zest and juice for 1 minute, loosening with pasta water until glossy.
Season with salt and black pepper, and serve with extra parmesan if you like.

stages.title: Prep
steps: Fill a large pot with about 3 litres of water, add the salt and bring it to the boil over high heat, which takes about 5 minutes.
While you wait, finely grate the parmesan, zest and juice the lemon, and measure out the peas, spinach and pesto so everything is ready to go.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and peas
steps: Add the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook for 8 minutes, stirring in the first minute so it doesn't stick, until al dente (tender with a slight bite in the centre).
Add the frozen peas to the pot for the last 2 minutes of cooking, until they are bright green and hot through.
Scoop out 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and peas in a colander. Don't rinse them, as the starch helps the pesto cling.
Return the empty pot to low heat and add the olive oil and the spinach. Stir for 1 minute, until the spinach just wilts.

Tip the pasta and peas back into the pot and take it off the heat. Add the pesto, parmesan, lemon zest and 2 tbsp of the lemon juice, and toss for 1 minute, until every strand is glossy and coated. Add splashes of the reserved pasta water if it looks dry or clumpy.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve straight away with extra parmesan if you like. Keep the pot off the heat when adding the pesto, as high heat makes it oily and dulls the basil.

tips: Keep a cup of pasta water before draining; its starch turns the thick pesto into a silky sauce.
Always add the pesto off the heat so the basil stays fresh and the oil doesn't split.
Toast a handful of pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 2 minutes and scatter on top for crunch.
Use fusilli or penne if you prefer; the peas catch in the twists.
variations: Add 2 cups of shredded cooked chicken with the pesto for extra protein.
Stir through 200 g halved cherry tomatoes and a drained 125 g tub of bocconcini for a caprese twist.
Swap the spaghetti for gluten-free pasta and check the pesto label.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in a pan over low heat with a splash of water, or microwave in 30-second bursts, stirring between each. Not ideal to freeze.

recipe.title: Bean quesadillas
recipe.summary: Flour tortillas filled with spiced black beans, sweetcorn and melted cheese, toasted until crisp and served with salsa for a quick vegetarian dinner.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 x 125 g can corn kernels, drained
1 cup chunky tomato salsa, to serve
method: Cook the onion in the olive oil over medium heat for 3 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic, cumin and paprika for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beans and corn and cook 2 minutes, mashing some beans. Stir in the lime juice, salt and pepper.
Spread the cheese and filling over half of each tortilla and fold over.
Toast in a medium pan with a light spray of oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, crisp and melted.
Rest 1 minute, cut into wedges and serve with the salsa, sour cream and lime wedges.

stages.title: Make the bean filling
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then cook the red onion for 3 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.
Add the black beans and corn, then cook for 2 minutes, mashing about a third of the beans with a fork so the filling holds together.
Stir in the lime juice, then season with salt and black pepper and tip the filling into a bowl. Wipe out the pan.

stages.title: Fill and toast the quesadillas
steps: Lay the tortillas on the bench and scatter the grated cheese over one half of each, then spoon the bean filling on top and fold each tortilla over to make a half-moon.

Heat the same pan over medium heat and lightly spray with olive oil. Cook 2 quesadillas at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and crisp and the cheese has melted. Avoid high heat, which burns the tortilla before the cheese melts.
Rest the quesadillas for 1 minute, then cut each into wedges and serve with the salsa, plus sour cream and lime wedges if you like.

tips: Mash some of the beans so the filling sticks together and doesn't spill out when you bite in.
Keep the heat at medium so the cheese has time to melt before the tortilla browns.
Press down gently with a spatula while toasting for even colour and crispness.
Grate the cheese yourself, as it melts better than pre-shredded.
variations: Add 1 diced jalapeño or 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the filling for more heat.
Add shredded cooked chicken or leftover pulled pork for a meat version.
Stir in a handful of baby spinach with the beans and let it wilt.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until crisp and hot in the middle.

recipe.title: Poke bowls
recipe.summary: Cubes of raw salmon in a soy sesame dressing over rice with edamame, cucumber and avocado, a fresh, high-protein dinner ready in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 500 g sashimi-grade salmon, skinless, cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Rinse the rice, then boil it with the water over high heat. Cover and cook on low for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Rest the rice off the heat for 5 minutes, then stir in 1 tbsp of the rice wine vinegar.
Whisk the soy sauce, remaining vinegar, sesame oil, honey and ginger until the honey dissolves.
Soak the edamame in boiling water for 3 minutes until bright green, then drain. Slice the cucumbers, avocado and spring onions.
Toss the salmon with some dressing until glossy, then pile it over the rice with the toppings, pickled ginger, sesame seeds, remaining dressing and lime wedges.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the sushi rice in a sieve under cold water for about 1 minute, until the water runs mostly clear, then tip it into a medium saucepan with the water.

Bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed and small steam holes show on the surface. Don't lift the lid while it cooks or the steam escapes and the rice cooks unevenly.
Take the pan off the heat and rest it, covered, for 5 minutes so the grains finish steaming, then stir in 1 tbsp of the rice wine vinegar and leave to cool slightly.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: While the rice cooks, whisk the soy sauce, the remaining 1 tbsp rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, honey and grated ginger in a small bowl for about 30 seconds, until the honey dissolves.
Keep the salmon in the fridge until you are ready to toss it, because raw fish should stay cold.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Put the frozen edamame in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water from the kettle and leave for 3 minutes, until bright green and tender, then drain well.
Slice the cucumbers, slice the avocado and thinly slice the spring onions, keeping the avocado for last so it doesn't brown.

Toss the salmon cubes with about 3 tablespoons of the dressing for 30 seconds, until evenly coated and glossy. Don't marinate for longer than a few minutes, as the acid and salt start to turn the flesh firm and opaque.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the warm rice among 4 bowls and arrange the salmon, edamame, cucumber and avocado on top in separate sections.
Scatter with the spring onions and sesame seeds, add a pile of pickled ginger, drizzle with the remaining dressing and serve straight away with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Buy fish labelled sashimi-grade from a fishmonger or the Coles or Woolworths seafood counter, and keep it in the fridge until the last minute.
Cut the salmon with a very sharp, wet knife for clean cubes that don't tear.
Cook the rice a little ahead and let it cool to warm, since hot rice will start to cook the fish.
Squeeze lime or lemon over the avocado slices if you are prepping the bowls early.
variations: Swap the salmon for sashimi-grade tuna, or use cubed firm tofu for a vegetarian bowl.
Add 1 tsp sriracha or chilli flakes to the dressing for some heat.
Use brown rice, cooked ahead, for a wholegrain version.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as raw fish is at its best and safest straight away. If there are leftovers, keep the fish and rice separately in the fridge and eat within 24 hours.

recipe.title: Turkey meatballs with zucchini noodles
recipe.summary: Baked turkey meatballs in a herby tomato sauce over zucchini noodles, a lean, vegetable-heavy take on spaghetti and meatballs.
ingredients: 1/4 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves, finely chopped
Small handful of basil leaves, torn
method: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Mix the turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, parmesan, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper, then roll into 20 balls and spiralise the zucchini.
Bake the meatballs for 15 to 18 minutes, until browned with no pink inside.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat for 4 minutes, until soft. Stir in the remaining garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes, until thickened. Stir in half the basil.
Add the meatballs and simmer on low for 2 minutes. Toss the zucchini in a dry pan over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes, until just tender.
Serve the meatballs and sauce over the zucchini noodles with the remaining basil.

stages.title: Shape the meatballs
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.

In a large bowl, combine the turkey mince, breadcrumbs, egg, 2 of the garlic cloves, parmesan, parsley, oregano, salt and black pepper. Mix with your hands for about 1 minute, just until combined, because overmixing makes the meatballs tough.
Roll the mixture into 20 balls, each about 3 cm wide, and place them on the lined tray with a little space between them.
Spiralise the zucchini into noodles and pat them dry with paper towel, so they don't turn watery later.

stages.title: Bake the meatballs and make the sauce
steps: Bake the meatballs for 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and cooked through. Cut one open to check that there is no pink inside.
While the meatballs bake, heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the remaining 2 garlic cloves and the tomato paste and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes, reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and a spoon leaves a trail on the base of the pan. Stir through half of the basil.

stages.title: Cook the noodles and serve
steps: Add the baked meatballs to the sauce and simmer on low for 2 minutes, until coated and piping hot.

At the same time, heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat with no oil. Toss the zucchini noodles with tongs for 1 to 2 minutes, until just tender but still with some bite. Don't cook them any longer or they will go soft and release water.
Divide the zucchini noodles among four bowls, spoon over the meatballs and sauce, and scatter with the remaining basil.

tips: Pat the zucchini noodles dry and cook them for no more than 2 minutes, or they will leave the sauce watery.
Wet your hands when rolling the meatballs so the mixture doesn't stick.
Make the meatballs and sauce up to 2 days ahead, then reheat and cook the zucchini just before serving.
Swap the zucchini noodles for wholemeal spaghetti if you want a more filling meal.
variations: Use chicken or lean beef mince instead of turkey.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the sauce with the garlic for a spicy arrabbiata-style version.
Stir a few handfuls of baby spinach through the sauce just before adding the meatballs.
recipe.storage: Keep the meatballs and sauce in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave until steaming hot, and cook fresh zucchini noodles when serving.

recipe.title: Flatbread pizzas
recipe.summary: Crisp flatbreads topped with tomato, mozzarella and ham or salami, baked in a hot oven in about 10 minutes for an easy weeknight dinner.
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line two trays. Mix the pasta sauce with the oregano, salt and pepper.
Place the flatbreads on the trays and brush the edges with olive oil.
Spread on the sauce, then add half the mozzarella, the ham, salami, capsicum, spinach and the rest of the mozzarella.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, swapping trays halfway, until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Rest for 2 minutes, top with basil if using, and slice.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Stir the pasta sauce and oregano together in a small bowl with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Tear the ham, slice the salami and capsicum, and grate the mozzarella if it isn't already grated.
Place the flatbreads on the trays and brush the edges lightly with the olive oil so they crisp up and don't dry out.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread the sauce over each flatbread, leaving a 1 cm border, then scatter over half the mozzarella.
Top with the ham, salami, capsicum and spinach, then finish with the remaining mozzarella. Don't overload them or the bases will turn soggy in the middle.
Bake in the 220°C oven for 8 to 10 minutes, swapping the trays halfway, until the cheese is melted and bubbling with golden spots and the edges are crisp.
Rest for 2 minutes, then scatter over the basil if using, and slice into wedges to serve.

tips: Pre-heat the trays in the oven for 5 minutes and slide the pizzas on for a crisper base.
Pat wet toppings such as mushrooms or fresh tomato dry so they don't make the base soggy.
Let the kids build their own pizzas with their favourite toppings.
variations: Vegetarian: skip the meats and add mushrooms, olives and sliced zucchini.
Hawaiian: swap the salami and capsicum for pineapple pieces and extra ham.
Spicy: add sliced jalapeños and a drizzle of chilli oil after baking.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh while the base is crisp. Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 2 days; reheat on a tray in a 180°C oven for 5 minutes.

recipe.title: Homemade pizza
recipe.summary: Classic pizza with a simple yeast dough, quick tomato sauce, mozzarella and fresh basil, baked hot for a crisp base and bubbling cheese.
ingredients: 500 g plain flour, plus extra for dusting
2 tbsp olive oil, plus extra for the bowl
250 g fresh mozzarella, torn into pieces
1 small bunch fresh basil, leaves picked
method: Mix the flour, salt, sugar, yeast, water and olive oil, then knead for 8–10 minutes until smooth and springy.
Cover the dough in an oiled bowl and rest 60–75 minutes in a warm spot, until doubled.
Heat the oven to 240°C fan-forced with trays inside. Simmer the garlic, tomatoes, oregano, salt and pepper in a pan over medium heat for 8 minutes until thick.
Divide and stretch the dough into 2 rounds, then top with sauce and mozzarella.
Bake each pizza 10–12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese bubbles.
Finish with basil and Parmesan if using, then rest 2 minutes before slicing.

stages.title: Make the dough
steps: Combine the flour, 1 tsp salt, sugar and yeast in a large bowl, then pour in the lukewarm water and 2 tbsp olive oil. Use water that feels just warm to the touch, as hot water will kill the yeast.
Stir with a wooden spoon until a shaggy dough forms, then tip it onto a lightly floured bench.
Knead for 8–10 minutes, until the dough is smooth, springy and springs back when poked. Add only a little extra flour if it sticks, because too much makes a dense base.

stages.title: Let the dough rise
steps: Lightly oil a clean bowl, add the dough and turn it to coat, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Leave in a warm spot for 60–75 minutes, until doubled in size and puffy.

stages.title: Make the sauce and heat the oven
steps: Heat the oven to 240°C fan-forced (or as hot as it goes) with two large baking trays inside so they get very hot.

Place a small saucepan over medium heat, add the crushed garlic with a splash of olive oil from the 2 tbsp measure if you have kept some back, and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Do not let it brown.
Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano, 1/4 tsp salt and black pepper, then simmer for 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened and no longer watery.

stages.title: Shape and bake
steps: Punch down the risen dough, divide it into 2 equal balls and roll or stretch each into a round about 30 cm wide on a floured sheet of baking paper.
Spread half the sauce over each base, leaving a 2 cm border, then scatter over the torn mozzarella.
Slide one pizza on its paper onto a hot tray and bake for 10–12 minutes, until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling with brown spots. Bake the second pizza the same way.
Top with basil leaves and Parmesan if using, then rest for 2 minutes before slicing. Add the basil after baking so it stays fresh and green.

tips: Preheat the trays for at least 20 minutes so the base crisps on contact.
Use low-moisture or well-drained mozzarella so the pizza doesn't turn soggy.
The dough can rise slowly in the fridge overnight for better flavour; bring it to room temperature before shaping.
variations: Add sliced salami or ham and olives before baking.
Make it vegetarian with mushrooms, capsicum and baby spinach.
Add chilli flakes to the sauce for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat slices in a 200°C oven for 8–10 minutes until crisp. Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipe.title: Minestrone
recipe.summary: A hearty Italian vegetable soup with cannellini beans and small pasta, finished with parmesan for a filling, budget-friendly main.
ingredients: 1 x 400 g can cannellini beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup small pasta, such as ditalini or small shells
150 g green beans, cut into 2 cm pieces
1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus extra to serve
method: Cook the onion, carrots and celery in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat for 6–7 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute, until fragrant and darkened.

Add the tomatoes, stock, parmesan rind, salt and pepper and boil over high heat for 3–4 minutes, then add the zucchini, green beans and cannellini beans and simmer on medium-low for 10 minutes, until the carrots are tender.
Stir in the pasta and simmer on medium for 8–10 minutes, until tender with a little bite.
Remove the rind, wilt in the spinach for 1 minute, then stir in the grated parmesan.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with extra parmesan and crusty bread.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat, then add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 6–7 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, tomato paste and oregano and stir for 1 minute, until the paste darkens slightly and smells fragrant. Don't let the garlic brown or it will turn bitter.
Dice the zucchini and trim and cut the green beans while the vegetables cook, so they are ready for the next stage.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Pour in the diced tomatoes and stock, add the parmesan rind if using, the salt and the pepper, and bring to the boil over high heat, about 3–4 minutes, until bubbling at the edges.
Reduce the heat to medium-low, add the zucchini, green beans and cannellini beans, and simmer for 10 minutes, until the carrots are tender when pierced with a fork.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and finish
steps: Increase the heat to medium, stir in the pasta and simmer for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then so it doesn't stick, until the pasta is tender but still has a little bite.
Remove the parmesan rind, then stir in the baby spinach for 1 minute, until just wilted and bright green.

Stir through the grated parmesan, taste and add more salt if needed. Rest the soup for 5 minutes so the flavours settle and the pasta finishes softening, then serve with extra parmesan and crusty bread if you like.

tips: Keep the parmesan rind in the freezer and add it to soups and sauces for a savoury, nutty depth.
For leftovers, cook the pasta separately and add it to each bowl, as it keeps absorbing liquid and turns soft in the fridge.
Use whatever vegetables are in the crisper, such as potato, leek or cabbage, adding firmer ones early and leafy ones last.
Finish each bowl with a drizzle of good olive oil for extra richness.
variations: Add 100 g diced pancetta or bacon with the onion for a smoky, meaty version.
Make it vegan by using vegetable stock and leaving out the parmesan rind and grated parmesan, finishing with a spoonful of pesto-style herb oil instead.
Stir in a pinch of chilli flakes with the garlic for a spicy kick.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 3 days, or frozen for up to 3 months (the pasta will be softer). Reheat gently on the stove until steaming hot, adding a splash of water or stock to loosen it.

recipe.title: Okonomiyaki
recipe.summary: Japanese savoury cabbage pancakes with crisp edges and a soft centre, topped with okonomiyaki sauce and Kewpie mayonnaise.
ingredients: 150 g bacon rashers, cut in half
method: Whisk the flour, dashi and salt until smooth, then whisk in 1 egg.
Fold through the wombok, spring onions and pickled ginger without pressing down.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, add a quarter of the mixture and top with bacon.
Cook 5 minutes until deep golden, flip, then cook 4 minutes until the bacon is crisp and the centre is firm.
Repeat with the rest, then top with okonomiyaki sauce, Kewpie mayonnaise, and bonito flakes and furikake if using.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Whisk the plain flour, dashi stock and salt in a large bowl until smooth, with no dry lumps remaining.
Whisk in 1 egg, then fold through the wombok, spring onions and pickled ginger until every shred is coated in batter.
Mix gently and avoid pressing down, as a loose, airy mixture gives a fluffier pancake.

stages.title: Cook the pancakes
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
