Add one quarter of the mixture and shape it into a round about 12 cm wide and 3 cm thick, then lay 3 or 4 bacon pieces on top.
Cook for 5 minutes, until the underside is deep golden and the edges look set, then flip in one confident motion and press lightly.
Cook the second side for 4 minutes, until the bacon is crisp and the centre feels firm when pressed. Crack in nothing more, as the batter already holds the eggs.
Repeat with the remaining oil, mixture and bacon, keeping cooked pancakes warm in a 100°C oven.
Brush each pancake with okonomiyaki sauce, drizzle with Kewpie mayonnaise and finish with the bonito flakes and furikake if using.

tips: Shred the wombok finely so the pancakes hold together and cook through.
Keep the heat at medium; too hot and the outside burns before the centre sets.
Cover the pan with a lid for the second side if the centre feels wet.
variations: Swap the bacon for peeled raw prawns or thinly sliced pork belly.
Leave out the bacon and add sliced shiitake mushrooms and corn for a vegetarian version.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for 2 days in an airtight container; reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 2 minutes each side, and add the toppings after.

recipe.title: Zucchini slice
recipe.summary: A baked slice of grated zucchini, carrot, onion, cheese and egg that's easy to make ahead and good hot or cold.
method: Heat the oven to 180°C fan-forced and line a baking tin. Grate the zucchini and carrot, then squeeze the zucchini very dry.
Cook the onion in olive oil in a frying pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, until soft, then cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs and vegetable oil. Mix the vegetables, onion, parsley, salt, pepper, flour and 1 cup of cheese, then stir in the egg until just combined.
Pour into the tin, top with the remaining cheese and bake 30-35 minutes, until deep golden and firm in the centre.
Rest 10 minutes so it sets, then cut into 6 and serve with tomato relish, if using.

stages.title: Prep the vegetables
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C fan-forced and line a 20 cm x 30 cm baking tin with baking paper, leaving a little overhang on the long sides.
Coarsely grate the zucchini and carrot into a large bowl, then squeeze the zucchini in handfuls or in a clean tea towel to remove the excess liquid; a soggy slice is the mistake to avoid.
Heat the olive oil in a small frying pan over medium heat, then cook the diced onion for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent but not browned, and let it cool slightly.

stages.title: Mix the batter
steps: Whisk the eggs and vegetable oil together in a jug until well combined.
Add the cooled onion, the parsley, the salt and the black pepper to the zucchini and carrot, then stir in the self-raising flour and 1 cup of the cheese until no dry flour remains.
Pour in the egg mixture and stir gently until just combined, then scrape into the lined tin and level the top with the back of a spoon.

stages.title: Bake and rest
steps: Scatter the remaining 1/2 cup of cheese over the top and bake in the middle of the oven for 30-35 minutes, until deep golden, puffed and firm to a light press in the centre.
Check that a skewer pushed into the middle comes out clean, with no wet egg on it; if it does, bake for another 5 minutes.
Rest the slice in the tin for 10 minutes so it sets and cuts cleanly, then lift out using the paper and cut into 6 pieces. Serve warm or at room temperature with tomato relish, if using.

tips: Squeeze the grated zucchini really well; it holds a lot of water and is the main cause of a soggy slice.
Cool the cooked onion before mixing so it doesn't start to cook the eggs.
Swap the tasty cheese for cheddar, or add a handful of crumbled feta for a saltier flavour.
Cut into squares and wrap individually to make lunchboxes easy.
variations: Add 1 cup of corn kernels or 1/2 cup of chopped semi-dried tomatoes for extra colour and sweetness.
Use 1 cup of wholemeal self-raising flour for a nuttier, more wholesome slice.
Stir in 1 tsp of chilli flakes or 1 tsp of smoked paprika for a bit of heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat in a 160°C oven for 10 minutes or microwave for 1 minute until hot through.

recipe.title: Tteokbokki
recipe.summary: Chewy Korean rice cakes simmered in a spicy-sweet gochujang sauce with fish cakes and boiled eggs, ready in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 200 g fish cake sheets, cut into triangles
4 spring onions, cut into 4 cm lengths
method: Soak the rice cakes in warm water for 10 minutes if hard or chilled, boil the eggs for 9 minutes until just set, then peel. Cut the fish cakes and spring onions.
Stir the water, dashi granules, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic in a pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until dissolved and bubbling.
Add the rice cakes and fish cakes, reduce to medium and simmer 8 minutes, stirring, until soft, chewy and the sauce is glossy and thick.
Add the eggs and spring onions and simmer 2 minutes until wilted. Season with salt, stir through the sesame oil and serve topped with sesame seeds.

stages.title: Prep the rice cakes and eggs
steps: If the rice cakes are hard or refrigerated, soak them in a bowl of warm water for 10 minutes so they soften and separate, then drain.
While they soak, place the eggs in a small saucepan of boiling water over medium-high heat and boil for 9 minutes until the yolks are just set, then cool under cold running water and peel.
Cut the fish cake sheets into triangles and the spring onions into 4 cm lengths, and crush the garlic.

stages.title: Make the sauce and simmer
steps: Combine the water, dashi granules, gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, brown sugar and garlic in a large deep frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir for 2 minutes until the gochujang dissolves and the sauce comes to a gentle boil.

Add the drained rice cakes and fish cakes, then reduce the heat to medium. Simmer for 8 minutes, stirring often so the rice cakes do not stick to the base, until they are soft and chewy and the sauce is glossy and thickened enough to coat a spoon.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Add the peeled eggs and spring onions and simmer for 2 minutes until the spring onions wilt and the eggs are heated through and tinted red.
Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed, then stir through the sesame oil. Remove from the heat and serve straight away, topped with the sesame seeds, because the sauce keeps thickening as it cools.

tips: Stir often while simmering, as the starch from the rice cakes thickens the sauce quickly and makes it catch on the pan.
Fresh or refrigerated rice cakes are in the fridge or freezer section of Asian grocers; soak frozen ones until pliable before cooking.
If the sauce gets too thick, loosen it with a splash of water.
Use less gochugaru for a milder sauce that kids will enjoy.
variations: Rabokki: add a packet of instant ramen noodles with an extra 1 cup of water in the last 4 minutes of simmering.
Cheesy tteokbokki: scatter 1 cup of grated mozzarella over the top, cover and cook for 2 minutes until melted.
Vegetarian: use vegetable stock instead of anchovy stock and skip the fish cakes, adding firm tofu cubes instead.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the rice cakes turn hard once cooled. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 2 days; reheat in a pan with a splash of water over low heat until soft again.

recipe.title: Pumpkin soup
recipe.summary: A smooth roast pumpkin soup with onion and a little cream, served with crusty bread for a filling winter main.
ingredients: 1.4 kg Kent pumpkin, peeled, cut into 3 cm pieces
1/2 cup (125 ml) thickened cream, plus extra to serve
1 crusty sourdough loaf, warmed, to serve
method: Roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp of the oil, salt and pepper at 220°C fan-forced for 25 minutes, until golden and tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in the remaining oil in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and cumin for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the pumpkin and stock and simmer for 5 minutes.
Blend until completely smooth, then stir in the cream and season to taste.
Reheat gently until steaming, swirl in extra cream and serve with the warmed sourdough.

stages.title: Roast the pumpkin
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.
Toss the pumpkin with 1 tbsp of the olive oil, 1/2 tsp salt and a pinch of black pepper on the tray, then spread it in a single layer so it browns rather than steams.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges are golden and a knife slides in easily.

stages.title: Cook the onion and simmer
steps: While the pumpkin roasts, heat the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and translucent but not browned.
Stir in the garlic and cumin and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant, then add the roasted pumpkin and the stock.
Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat and cook for 5 minutes so the flavours meld.

stages.title: Blend and serve
steps: Remove the pan from the heat and blend with a stick blender for 1–2 minutes until completely smooth, or blend in batches in a jug blender, filling it no more than half full and holding the lid down with a tea towel because hot soup expands.
Stir in the cream, then taste and season with extra salt and black pepper.
Reheat gently for 1–2 minutes without boiling, until steaming, then ladle into bowls, swirl through a little extra cream and serve with the warmed sourdough.

tips: Roasting the pumpkin until the edges caramelise gives far more flavour than boiling it.
Don't overcrowd the tray, or the pumpkin will steam and turn pale and watery.
If the soup is too thick, thin it with a splash of hot stock or water after blending.
Warm the sourdough in a 180°C oven for 5 minutes to crisp the crust.
variations: Dairy-free: swap the cream for coconut cream.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the cumin for a gentle heat.
Top with crisp bacon pieces and toasted pepitas for extra crunch.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 4 days or frozen for 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium-low heat, stirring, until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Mujadara
recipe.summary: A Lebanese dish of brown lentils and rice topped with deeply caramelised onions, served with cool garlicky yoghurt for a cheap, filling vegetarian dinner.
ingredients: 4 large brown onions (about 800 g), thinly sliced
method: Cook the sliced onions in the olive oil with some salt over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring, until deep golden brown. Rinse the lentils and rice.
Set half the onions aside. Stir the cumin, coriander and cinnamon into the pan for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the lentils and water, boil on high, then cover and simmer on low for 10 minutes, until starting to soften.
Add the rice, remaining salt and pepper. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until tender, then rest 5 minutes and fluff.
Mix the yoghurt, garlic and lemon juice. Top the mujadara with the onions and parsley, and serve with the yoghurt and lemon wedges.

stages.title: Caramelise the onions
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat, then add the sliced onions and 1/2 tsp of the salt.

Cook for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the onions are deep golden brown and sticky at the edges. Turn the heat down if they darken before they soften, because burnt onions turn bitter.
While the onions cook, rinse the lentils and rice in separate sieves under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.

stages.title: Cook the lentils and rice
steps: Scoop half the onions into a bowl and leave the rest in the pan with its oil. Add the cumin, coriander and cinnamon to the pan and stir for 30 seconds over medium heat, until fragrant.
Add the lentils and the water, bring to the boil over high heat, then cover, reduce to low and simmer for 10 minutes, until the lentils are just starting to soften.

Stir in the rice, the remaining 1/2 tsp salt and the pepper. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the rice and lentils are tender. Resist lifting the lid early, as the steam does the cooking.
Turn off the heat and leave the lid on for 5 minutes so the rice finishes steaming, then fluff with a fork.

stages.title: Make the yoghurt and serve
steps: Stir the yoghurt, garlic and lemon juice together in a small bowl until smooth.
Spoon the mujadara onto plates, top with the reserved onions and the parsley, and serve with the garlic yoghurt and lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Slice the onions evenly so they brown at the same rate, and don't crowd the pan.
Use brown or green lentils; red lentils break down to mush in this dish.
The onions can be caramelised a day ahead and kept in the fridge, then warmed before serving.
variations: Add a handful of baby spinach to the pan with the rice for extra greens.
Swap the rice for 1 cup of burghul (cracked wheat), reducing the water to 2 1/2 cups, for a more traditional wholegrain version.
Serve with a chopped tomato and cucumber salad for freshness.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for 4 days or the freezer for 2 months; reheat with a splash of water in the microwave or a covered pan until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Misir wot
recipe.summary: An Ethiopian red lentil stew simmered with onion, garlic and berbere spice until thick and rich, good with flatbread or rice.
ingredients: Flatbread or steamed rice, to serve
method: Rinse the lentils and drain; finely dice the onions and grate the garlic and ginger.
Cook the onions in the olive oil with the salt over medium heat for 8–10 minutes, until soft and just golden.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the tomato paste, berbere and paprika for 2–3 minutes, until the oil turns deep red.
Add the lentils, water and vegetable stock, boil on high, then simmer on low for 18–20 minutes, until thick and the lentils have broken down.
Season with the pepper, then serve with flatbread or rice and coriander if you like.

stages.title: Prepare the lentils and aromatics
steps: Rinse the red lentils in a fine sieve under cold running water for about 1 minute, until the water runs mostly clear, then drain well.
Finely dice the onions into pieces about 5 mm wide, so they melt into the stew, and grate the garlic and ginger.

stages.title: Cook the onions and spices
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based saucepan over medium heat, then add the onions and the salt.
Cook the onions for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until soft, translucent and just starting to turn golden; do not let them brown or catch, as this makes the stew bitter.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomato paste, berbere and paprika and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens and the oil turns deep red.

stages.title: Simmer the stew
steps: Add the drained lentils, the water and the vegetable stock to the pan and stir well, scraping up any spice from the base, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 18–20 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the lentils have broken down and the stew is thick like a loose porridge.
If the stew starts to stick or looks dry before the lentils are soft, add a splash of hot water; if it is too runny, simmer uncovered for 2–3 minutes more.
Season with the black pepper and extra salt if needed, then serve hot with flatbread or steamed rice, topped with chopped coriander if you like.

tips: Cook the onions slowly without browning them; this gives the stew its sweet, mellow base.
Berbere varies in heat between brands, so start with 2 tbsp if yours is hot and add more at the end.
Stir regularly in the last 10 minutes, as red lentils stick easily once they start to thicken.
The stew thickens as it cools, so loosen it with a splash of water when reheating.
variations: Add 2 tbsp of niter kibbeh or butter at the end for a richer, more traditional flavour.
Swap the red lentils for yellow split peas, and simmer for about 45 minutes until tender.
Stir in 2 big handfuls of baby spinach in the last 3 minutes for extra greens.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water, stirring, until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Nasi goreng
recipe.summary: Indonesian fried rice tossed with kecap manis, garlic and chilli, topped with a fried egg for a fast, filling weeknight dinner.
ingredients: 3 cups cooked jasmine rice, chilled (from 1 1/2 cups raw)
2 tbsp vegetable oil, plus 1 tbsp for the eggs
3 eggs, for the eggs on top
400 g chicken thigh fillets, cut into 2 cm pieces
150 g green beans, cut into 2 cm lengths
method: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat. Cook the chicken with the salt and pepper for 4 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Stir in the garlic, chillies and white spring onion for 30 seconds, then the carrot and beans for 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender.

Add the rice and fry for 2 minutes, until hot and separate. Pour in the kecap manis, soy sauce and sambal oelek mixed together and toss for 1 minute, until glossy and dark brown, then add the green spring onion.
Fry the eggs in 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks runny. Serve on the rice with cucumber and lime, if using.

stages.title: Prep
steps: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers so it fries evenly; day-old rice works best, as fresh warm rice turns mushy.
Slice the spring onions, finely chop the garlic and chillies, cut the chicken into 2 cm pieces, trim and cut the green beans, dice the carrot, and slice the cucumber.
Stir the kecap manis, soy sauce and sambal oelek together in a small bowl so the sauce is ready to pour in.

stages.title: Cook the chicken and vegetables
steps: Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large wok or frying pan over high heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Add the chicken, sprinkle with the salt and black pepper, and cook for 4 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and no pink remains in the centre of the largest piece.
Add the garlic, chillies and white parts of the spring onions and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic burn.
Add the carrot and green beans and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the beans are bright green and just tender.

stages.title: Fry the rice
steps: Add the rice to the pan and press it flat, then leave for 1 minute so it begins to crisp; stir and repeat for 2 minutes in total, until the rice is hot and the grains separate.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute, until every grain is evenly glossy and dark brown. Turn off the heat and stir through the green spring onion tops.

stages.title: Fry the eggs and serve
steps: Heat the extra 1 tbsp oil in a non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Crack in the eggs and fry for 2–3 minutes, until the whites are set and crisp at the edges and the yolks are still runny.
Divide the rice among bowls, top each with a fried egg (use the third egg to share or give it to the hungriest), and serve with the cucumber and lime wedges, if using.

tips: Use rice cooked the day before and chilled uncovered for a few hours; cold, dry grains fry rather than steam.
Keep the pan very hot and don't overcrowd it; cook in two batches if your pan is small.
Kecap manis is sold in the Asian aisle at Coles and Woolworths; if you can't find it, mix 2 tbsp soy sauce with 2 tbsp brown sugar.
variations: Swap the chicken for 300 g peeled raw prawns, cooking them for 2 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian by using 250 g firm tofu, cubed, in place of the chicken and cooking it until golden on all sides.
Add more heat with an extra chilli or a teaspoon more sambal oelek.
recipe.storage: Keep the rice without the eggs in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 1 day, then reheat in a hot pan or microwave until steaming hot throughout. Cook fresh eggs each time.

recipe.title: Black bean burgers
recipe.summary: Pan-fried black bean and oat patties served in toasted buns with avocado, lettuce and tomato, a filling vegetarian burger that holds together well.
ingredients: 2 x 400 g cans black beans, drained and rinsed
Extra tomato sauce or mayonnaise, to serve (optional)
method: Mash the black beans roughly, then mix with the onion, garlic, oats, egg, tomato sauce, spices, salt and pepper.
Rest 5 minutes, then shape into 4 patties about 2 cm thick.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat and cook the patties 5-6 minutes, until deep brown and crisp.
Flip carefully and cook 4-5 minutes more, until browned and hot through.
Toast the buns 1-2 minutes until golden, then fill with lettuce, tomato, patty, avocado and extra sauce or mayonnaise if using.

stages.title: Make the patty mixture
steps: Tip the black beans into a large bowl and mash with a fork or potato masher until about two thirds are broken down, leaving some whole beans for texture.
Add the diced onion, crushed garlic, rolled oats, egg, tomato sauce, smoked paprika, ground cumin, salt and black pepper, then mix well with your hands.

Rest the mixture for 5 minutes so the oats absorb moisture, then shape it into 4 patties about 2 cm thick; it should hold together when pressed, and if it is sticky and wet, add another tablespoon of oats.

stages.title: Cook the patties
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, until it shimmers.
Cook the patties for 5-6 minutes on the first side, until the base is deep brown and crisp and they release easily from the pan; don't move or flip them early or they will break apart.
Flip carefully with a wide spatula and cook another 4-5 minutes, until browned on both sides and hot through the centre.

stages.title: Toast the buns and assemble
steps: Toast the split buns in a dry pan or toaster for 1-2 minutes, until lightly golden on the cut side.
Layer each bun base with lettuce, tomato, a patty and sliced avocado, adding extra tomato sauce or mayonnaise if you like, then top with the bun lid and serve straight away.

tips: Leave some beans whole when mashing; a completely smooth mixture turns pasty and gummy.
Don't flip the patties until the underside is deeply browned and releases easily, or they will stick and crumble.
Shape the patties up to a day ahead and keep them covered in the fridge; chilled patties hold together even better.
Pat the beans dry with paper towel after rinsing so the mixture isn't wet.
variations: Swap the smoked paprika for 1 tbsp chipotle in adobo for a smoky, spicy kick.
Serve in a lettuce cup or on a wholemeal bun for a lighter version.
Top with sliced cheddar for the last minute of cooking to make a cheeseburger.
recipe.storage: Cooked patties keep in an airtight container in the fridge for 4 days or frozen for 2 months. Reheat in a frying pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes each side until hot through, and add fresh toppings and buns when serving.

recipe.title: Jollof rice
recipe.summary: A Nigerian party-style rice cooked in a smoky tomato, capsicum and chilli sauce until every grain is tender and richly coloured.
ingredients: 3 red capsicums (about 600 g), deseeded and chopped
2 onions, 1 roughly chopped and 1 finely diced
method: Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear, then blend the capsicums, tomatoes, chopped onion and chilli until smooth.
Fry the diced onion in the oil over medium heat for 4–5 minutes until golden, then cook the tomato paste for 3 minutes until deep brick red.
Stir in the curry powder, thyme, paprika and bay leaves for 30 seconds, then add the blend and stock cubes and simmer 15 minutes until thick and oily.
Add the salt, pepper and stock, bring to a boil, then stir in the rice, cover tightly and cook on low for 25 minutes until tender.
Rest 5 minutes covered, then fluff and serve with fried plantain if you like.

stages.title: Blend the base
steps: Rinse the rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1–2 minutes, until the water runs almost clear, then drain well.
Blend the capsicums, tomatoes, the roughly chopped onion and the chilli until completely smooth, about 1 minute.

stages.title: Reduce the sauce
steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat, then fry the diced onion for 4–5 minutes, until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring, until it darkens to a deep brick red.
Add the curry powder, thyme, smoked paprika and bay leaves and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Pour in the blended mixture, crumble in the stock cubes, and simmer over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and the oil floats on top. Do not rush this step, as a watery sauce makes mushy rice.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Stir the salt, black pepper and 2 cups of chicken stock into the sauce and bring to a boil over high heat.

Add the rinsed rice and stir once to combine, then cover the pot with foil and a tight lid. Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25 minutes, without lifting the lid more than once, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.
Turn off the heat and rest, covered, for 5 minutes so the steam finishes the grains. Remove the bay leaves, fluff with a fork and serve with fried plantain if you like.

tips: Use parboiled long-grain rice, as it stays separate and holds up to the thick sauce.
Cook the sauce until the oil separates on top; this gives the deeper flavour and the classic colour.
Cover the pot with foil under the lid for a tight seal, and avoid stirring once the rice is cooking, so the base can steam evenly and pick up a little smokiness.
Add the chilli seeds for more heat, or leave out the habanero and use a milder chilli.
variations: Add 600 g chicken thigh fillets, browned first and cooked in the sauce, for a one-pot meal.
Make it vegetarian by using vegetable stock and stock cubes, and stir through frozen peas and diced carrot with the rice.
Use prawns, stirred in for the last 5 minutes of resting, for a seafood version.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 4 days or frozen for 2 months. Reheat with a splash of water, covered, in the microwave or a pan until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Eggplant parmigiana
recipe.summary: Layers of golden fried eggplant, rich tomato sauce and melted mozzarella and parmesan, baked until bubbling for a comforting Italian main.
ingredients: 1/2 cup grated parmesan, plus 1/4 cup extra
1 cup vegetable oil, for shallow frying
method: Salt the sliced eggplant for 10 minutes until beads of moisture form, then pat dry.
Soften the onion and garlic in olive oil over medium heat, then simmer with the tomatoes, sugar, oregano and pepper for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in half the basil.
Crumb the eggplant in flour, egg and panko mixed with 1/2 cup parmesan. Fry in the vegetable oil over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden.
Layer the eggplant, sauce and both mozzarellas in a dish, then top with the extra parmesan.
Bake at 200°C fan-forced for 20 minutes until golden and bubbling. Rest 5 minutes and top with the remaining basil.

stages.title: Prepare the eggplant
steps: Cut the eggplants into 1 cm thick slices, lay them on a tray and sprinkle both sides with the salt.
Leave the slices for 10 minutes until beads of moisture appear on the surface, then pat them dry with paper towel so they fry crisp rather than steam.

stages.title: Make the sauce
steps: Heat the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat, then cook the onion for 4–5 minutes, stirring, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant, then stir in the crushed tomatoes, sugar, oregano and a good grind of black pepper.
Simmer over low heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and a spoon drawn across the base leaves a clear trail. Stir through half the basil and set aside.

stages.title: Crumb and fry the eggplant
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C fan-forced. Put the flour, the eggs (lightly beaten) and the panko mixed with 1/2 cup parmesan into three shallow bowls.
Dip each eggplant slice in the flour, then the egg, then press it firmly into the crumb mix so it is evenly coated.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat for about 2 minutes, until a breadcrumb sizzles straight away when dropped in.
Fry the slices in batches for 2–3 minutes per side, until deep golden and crisp, then drain on paper towel. Avoid crowding the pan, as the oil temperature drops and the crumb turns greasy.

stages.title: Assemble and bake
steps: Spread a thin layer of sauce over the base of a 20 x 30 cm baking dish, then add a layer of eggplant slices, slightly overlapping.
Top with more sauce, some of the sliced fresh mozzarella and a little grated mozzarella, then repeat the layers, finishing with sauce.
Scatter the remaining grated mozzarella and the extra 1/4 cup parmesan over the top.

Bake for 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden in patches and the sauce bubbles at the edges. Rest for 5 minutes so the layers hold together when cut, then scatter with the remaining basil.

tips: Salting the eggplant draws out moisture and bitterness, so don't skip the patting dry step.
Keep the crumbed slices in a single layer on a wire rack so they stay crisp until you assemble.
Make the sauce a day ahead; the flavour deepens in the fridge.
For a lighter version, bake the crumbed slices on oiled trays at 220°C fan-forced for 20 minutes, turning once, instead of frying.
variations: Add 150 g sliced leg ham between the layers for a meatier bake.
Swap the eggplant for crumbed zucchini slices, frying for 2 minutes per side.
Stir 1/2 tsp chilli flakes into the sauce for some heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for 3 days or frozen for 2 months. Reheat covered with foil at 180°C fan-forced for 20 minutes, removing the foil for the last 5 minutes.

recipe.title: Tofu and greens red curry
recipe.summary: Golden firm tofu and crisp greens in a light coconut red curry over brown rice, filling and ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 750 g firm tofu, drained and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 head broccoli (about 400 g), cut into small florets
200 g green beans, trimmed and cut into 4 cm lengths
3 baby bok choy (about 300 g), quartered lengthways
method: Boil the brown rice in a large pan of water over high heat for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew.
Fry the tofu in the oil over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden. Set aside.
Cook the onion over medium heat for 2 minutes, then stir in the garlic and curry paste for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, stock, broccoli and green beans and simmer 4 minutes, then add the bok choy for 2 minutes, until wilted.
Return the tofu for 2 minutes, then stir in the soy sauce, sugar, lime juice, salt and pepper. Drain the rice and serve with the curry and coriander.

stages.title: Start the rice and prep
steps: Bring a large saucepan of water to the boil over high heat, add the brown rice and boil for 25 minutes, until tender with a slight chew.
While the rice cooks, pat the tofu cubes dry with paper towel so they brown rather than steam.
Dice the onion, crush the garlic, cut the broccoli into small florets, trim and cut the green beans, and quarter the bok choy lengthways.

stages.title: Brown the tofu
steps: Heat the oil in a large deep frying pan or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 5–6 minutes, turning only every minute or so, until golden on most sides. Avoid stirring constantly, or the tofu will break up and stick.
Transfer the tofu to a plate and keep the pan on the stove.

stages.title: Simmer the curry
steps: Reduce the heat to medium, add the onion to the same pan and cook for 2 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic and red curry paste and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant and the paste darkens slightly.
Pour in the coconut milk and stock, scraping up any browned bits, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the broccoli and green beans and simmer for 4 minutes, until bright green and just tender when pierced with a knife.
Add the bok choy and simmer for 2 minutes, until the stems are tender-crisp and the leaves have wilted.
Return the tofu to the pan and simmer for 2 minutes to heat through.
Stir in the soy sauce, brown sugar and lime juice, then taste and season with salt and black pepper.
Drain the rice, which should be ready by now, and serve the curry over it, topped with coriander leaves.

tips: Pressing the tofu in paper towel for a few minutes before cooking gives a firmer, golden crust.
Red curry pastes vary in heat, so start with 1½ tablespoons if yours is hot and add more to taste.
Cut the vegetables to a similar size so they cook evenly and stay crisp.
Cook a double batch of rice and refrigerate half for quick lunches during the week.
variations: Swap the tofu for 600 g chicken breast strips, cooking them for 5–6 minutes until white throughout before adding to the curry.
Use zucchini, snow peas or capsicum in place of the beans and broccoli.
Add a thinly sliced red chilli with the garlic for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or frozen without the rice for up to 2 months. Reheat in a saucepan over medium heat until steaming hot throughout, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

recipe.title: Sweet potato and black bean chilli
recipe.summary: A smoky vegetarian chilli of sweet potato, black beans and tomatoes, topped with yoghurt and coriander, high in fibre and filling.
ingredients: 1 red capsicum, cut into 2 cm pieces
2 medium sweet potatoes (about 700 g), cut into 2 cm cubes
1 tsp chilli flakes, or to taste
2 x 400 g cans black beans, drained and rinsed
method: Cook the onion in the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and capsicum for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the paprika, cumin, oregano, chilli flakes and tomato paste for 1 minute until darkened and toasty.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, black beans, water, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then simmer gently for 20 minutes until the sweet potato mashes easily.
Stir in the lime juice, then top with yoghurt and coriander and serve with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat, then cook the diced onion for 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and capsicum and cook for 3 minutes, until the garlic smells fragrant and the capsicum starts to soften; don't let the garlic brown or it turns bitter.
Stir in the smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, chilli flakes and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens slightly and the spices smell toasty.

stages.title: Simmer the chilli
steps: Add the sweet potato, diced tomatoes, black beans, water, salt and black pepper, and stir well, scraping any spices off the bottom of the pot.

Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low-medium so it bubbles gently, cover with the lid slightly ajar and cook for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until a cube of sweet potato mashes easily against the side of the pot with a spoon.
If the chilli looks watery, cook uncovered for the last 5 minutes until it is thick enough to leave a trail when you drag a spoon across the base; add a splash of water if it catches on the bottom.
Stir through the lime juice, then taste and add a little more salt if needed.

stages.title: Serve
steps: Spoon the chilli into bowls and top each with a dollop of Greek yoghurt and a scatter of chopped coriander.
Serve with lime wedges on the side if you like.

tips: Cut the sweet potato into even 2 cm cubes so it cooks at the same rate and doesn't turn to mush.
Mash a few spoonfuls of the beans against the side of the pot near the end for a thicker, creamier chilli without adding anything.
Serve over brown rice or with a warmed wholemeal tortilla for a more filling meal.
The flavour deepens overnight, so it's a good one to make a day ahead.
variations: Add 500 g lean beef or turkey mince, browned after the onion, for extra protein.
Swap the black beans for kidney beans or a mix of both.
Add 1 to 2 chipotle chillies in adobo with the tomato paste for more smoke and heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat in a pot over medium heat with a splash of water, stirring until piping hot; add the yoghurt and coriander fresh.

recipe.title: Buddha bowl
recipe.summary: Roasted sweet potato and chickpeas over quinoa and spinach, topped with avocado and a lemony tahini dressing, for an easy meat-free dinner.
ingredients: 1 large sweet potato (about 500 g), cut into 1.5 cm cubes
2 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
method: Heat the oven to 220°C fan-forced. Toss the chickpeas with half the oil, paprika, cumin and salt; toss the sweet potato with the remaining oil, salt and pepper.
Roast both on separate trays for 20 minutes, shaking halfway, until the sweet potato is golden and tender and the chickpeas are crisp.
Meanwhile, boil the rinsed quinoa in the water over high heat, then cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, until the water is almost absorbed.
Scatter over the edamame, cover and rest off the heat for 5 minutes until the quinoa is fluffy, then fork it through.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, water and salt until pourable.
Fill bowls with quinoa, spinach, cucumber, avocado, sweet potato and chickpeas, then drizzle with the dressing.

stages.title: Prep and start the roast
steps: Preheat the oven to 220°C fan-forced and line two large baking trays with baking paper.
Pat the chickpeas dry with a clean tea towel, then toss them on one tray with half the olive oil, the smoked paprika, the cumin and a good pinch of salt.
Toss the sweet potato on the second tray with the remaining olive oil, a pinch of salt and some black pepper, then spread everything in a single layer so it roasts rather than steams.
Slide both trays into the oven, then rinse the quinoa in a fine sieve under cold water for 30 seconds to remove its bitter coating.

stages.title: Roast and cook the quinoa
steps: Roast the sweet potato and chickpeas for 20 minutes, shaking the trays halfway, until the sweet potato is golden at the edges and tender when pierced with a fork and the chickpeas are crisp.
While they roast, put the quinoa and the 2 cups of water in a medium saucepan over high heat and bring it to the boil.
Reduce to low, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the water is almost absorbed and you can see little curly tails on the grains.

Scatter the edamame over the quinoa, put the lid back on and take the pan off the heat for 5 minutes so the edamame thaws and the quinoa steams until fluffy, then fluff it with a fork and season with a pinch of salt.

stages.title: Make the dressing and assemble
steps: Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, the 3 tbsp of water and a pinch of salt in a small bowl until smooth and pourable like thick cream, adding a splash more water if it is stiff.
Divide the quinoa and edamame between four bowls, then top with the baby spinach, cucumber, avocado, roasted sweet potato and chickpeas.
Drizzle with the tahini dressing and finish with a crack of black pepper, adding the dressing just before serving so the spinach stays fresh.

tips: Dry the chickpeas well before roasting; wet chickpeas steam and stay soft instead of crisping.
Don't crowd the trays. Use two trays so the sweet potato browns instead of going soggy.
Make the dressing up to 4 days ahead; it thickens in the fridge, so whisk in a little water before using.
Cut the sweet potato into even 1.5 cm cubes so the pieces cook at the same rate.
variations: Swap the quinoa for brown rice, or use microwave brown rice pouches to save time.
Add a soft-boiled egg or a handful of crumbled feta to each bowl for extra protein.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the chickpeas for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keep the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, quinoa and dressing in separate containers in the fridge for up to 3 days; reheat the quinoa and roasted veg in the microwave until hot, and slice the avocado fresh as it browns.

recipe.title: Chickpea and spinach curry
recipe.summary: A fast, spiced chickpea curry with tomato and baby spinach, served over brown rice with a spoonful of yoghurt.
ingredients: 15 g fresh ginger (3 cm piece), finely grated
3 x 400 g cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed
2 x 250 g pouches microwave brown rice
200 g plain Greek yoghurt, to serve
method: Cook the onions in the oil in a large pan over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the garam masala, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli flakes for 1 minute until toasty.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, water and salt, then simmer over medium-low heat for 10 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Stir through the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted, then add the lemon juice and pepper.
Microwave the rice for about 2 minutes until steaming. Serve the curry over the rice with yoghurt and coriander leaves if using.

stages.title: Cook the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large deep frying pan over medium heat, add the onions and cook for 5 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add the garam masala, cumin, ground coriander, turmeric and chilli flakes and stir for 1 minute until the spices smell toasty. Add a splash of water if they stick, as burnt spices turn the curry bitter.

stages.title: Simmer the curry
steps: Pour in the diced tomatoes, chickpeas, water and salt, and stir well, scraping up any spices stuck to the base of the pan.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Press a few chickpeas against the side of the pan with your spoon to thicken the sauce slightly.

stages.title: Finish and serve
steps: Add the baby spinach a handful at a time and stir for 2 minutes until just wilted but still bright green.
Stir in the lemon juice and black pepper, then taste and add more salt if needed.
Heat the rice pouches in the microwave for about 2 minutes, following the packet, until steaming hot.
Divide the rice among four bowls, spoon over the curry, and top with the Greek yoghurt and coriander leaves if using.

tips: Rinse the canned chickpeas well to remove the tinny liquid and make the sauce taste cleaner.
Microwave rice pouches keep this a 30-minute meal, as cooking brown rice from scratch takes about 30 minutes on its own.
Add the lemon juice at the end, because cooking it dulls its fresh flavour.
Use frozen spinach if you like: add about 150 g straight to the pan and cook until thawed and hot.
variations: Add 400 g of diced sweet potato with the tomatoes and simmer for 5 extra minutes, until tender when pierced with a fork.
Swap the yoghurt for a splash of coconut milk stirred in with the spinach for a creamier curry.
Stir in 2 tbsp of tomato paste with the spices and add an extra pinch of chilli flakes for a richer, hotter curry.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat in a pan or microwave until steaming hot, adding a splash of water if it has thickened.

recipe.title: Mushroom and lentil bolognese
recipe.summary: A meat-free bolognese of finely chopped mushrooms and brown lentils in a rich tomato sauce, served over wholemeal spaghetti.
ingredients: 1 cup (200 g) dried brown lentils, rinsed
method: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 4 minutes, until soft.
Add the garlic, mushrooms and salt and cook 4 minutes, until golden. Stir in the tomato paste and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock and water, then bring to the boil. Simmer on low for 20 minutes, until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile, boil the spaghetti for 10 to 11 minutes until al dente, then drain.
Season with the pepper, then serve over the spaghetti with parmesan and basil if using.

stages.title: Prep the vegetables
steps: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery into pieces about 5 mm wide, so they melt into the sauce.
Crush the garlic and rinse the lentils under cold water in a sieve.
Finely chop the mushrooms into small, even pieces about 5 mm, as this gives the sauce a mince-like texture.

stages.title: Build the sauce base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large, deep frying pan or saucepan over medium heat, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 4 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is soft and translucent.

Add the garlic and mushrooms with the salt and cook for 4 minutes, stirring, until the mushrooms release their liquid and start to turn golden. Avoid overcrowding by stirring often, so they brown rather than steam.
Stir in the tomato paste and oregano and cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens slightly and smells rich.

stages.title: Simmer the lentils and cook the spaghetti
steps: Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, vegetable stock and water, then bring to the boil over high heat, which takes about 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are tender and the sauce is thick. Add a splash of water if it starts to catch on the base.

About 12 minutes before the sauce is ready, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water over high heat for 10 to 11 minutes, or following the packet, until al dente (tender with a slight bite). Drain, keeping a small cup of the cooking water.
Season the sauce with the pepper and extra salt if needed, then toss through a splash of the cooking water if it's too thick. Serve over the spaghetti, topped with parmesan and basil if using.

tips: Chop the mushrooms very finely, or pulse them in a food processor in short bursts, for a mince-like texture.
Don't add salt to the lentils until the mushrooms are cooked down; it's fine to season again at the end, once the lentils are tender.
A splash of the spaghetti cooking water loosens the sauce and helps it cling to the pasta.
Use a vegetarian-friendly parmesan, or skip it, to keep the dish fully vegetarian.
variations: Stir in 100 g baby spinach at the end for extra greens, letting it wilt for 1 minute.
Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the oregano for a spicy version.
Serve over zucchini noodles or with steamed vegetables instead of spaghetti for a lighter, lower-carb meal.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days, or the sauce alone can be frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat in a saucepan over low heat with a splash of water until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Greek chicken salad
recipe.summary: Oregano and lemon chicken breast sliced over a crisp Greek salad with feta and olives, a high-protein lunch that comes together in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 4 Lebanese cucumbers (about 400 g), cut into chunks
method: Slice the chicken breasts into 4 thinner fillets and marinate in the oil, oregano, lemon zest, 2 tbsp lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 4–5 minutes per side, until golden and white through the centre with clear juices.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice across the grain.
Toss the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, capsicum and olives with the vinegar, extra virgin olive oil and remaining lemon juice.
Top the salad with the chicken and feta, and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thinner fillets, so they cook quickly and evenly.
In a bowl, combine the olive oil, oregano, lemon zest, 2 tbsp of the lemon juice, garlic, salt and black pepper, then add the chicken and turn to coat. Leave it to sit while you prepare the salad.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan or chargrill pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until hot.

Cook the chicken for 4–5 minutes per side, until deep golden and the juices run clear when you cut into the thickest part; the centre should be white with no pink. Avoid moving the chicken around so it browns well.
Transfer the chicken to a board and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice across the grain.

stages.title: Build the salad
steps: In a large bowl, toss the cos lettuce, cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, capsicum and olives together.
Whisk the red wine vinegar, extra virgin olive oil and 1 tbsp of the remaining lemon juice in a small cup, pour over the salad and toss gently.
Divide the salad among 4 plates, top with the sliced chicken and crumbled feta, and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Slicing the breasts in half horizontally keeps the chicken juicy because it cooks in under 10 minutes.
Marinate the chicken in the fridge for up to 8 hours for more flavour.
Dress the salad just before serving so the cucumber and lettuce stay crisp.
Buy feta in a block and crumble it yourself; it is creamier than pre-crumbled.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g lamb backstrap, cooked 3–4 minutes per side for medium.
Make it vegetarian with 2 sliced haloumi blocks or a drained tin of chickpeas instead of chicken.
Serve in wholemeal pita pockets with a spoonful of Greek yoghurt.
recipe.storage: Store the cooked chicken and undressed salad separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days; serve the chicken cold or reheat in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes.

recipe.title: Tofu stir-fry with brown rice
recipe.summary: Crisp cubes of tofu and colourful vegetables in a ginger soy sauce over brown rice, a high-protein dinner ready in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 700 g firm tofu, drained and cut into 2 cm cubes
1 large head broccoli (about 400 g), cut into small florets
2 x 250 g microwave brown rice pouches
method: Pat the tofu dry and toss with 2 tbsp cornflour, salt and pepper. Whisk the soy, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, water and 1 tbsp cornflour into a sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp peanut oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the tofu 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp, then set aside.
Add the remaining oil over high heat and stir-fry the carrots 2 minutes, then the broccoli, capsicum and edamame 3 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Stir in the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds until fragrant, then add the sauce and cook 1 minute until thickened.
Return the tofu with the spring onions and toss 30 seconds. Microwave the rice pouches per the packet, then serve topped with the stir-fry and sesame seeds if using.

stages.title: Prep the tofu, vegetables and sauce
steps: Pat the tofu cubes dry with paper towel, as wet tofu will not crisp and will spit in the pan.
Toss the tofu in a bowl with 2 tbsp of the cornflour, the salt and the black pepper until every cube has a light, even coating.
Cut the broccoli, capsicum, carrots and spring onions, and keep the garlic and ginger together in a small bowl.
In a jug, whisk the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, honey, sesame oil, water and the remaining 1 tbsp cornflour until smooth, so the cornflour does not clump later.

stages.title: Crisp the tofu
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the peanut oil in a large non-stick frypan or wok over medium-high heat until it shimmers.

Add the tofu in a single layer and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning every minute or so, until all sides are golden and crisp. Avoid stirring constantly, as the tofu needs time against the pan to form a crust.
Tip the tofu onto a plate and wipe out any burnt cornflour from the pan.

stages.title: Stir-fry and finish
steps: Return the pan to high heat, add the remaining 1 tbsp peanut oil, then stir-fry the carrots for 2 minutes until they start to brighten.
Add the broccoli, capsicum and frozen edamame and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the broccoli is bright green and just tender but still crisp.
Add the garlic and ginger and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant, taking care not to let the garlic brown and turn bitter.
Give the sauce a quick whisk, pour it in and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until it thickens and coats the vegetables. Return the tofu and spring onions and toss gently for 30 seconds to heat through.
Heat the rice pouches in the microwave following the packet directions while the sauce thickens, then divide the rice among four bowls, top with the stir-fry and sprinkle with sesame seeds if using.

tips: Press the tofu between paper towels under a heavy plate for 10 minutes if you have time, for an even crisper crust.
Keep the pan hot and the vegetables moving so they stay crunchy instead of steaming.
Swap the microwave pouches for 1 1/2 cups of brown rice cooked ahead, which also suits meal prep.
variations: Use chicken breast strips instead of tofu, cooked until white through the centre and no longer pink.
Add 1 tsp chilli flakes or a spoonful of sambal oelek with the garlic for more heat.
Swap the broccoli and capsicum for snow peas, bok choy or green beans.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in the microwave until steaming hot; the tofu will soften but still taste good.

recipe.title: Haloumi and chickpea salad
recipe.summary: Golden grilled haloumi on a salad of chickpeas, rocket, cucumber and tomato with a fresh lemon and herb dressing.
ingredients: 250 g haloumi, cut into 1 cm slices
400 g can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
method: Whisk the lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, garlic, honey, salt and pepper, then stir in the parsley and mint.
Dry the chickpeas and put the rocket, cucumber, tomatoes and red onion in a large bowl.
Cook the chickpeas with the olive oil and cumin in a pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes until golden, then add to the bowl.
Fry the haloumi in the hot pan over medium-high heat for 1–2 minutes per side until deep golden.
Toss the salad with most of the dressing, top with haloumi, drizzle over the rest and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the dressing and salad
steps: In a small bowl, whisk the lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, crushed garlic, honey, a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper until the dressing looks slightly thick and combined.
Stir the parsley and mint through the dressing so the herbs stay bright green.
Pat the drained chickpeas dry with paper towel, as wet chickpeas won't crisp in the pan.
Place the rocket, cucumber, cherry tomatoes and red onion in a large bowl, ready to toss later.

stages.title: Cook the chickpeas and haloumi
steps: Heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat, then add the chickpeas and cumin and cook, shaking the pan often, for 3 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Tip them into the salad bowl.

Wipe out the pan if needed and return it to medium-high heat. Add the haloumi slices in a single layer, with no extra oil as the cheese releases its own, and cook for 1–2 minutes per side until deep golden brown and soft in the middle. Don't move the slices until they release easily, or they will tear.
Pour most of the dressing over the salad and toss gently, then divide between two plates, top with the hot haloumi, drizzle over the remaining dressing and serve with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Pat the haloumi dry before cooking so it browns instead of steaming.
Serve straight away, as haloumi turns rubbery once it cools.
Add a handful of toasted pita or Lebanese bread pieces for crunch.
Dress the salad just before serving so the rocket stays crisp.
variations: Swap the haloumi for grilled chicken thigh fillets seasoned with cumin for a non-vegetarian meal.
Add 1 tsp sumac to the dressing and a handful of pomegranate seeds for a tangy finish.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the chickpeas for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the haloumi goes rubbery and the rocket wilts. Leftover chickpeas, salad and dressing keep separately in the fridge for 2 days.

recipe.title: Chicken and quinoa salad
recipe.summary: A grilled chicken and quinoa salad with spinach, tomato and cucumber in a lemon dressing, filling and ready in 30 minutes.
method: Whisk the lemon zest and juice, extra virgin olive oil, garlic, mustard and pepper. Halve the chicken breasts into 4 steaks, rub with oil, paprika, half the salt and pepper, and chop the vegetables and parsley.
Simmer the quinoa, water and remaining salt in a saucepan over medium-high heat to a boil, then cover on low for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed. Stand covered for 5 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the chicken in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes per side, until golden with no pink inside.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice.
Toss the quinoa with the spinach, tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, parsley and half the dressing. Top with chicken and the remaining dressing.

stages.title: Prep the dressing, chicken and vegetables
steps: In a small bowl or jar, whisk the lemon zest, 3 tbsp lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, garlic, Dijon mustard and a pinch of the black pepper until it looks creamy and combined.
Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 even steaks about 1.5 cm thick, so they cook through without drying out.
Rub the chicken with the 1 tbsp olive oil, smoked paprika, half the salt and the remaining black pepper.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumbers, slice the red onion and chop the parsley, then set them aside with the baby spinach.

stages.title: Cook the quinoa and chicken
steps: Put the quinoa, water and the remaining salt in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat and bring to the boil, about 3 minutes.

Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the quinoa shows little curly tails. Take the pan off the heat and leave it covered for 5 minutes to steam. Don't lift the lid early, as the steam does the cooking.
While the quinoa simmers, heat a grill pan or frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until hot.
Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes per side, until golden with grill marks and no pink in the centre (75°C in the thickest part, if you have a thermometer).
Rest the chicken on a board for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it across the grain.

stages.title: Assemble the salad
steps: Fluff the quinoa with a fork and let it sit for a couple of minutes so it isn't piping hot, which would wilt the spinach too much.
Toss the quinoa with the baby spinach, cherry tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, parsley and half the dressing until everything is lightly coated.
Divide the salad among 4 bowls, top with the sliced chicken and drizzle over the remaining dressing.

tips: Rinse the quinoa under cold water in a fine sieve to remove its bitter coating.
Slicing the breasts in half makes them cook faster and more evenly, which keeps them juicy.
For lunchboxes, keep the dressing in a separate container and add it just before eating so the spinach stays fresh.
Swap the smoked paprika for ground cumin or sumac if you prefer.
variations: Swap the chicken for grilled salmon fillets or firm tofu.
Add 1 can of drained chickpeas and 100 g crumbled feta for a more filling vegetarian option, leaving out the chicken.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the dressing for some heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days, with the dressing stored separately; eat cold or at room temperature, and reheat the chicken only until just warm.

recipe.title: Tuna Niçoise salad
recipe.summary: A classic French salad of tuna, jammy eggs, baby potatoes, green beans, olives and tomato with a sharp mustard vinaigrette, filling and ready in 25 minutes.
ingredients: 2 x 185 g cans tuna in springwater, drained
1 baby cos lettuce (about 200 g), leaves separated
method: Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper into a thick vinaigrette.
Simmer the potatoes in salted water over medium heat for 5 minutes, then add the eggs for 7 minutes, until the yolks are jammy.
Add the green beans for the last 3 minutes, until bright green and tender-crisp. Cool the eggs in iced water, then peel and halve them.
Arrange the cos, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, red onion and olives on plates, top with flaked tuna and eggs, drizzle with the vinaigrette and serve with lemon wedges.

stages.title: Make the vinaigrette and prep
steps: In a small bowl or jar, whisk the olive oil, red wine vinegar, lemon juice, dijon mustard and grated garlic with a good pinch of salt and pepper until thick and glossy. Taste it and add a little more vinegar if it seems flat.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, slice the red onion thinly, separate the cos leaves and drain the tuna, then set everything aside. Fill a large bowl with cold water and ice, ready for the eggs.

stages.title: Cook the potatoes, eggs and beans
steps: Put the halved baby potatoes in a large saucepan, cover with cold water, add a generous pinch of salt and bring to the boil over high heat. Reduce to medium and simmer for 5 minutes.
Gently lower the eggs into the same pan and simmer for 7 minutes for jammy yolks, keeping the water at a steady simmer so the shells don't crack.
Add the trimmed green beans for the last 3 minutes, until they are bright green and just tender with a slight snap.

Lift out the eggs with a slotted spoon straight into the iced water. Check the potatoes are done by sliding in a knife; it should go through with no resistance. Drain the potatoes and beans and let them steam dry for 2 minutes.

stages.title: Assemble the salad
steps: Peel the eggs once cool enough to handle, about 2 minutes in the cold water, then cut them in half.

Arrange the cos leaves on two plates or a platter, then top with the potatoes, green beans, tomatoes, red onion and olives. Flake the tuna over the top in large chunks and don't stir it in, so it stays in pieces.
Tuck in the egg halves, then spoon over the vinaigrette just before serving so the leaves stay crisp. Finish with extra pepper and lemon wedges, if using.

tips: Dress the salad just before serving so the lettuce and beans stay crisp.
Cooking the eggs and beans in the potato water saves a pot and keeps the washing up light.
Choose tuna in springwater to keep the salad lean, or tuna in olive oil for a richer flavour and use the oil in the dressing.
Cook the potatoes, eggs and beans ahead and keep them cold in the fridge for a quick lunch the next day.
variations: Swap the canned tuna for seared fresh tuna steaks, about 2 minutes each side for a pink centre.
Add 2 tbsp of capers and a few anchovy fillets for a more traditional, salty finish.
For a vegetarian version, leave out the tuna and add a can of drained chickpeas.
recipe.storage: Keep the components and dressing separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 2 days, and assemble just before eating; it's best eaten cold, not reheated.

recipe.title: Salmon soba noodle salad
recipe.summary: Flaked pan-seared salmon tossed through cold soba noodles with edamame, cucumber and carrot in a sesame ginger dressing, an easy lunch that keeps well.
method: Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, honey, ginger, garlic and lime juice in a large bowl. Slice the cucumbers, carrots and spring onions.
Season the salmon with the olive oil, salt and pepper. Cook in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 3–4 minutes, then 2–3 minutes after flipping, until golden and flaking, then rest and flake.
Boil the edamame for 2 minutes, then the soba for about 4 minutes, until tender. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Toss the noodles, edamame, cucumber, carrot and spring onions through the dressing. Top with the salmon, sesame seeds and coriander if using.

stages.title: Make the dressing and prep the vegetables
steps: In a large bowl, whisk the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, sesame oil, honey, ginger, garlic and lime juice until the honey dissolves and the dressing looks evenly mixed.
Slice the cucumbers, cut the carrots into matchsticks and slice the spring onions, then set them aside on a board so they are ready when the noodles are done.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towel, then rub them with the olive oil and season both sides with the salt and black pepper. Dry fillets sear properly instead of steaming.

stages.title: Cook the salmon
steps: Half-fill a large saucepan with water, cover it and bring it to the boil over high heat while you cook the salmon.

Heat a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, then add the salmon. Cook for 3–4 minutes without moving it, until the underside is golden and the flesh looks opaque about two-thirds of the way up the side.

Flip the fillets and cook for 2–3 minutes more, until the salmon is just cooked through and flakes easily when pressed with a fork. Rest it on a plate for 1–2 minutes, then flake it into large chunks; do not overcook it or it will turn dry.

stages.title: Cook the noodles and edamame
steps: Add the frozen edamame to the boiling water and cook for 2 minutes, until bright green and heated through.
Add the soba noodles to the same pot and cook for about 4 minutes, or to the packet time, until tender but still slightly chewy. Stir once in the first minute so they do not clump.
Drain the noodles and edamame into a colander and rinse under cold running water for 30 seconds, until completely cool. Shake well, because wet noodles will water down the dressing.

stages.title: Toss the salad
steps: Add the noodles and edamame to the bowl with the dressing, along with the cucumber, carrot and spring onions. Toss with tongs for about 1 minute, until every strand is glossy with dressing.
Divide the salad among four bowls, top with the flaked salmon and sprinkle over the sesame seeds. Add coriander leaves if using, and serve straight away.

tips: Rinse the cooked soba under cold water until completely cool, which stops the cooking and washes off the starch that makes them gluey.
Cook the salmon until it just flakes. It keeps cooking while it rests, so pull it off the heat slightly early.
Check the soba packet, as some brands are 100% buckwheat and gluten-free, while others contain wheat.
Make the dressing up to 3 days ahead and keep it in a jar in the fridge; shake it well before using.
variations: Swap the salmon for 600 g of firm tofu, pressed and pan-fried until golden, for a vegetarian version.
Use two cans of drained tuna or shredded cooked chicken breast instead of salmon for a no-cook protein.
Add 1 tsp of chilli flakes or a thinly sliced red chilli to the dressing for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 2 days; serve cold or at room temperature, and toss with a splash of water or lime juice to loosen the noodles. Not suitable to freeze.

recipe.title: Prawn and mango salad
recipe.summary: A fresh no-cook salad of cooked prawns, ripe mango and avocado with a lime and chilli dressing, high in protein and ready in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 600 g cooked prawns, peeled, tails on
1 small red onion (about 100 g), thinly sliced
method: Whisk the lime zest, 2 limes' juice, oil, fish sauce, honey, chilli, salt and pepper, then soak the red onion in it for 5 minutes until pink.
Pat the prawns dry, then cube the mango, slice the cucumbers and pick the coriander.
Slice the avocados and squeeze over the last lime's juice so they stay green.
Toss the prawns, mango, cucumber, leaves and coriander in the dressing until lightly coated, then gently fold in the avocado.
Serve straight away with lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Make the dressing
steps: Whisk the lime zest, the juice of 2 limes, olive oil, fish sauce, honey, chilli, salt and pepper in a large bowl until the honey dissolves and the dressing looks slightly thickened.
Add the sliced red onion and leave it for 5 minutes, until it turns a little pink and loses its raw bite.

stages.title: Prep the salad
steps: Pat the prawns dry with paper towel so they don't water down the dressing, then check each one for any stray shell.
Cut the mango into 2 cm cubes, slice the cucumbers into thin half-moons and pick the coriander leaves from the stems.
Slice the avocados last so they stay bright green, and squeeze the juice of the remaining lime over them to stop browning.

stages.title: Toss and serve
steps: Add the prawns, mango, cucumber, mixed leaves and coriander to the bowl with the dressing and toss gently until everything is lightly coated and the leaves still look crisp.
Fold through the avocado with a light hand, because rough mixing will turn it mushy, then divide among 4 plates and serve straight away with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Buy prawns that smell clean and sea-fresh, and keep them chilled until you make the salad.
Choose mangoes that give slightly when pressed so the cubes stay firm and sweet.
Make the dressing and slice the onion up to a day ahead, then add the rest just before serving.
Serve with a slice of wholegrain toast or cooked brown rice if you want a more filling meal.
variations: Swap the prawns for shredded barbecue chicken or flaked hot-smoked salmon.
Make it vegetarian with firm tofu, marinated in the dressing for 10 minutes, and use soy sauce instead of fish sauce.
Add a second chilli or a pinch of chilli flakes for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the avocado browns and the leaves wilt in the dressing; keep leftover undressed prawns and mango in the fridge for up to 1 day.

recipe.title: Turkey and hummus wraps
recipe.summary: Wholemeal wraps filled with sliced turkey, hummus, spinach, cucumber and carrot, a quick lunch that is high in protein and light on fat.
method: Toss the carrot and cucumber with the lemon juice, salt and pepper, and pat away extra moisture.
Spread the hummus over the wraps, leaving a 3 cm border.
Layer the spinach, turkey and vegetable mixture on top, and sprinkle with sumac if using.
Fold in the sides and roll up tightly, then slice in half on an angle and serve.

stages.title: Prep the fillings
steps: Toss the grated carrot and sliced cucumber in a small bowl with the lemon juice, salt and black pepper, so the vegetables are lightly seasoned and taste fresh.
Pat the cucumber slices with paper towel if they look wet, because extra moisture will make the wraps soggy.

stages.title: Assemble and roll
steps: Lay the wraps flat on a board and spread the hummus over each one, leaving a 3 cm border around the edge so the filling stays inside.
Layer the baby spinach across the centre of each wrap, then add the sliced turkey, followed by the carrot and cucumber mixture. Sprinkle with the sumac if using.
Fold in the two sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom, tucking in the filling as you go. Do not overfill, or the wrap will tear when you roll it.
Cut each wrap in half on an angle with a sharp knife and serve straight away.

tips: Warm the wraps for 10 seconds in the microwave so they fold without cracking.
Pat the cucumber dry so the wraps do not go soggy, especially if packing them for lunch.
Use roasted capsicum hummus for extra flavour without adding much effort.
variations: Swap the turkey for shredded barbecue chicken or tinned tuna.
For a vegetarian version, use falafel or a handful of chickpeas mashed with the hummus instead of the turkey.
Add sliced pickled turnip or a spoonful of chilli sauce for extra heat and tang.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge, wrapped tightly in baking paper or foil, for up to 1 day; best eaten fresh as the wrap softens over time. Not suitable for freezing.

recipe.title: High-protein chicken pasta salad
recipe.summary: A cold pasta salad with paprika chicken, spinach, corn and tomatoes in a lemony Greek yoghurt dressing that makes a filling, lean lunch.
ingredients: 1 tsp salt, plus extra for the pasta water
method: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally, rub with the oil, paprika, salt and pepper, and make the dressing from yoghurt, lemon juice, mustard, garlic and parsley.
Boil the penne in salted water over high heat for 10 minutes until tender, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Fry the chicken in a pan over medium-high heat for 5–6 minutes per side, until golden and white inside with clear juices.
Rest the chicken for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it.
Toss the pasta, corn, tomatoes, onion and spinach through the dressing, then top with the chicken.

stages.title: Prep the chicken, vegetables and dressing
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thinner pieces about 1.5 cm thick, so they cook evenly and don't dry out.
Rub the chicken with the olive oil, smoked paprika, 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and 1/4 teaspoon of the black pepper, then set aside.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, thinly slice the red onion and drain the corn.
In a large bowl, whisk the Greek yoghurt, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, crushed garlic, parsley and the remaining salt and pepper until smooth and pourable.

stages.title: Cook the pasta and chicken
steps: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil over high heat, then add the wholemeal penne and cook for 10 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender with a little bite.
While the pasta cooks, heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute until hot, then add the chicken.
Cook the chicken for 5–6 minutes per side, until deep golden and the centre is white with no pink, and the juices run clear. Avoid moving it around the pan, as it won't brown.
Drain the pasta and rinse it under cold running water for 30 seconds until no longer steaming, then shake off the excess water.

stages.title: Rest the chicken and toss the salad
steps: Move the chicken to a board and rest it for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it across the grain into strips.
Add the cooled pasta, corn, cherry tomatoes, red onion and baby spinach to the bowl of dressing and toss until everything is evenly coated.
Top with the sliced chicken and serve straight away, or toss gently once more so the chicken is coated.

tips: Rinse the cooked pasta under cold water so it doesn't keep cooking and the yoghurt dressing doesn't turn warm and thin.
Slicing the chicken breasts in half makes them cook faster and stay juicy, which is the easiest way to avoid dry chicken.
For meal prep, keep the dressing and spinach separate from the pasta and chicken until you're ready to eat.
Use a barbecue chook instead of cooking the chicken if you're short on time; shred about 3 cups of meat.
variations: Swap the chicken for 2 cans of drained tuna or 400 g canned chickpeas for a no-cook or vegetarian version.
Add 1/2 teaspoon of chilli flakes to the chicken rub and a diced chilli to the dressing for more heat.
Stir in a diced avocado and 100 g of crumbled feta just before serving.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 2 days, best with the spinach added fresh. Eat cold and don't freeze, as the dressing will split.

recipe.title: Chicken and avocado wraps
recipe.summary: Wholemeal wraps filled with spiced chicken breast, avocado, crisp lettuce, tomato and a lemony yoghurt dressing, ready in 15 minutes.
ingredients: 2 large chicken breasts (about 600 g), thinly sliced
method: Toss the sliced chicken with the oil, paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Stir the yoghurt, lemon zest and juice, and garlic together for the dressing.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan over medium-high heat for 5 minutes, until golden and no longer pink inside. Rest it for 2 minutes.
Warm the wraps in the pan over medium heat for about 15 seconds a side, until soft.
Slice the avocados, tomatoes and lettuce, spread the wraps with dressing and fill with the chicken and vegetables.
Roll up firmly, cut in half and serve.

stages.title: Prep the dressing and fillings
steps: Cut the chicken breasts across the grain into 1 cm strips, then toss them in a bowl with the olive oil, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and black pepper until evenly coated.
In a small bowl, stir the yoghurt with the lemon zest, 2 tbsp of the lemon juice and the grated garlic until smooth, then taste and add a pinch more salt if it needs it.
Shred the lettuce and slice the tomatoes. Leave the avocados whole until the last minute, because cut avocado browns quickly.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 1 minute, until a drop of water sizzles on contact.
Add the chicken in a single layer, working in two batches if it won't fit without crowding, because crowded chicken steams and turns grey instead of browning.
Cook for 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on the outside and white with no pink when you cut into the thickest strip.
Tip the chicken onto a plate and rest it for 2 minutes so the juices settle.

stages.title: Assemble the wraps
steps: Return the empty pan to medium heat and warm each wrap for about 15 seconds per side, until soft and lightly flecked, then stack them under a clean tea towel to keep warm.
Halve, stone and slice the avocados, then squeeze over a little of the remaining lemon juice.
Spread each wrap with the yoghurt dressing, then top with lettuce, tomato, avocado and chicken.
Fold in the sides and roll up firmly, then cut in half and serve straight away.

tips: Slice the chicken thinly and evenly so it cooks through in 5 minutes without drying out.
Slice the avocado just before filling the wraps, and squeeze a little lemon juice over it to stop it browning.
Cook the chicken and make the dressing up to a day ahead, then assemble cold for packed lunches.
Use a ripe avocado that gives slightly when pressed gently at the stem end.
variations: Swap the chicken for canned chickpeas, drained and fried with the same spices, for a vegetarian version.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the chicken, or a spoonful of sriracha to the dressing, for more heat.
Use lean turkey breast strips or firm tofu instead of chicken.
recipe.storage: Keep the cooked chicken and dressing separately in airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Assembled wraps are best eaten fresh because the avocado browns and the wrap goes soggy.

recipe.title: Prawn rice paper rolls
recipe.summary: Fresh rice paper rolls filled with prawns, vermicelli, herbs and crisp vegetables, served with a quick peanut dipping sauce.
ingredients: 1 Lebanese cucumber, cut into thin sticks
1 cup fresh Thai basil or coriander leaves
method: Soak the vermicelli in boiling water for 4–5 minutes, until soft and white, then rinse and drain. Halve the prawns lengthways and cut the carrot and cucumber into sticks.
Shred the lettuce and pick the mint and Thai basil or coriander leaves.
Whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, lime juice, soy sauce, sriracha and warm water until smooth and pourable, then top with the crushed peanuts.
Dip each rice paper round in warm water for about 10 seconds, until just pliable. Lay prawns, vermicelli, vegetables and herbs on the lower third.
Fold in the bottom and sides, then roll tightly until sealed. Cover finished rolls with a damp tea towel and serve with the sauce.

stages.title: Prepare the fillings
steps: Place the vermicelli in a heatproof bowl, cover with boiling water and leave for 4–5 minutes, until soft and white with no hard centre, then drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
