Slice each prawn in half lengthways so you have 32 halves, which makes the rolls neat and easy to bite.
Cut the carrot and cucumber into thin sticks about 8 cm long, shred the lettuce, and pick the mint and Thai basil or coriander leaves, then arrange everything within reach on a board.

stages.title: Make the peanut sauce
steps: In a small bowl, whisk the peanut butter, hoisin, lime juice, soy sauce and sriracha with 2 tbsp warm water until smooth and pourable like thin custard, adding another splash of water if it is too thick.
Spoon the sauce into a serving bowl and scatter over the crushed peanuts.

stages.title: Roll and serve
steps: Fill a wide shallow dish with warm tap water and dip one rice paper round in for about 10 seconds, until just pliable but still slightly firm, then lay it on a clean damp tea towel or board; it will keep softening as you fill it.
Lay 4 prawn halves in a row across the lower third of the round, cut side up, so they show through the paper.
Top with a small handful of vermicelli, some carrot, cucumber, lettuce, mint and Thai basil, keeping the filling flat and not overstuffed, which stops the paper tearing.
Fold the bottom edge over the filling, fold in both sides, then roll up tightly until sealed and the paper feels slightly tacky.
Repeat with the remaining rounds to make 12 rolls, keeping finished rolls under a damp tea towel so they do not dry out or stick together, and serve with the peanut sauce.

tips: Do not soak the rice paper for too long; it should feel slightly firm, as it keeps softening on the board.
Place the prawns first, cut side up, so they show through the wrapper for a neat look.
Keep the rolls covered with a damp tea towel and do not let them touch, or they will stick together and tear.
For extra protein, double the prawns or add shredded cooked chicken.
variations: Swap the prawns for shredded poached chicken or thin slices of grilled pork.
For a vegetarian version, use firm tofu strips pan-fried until golden and add avocado slices.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the rice paper turns tough and dry in the fridge. If needed, wrap rolls individually in damp paper towel and cling wrap and keep for up to 4 hours; the sauce keeps in the fridge for 3 days.

recipe.title: Chicken and corn soup
recipe.summary: A silky Chinese-style soup of tender chicken, sweet corn and egg ribbons that comes together in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 3 cm piece fresh ginger, finely grated
4 spring onions, whites and greens separated, thinly sliced
method: Fry the ginger and spring onion whites in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the stock, soy sauce and rice wine, and boil on high for 3 minutes. Reduce to medium-low, add the sliced chicken and simmer 4 minutes, until white through.
Stir in the creamed corn and corn kernels, and simmer 3 minutes, until hot and creamy.
Stir in the cornflour mixture and simmer 2 minutes, until the soup coats a spoon.
Swirl the soup and drizzle in the egg, then leave 30 seconds until ribbons set. Stir in the sesame oil, salt and pepper.
Serve topped with the spring onion greens and chilli oil, if using.

stages.title: Prep
steps: Slice the chicken breasts across the grain into very thin slices about 5 mm thick, then cut the slices into bite-sized strips. Thin slices cook quickly and stay tender.
Grate the ginger and slice the spring onions, keeping the white parts and green parts in separate piles.
Stir the cornflour and cold water together in a small bowl until smooth, and lightly beat the eggs in a jug so they pour easily.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger and spring onion whites for 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant but not browned.
Pour in the stock, soy sauce and Shaoxing rice wine, then turn the heat to high and bring to a boil, about 3 minutes.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and add the chicken, stirring to separate the strips. Simmer gently for 4 minutes, until the chicken is white all the way through with no pink in the centre. Avoid a hard boil, which toughens the chicken.
Stir in the creamed corn and frozen corn kernels, and simmer for 3 minutes, until the kernels are hot and the soup looks creamy and evenly mixed.

stages.title: Thicken and finish
steps: Give the cornflour mixture a quick stir, then pour it into the soup while stirring. Simmer for 2 minutes, until the soup thickens slightly and coats the back of a spoon.

Stir the soup in one direction to create a gentle swirl, then slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs in a thin stream. Leave it alone for 30 seconds, until the egg sets into ribbons, then stir once gently. Stirring too early makes the soup cloudy.
Turn off the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Season with salt and black pepper, tasting first because the stock and soy are already salty.
Ladle into bowls and top with the spring onion greens, and a drizzle of chilli oil if you like heat.

tips: Freeze the chicken for 15 minutes before slicing so you can cut it very thinly.
Pour the egg from a height in a thin stream for fine, silky ribbons.
Add the cornflour mixture slowly and stir it first, because the starch settles at the bottom of the bowl.
Use salt-reduced stock so you can control the seasoning at the end.
variations: Swap the chicken for 300 g peeled raw prawns, simmered 2 minutes until pink and curled.
Make it vegetarian with vegetable stock and 200 g firm tofu cubes instead of the chicken.
Add 1 tsp white pepper and a splash of Chinkiang black vinegar for a sharper, warmer soup.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a pot over medium-low heat, stirring, until steaming, and add a splash of water if it has thickened too much. It is not ideal to freeze because the egg ribbons turn spongy.

recipe.title: Lentil and vegetable soup
recipe.summary: A hearty red lentil soup with carrot, celery, tomato and cumin that is high in fibre and plant protein and easy to make in one pot.
method: Dice the onion, carrots and celery, chop the garlic and rinse the lentils until the water runs mostly clear.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the vegetables for 6–8 minutes until the onion is soft. Add the garlic, cumin and turmeric for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock and water. Boil on high, then simmer on low-medium for 15–18 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Stir in the spinach, lemon juice, salt and pepper for 1–2 minutes until wilted. Serve topped with parsley if using.

stages.title: Prepare the vegetables
steps: Dice the onion, carrots and celery into 1 cm pieces so they cook evenly, which takes about 10 minutes.
Finely chop the garlic, then rinse the red lentils in a sieve under cold water for about 1 minute until the water runs mostly clear.
Measure out the spices, stock and water, and open the diced tomatoes so everything is ready before you start cooking.

stages.title: Build the base
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring often, until the onion is soft and translucent. Don't let them brown.
Stir in the garlic, cumin and turmeric and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Take care not to burn the garlic or the soup will taste bitter.

stages.title: Simmer the soup
steps: Add the lentils, diced tomatoes, stock and water, and stir well, scraping any bits from the base of the pot.

Bring to the boil over high heat, then reduce to low-medium and simmer, partly covered, for 15–18 minutes, stirring now and then, until the lentils are completely soft and the carrots are tender when pierced with a fork.
Stir in the baby spinach, lemon juice, salt and black pepper and cook for 1–2 minutes until the spinach wilts. Taste and add a little more salt if needed.
Ladle into bowls and scatter with chopped parsley if using.

tips: Rinse the lentils well to remove dust and reduce foam while simmering.
For a creamier soup, blitz about a third with a stick blender and stir it back in.
Add the lemon juice at the end, as it brightens the flavour of the lentils.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp chilli flakes with the spices for more heat.
Swap the spinach for kale and simmer an extra 3–4 minutes until tender.
Stir through 2 cups shredded cooked chicken at the end for extra protein.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days or in the freezer for 3 months. Reheat on the stove over medium heat, adding a splash of water, until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Miso soup with tofu and noodles
recipe.summary: A light Japanese-style noodle soup of miso broth, silken tofu, soba, spinach and edamame that is ready in 15 minutes.
ingredients: 1 litre water, for cooking the noodles
300 g silken tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Boil the 1 litre of water in a large pot over high heat and cook the soba for 4 minutes, until tender but chewy. Drain, rinse in cold water and divide between two bowls.
Simmer the 800 ml of water and dashi in a saucepan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until dissolved. Add the edamame and simmer 2 minutes, until bright green.
Turn the heat to low, add the tofu and warm for 1 minute, until heated through.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of hot broth until smooth, stir it into the pot and turn off the heat. Don't boil it.
Stir in the spinach for 30 seconds, until wilted, then ladle over the noodles and top with the spring onions.

stages.title: Prep the ingredients
steps: Cut the silken tofu into 2 cm cubes, handling it gently so it doesn't break up, and thinly slice the spring onions.
Measure the miso paste into a small bowl and set out the baby spinach, edamame and dashi granules next to the stove so everything is ready to go.

stages.title: Cook the noodles
steps: Bring the 1 litre of water to a boil in a large pot over high heat, then add the soba noodles and stir so they don't clump.
Cook for 4 minutes, until the noodles are tender but still slightly chewy, then drain and rinse well under cold running water to remove the surface starch, which can make the soup cloudy and gluey.
Divide the noodles between two deep bowls.

stages.title: Make the soup
steps: Combine the 800 ml of water and the dashi granules in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat and bring to a gentle simmer, about 2 minutes, until the granules have dissolved.
Add the edamame and simmer for 2 minutes, until they are bright green and tender.
Reduce the heat to low, add the tofu and warm for 1 minute, until heated through, stirring gently so the cubes stay whole.

Ladle about 100 ml of hot broth into the bowl of miso and whisk until smooth, then stir it back into the pot and turn off the heat. Don't let the soup boil after the miso goes in, as boiling dulls its flavour.
Add the spinach and stir for about 30 seconds, until just wilted, then ladle the soup over the noodles and top with the spring onions.

tips: Check the soba packet, as some brands are wheat-heavy and some are 100% buckwheat, which is gluten-free.
Rinsing the noodles in cold water stops them cooking and keeps the broth clear.
Different miso pastes vary in saltiness, so start with 2 tbsp and add more to taste before serving.
For a more filling lunch, add a soft-boiled egg to each bowl.
variations: Swap the tofu for 200 g of sliced cooked chicken breast, added with the spinach just to warm through.
Add 100 g of sliced shiitake mushrooms to the broth with the edamame and simmer 3 minutes, until soft.
Stir in a pinch of chilli flakes or a drizzle of chilli oil at the end for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the noodles go soft and the miso flavour fades. If you have leftovers, keep the broth and noodles separately in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheat the broth gently without boiling.

recipe.title: Roast pumpkin, feta and quinoa salad
recipe.summary: A hearty lunch salad of roast pumpkin, fluffy quinoa, baby spinach, feta and pepitas, finished with a lemon dressing.
ingredients: 800 g butternut pumpkin, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Roast the pumpkin with 1 tbsp oil, paprika, salt and pepper at 200°C fan-forced for 25 minutes, until golden and tender.
Simmer the quinoa and water, covered, over low heat for 12 minutes until the water is absorbed, then stand 5 minutes and fluff.
Toast the pepitas in a pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until they pop, then whisk the lemon juice, remaining oil, Dijon and honey.
Toss the quinoa with the onion and dressing, cool 5 minutes, then fold in the spinach and pumpkin. Top with feta and pepitas.

stages.title: Roast the pumpkin
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C fan-forced and line a large baking tray with baking paper.

Toss the pumpkin on the tray with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, the smoked paprika, a pinch of salt and some black pepper, then spread it into a single layer with space between the pieces so it roasts rather than steams.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once halfway, until the edges are golden and a knife slides in easily.

stages.title: Cook the quinoa
steps: Put the rinsed quinoa and the water in a medium saucepan with a pinch of salt and bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until the water is absorbed and you can see the small white spirals separating from the grains.
Take the pan off the heat, keep the lid on and stand for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork. Do not stir it while it simmers or it turns gluggy.

stages.title: Toast the pepitas and make the dressing
steps: Heat a small frying pan over medium heat and add the pepitas.
Toast for 2 to 3 minutes, shaking the pan often, until they puff up and start to pop, then tip them onto a plate straight away so they don't burn.
Whisk the lemon juice, the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, the Dijon mustard and the honey in a small bowl, then season with salt and black pepper.

stages.title: Assemble the salad
steps: Put the warm quinoa in a large bowl with the sliced red onion and the dressing, and toss so the quinoa soaks up the lemon.
Let it cool for about 5 minutes so the spinach doesn't wilt, then add the baby spinach and the roast pumpkin and toss gently.
Scatter over the crumbled feta and toasted pepitas, and serve warm or at room temperature.

tips: Rinse the quinoa under cold water for 30 seconds to remove the bitter coating.
Cut the pumpkin into even pieces so it all cooks at the same time.
Add the spinach only after the quinoa has cooled a little, or it will go limp.
For a packed lunch, keep the dressing separate and toss it through just before eating.
variations: Swap the feta for goat's cheese or haloumi cubes fried until golden.
Make it vegan by leaving out the feta and honey, using maple syrup, and adding a can of drained chickpeas.
Add 500 g of shredded cooked chicken for extra protein.
recipe.storage: Keeps in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days; serve cold or at room temperature, and add the pepitas just before eating so they stay crunchy.

recipe.title: Egg and avocado rice bowl
recipe.summary: Brown rice topped with soft-boiled eggs, avocado, kimchi and wilted spinach, a quick Korean-style lunch with plenty of protein and fibre.
method: Boil the eggs over medium heat for 6 minutes until the whites are set and yolks jammy, then chill in iced water and peel.
Microwave the rice for about 2 minutes until steaming hot.
Wilt the spinach in 1 tsp sesame oil over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes, then season with soy sauce, vinegar, salt and pepper.
Slice the avocado and mix the gochujang with the remaining sesame oil.
Top the rice with spinach, kimchi, avocado and halved eggs, then drizzle with the gochujang and scatter over the sesame seeds and spring onions.

stages.title: Cook the eggs and rice
steps: Bring a small saucepan of water to a rolling boil over high heat, then gently lower in the 4 eggs with a spoon.
Reduce to medium heat and cook the eggs for 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still soft and jammy; don't let them go past 7 minutes or the yolks will turn chalky.
While the eggs cook, heat the brown rice in the microwave following the packet directions, usually about 2 minutes, until steaming hot.
Transfer the eggs to a bowl of iced water for 2 minutes so they stop cooking, then peel them under the water.

stages.title: Wilt the spinach
steps: Heat 1 tsp of the sesame oil in a large frying pan over medium heat for 30 seconds, until it shimmers.
Add the baby spinach and cook, tossing, for 1 to 2 minutes, until just wilted but still bright green.
Stir in the soy sauce, rice wine vinegar, salt and black pepper, then take the pan off the heat so the spinach doesn't turn soggy.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Halve, stone and peel the avocado, then slice the flesh into thin pieces.
Mix the gochujang with the remaining 1 tsp sesame oil in a small bowl until smooth.
Divide the rice between 2 bowls and top with the spinach, kimchi and avocado.
Halve the eggs and place them on top, then drizzle with the gochujang mixture and scatter over the sesame seeds and spring onions. Serve straight away.

tips: Time the eggs with a timer: 6 minutes gives a jammy yolk, 8 minutes gives a firmer one.
Squeeze the kimchi lightly before adding it so the bowl doesn't turn watery.
Cook a batch of brown rice on the weekend and use it cold from the fridge, reheated in the microwave.
variations: Swap the eggs for 300 g of pan-fried firm tofu for a vegetarian bowl without the eggs.
Add 150 g of shredded barbecue chicken for extra protein.
Use 2 tsp of gochujang in the drizzle for more heat.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the avocado browns and the rice dries out; the cooked rice and peeled eggs keep separately in the fridge for 2 days.

recipe.title: Sushi bowl
recipe.summary: Seasoned sushi rice topped with fresh salmon, avocado, cucumber, nori and pickled ginger, a light lunch with all the flavours of sushi and no rolling.
ingredients: 300 g sashimi-grade salmon, cut into 1.5 cm cubes
2 nori sheets, cut into thin strips
method: Rinse the rice, then simmer it with the water over high heat for 2 minutes, until bubbling. Cover and cook on low for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed, then rest 5 minutes.
Cook the edamame in boiling water for 2 minutes, until bright green, then drain and rinse under cold water.
Fold the vinegar, sugar and salt through the rice for 1–2 minutes, until glossy and just warm.
Toss the salmon in the soy sauce and sesame oil for 30 seconds, until glossy.
Top the rice with the salmon, avocado, cucumber, edamame and pickled ginger, then add the nori, sesame seeds and lemon wedges if you like.

stages.title: Cook the rice
steps: Rinse the sushi rice in a sieve under cold running water for 1–2 minutes, until the water runs almost clear, then drain well.
Put the rice and the water in a small saucepan with a lid and bring to the boil over high heat, about 2 minutes, until you see steam and bubbles at the edge.
Reduce the heat to low, cover and cook for 10 minutes, until the water is absorbed. Avoid lifting the lid, as the steam is what cooks the rice.
Meanwhile, stir the rice vinegar, caster sugar and salt together in a small bowl for about 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves.
Take the rice off the heat and keep it covered for 5 minutes, which finishes the cooking and keeps the grains tender.

stages.title: Season the rice and prepare the toppings
steps: Cook the edamame in a bowl of boiling water from the kettle for 2 minutes, until bright green and tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.

Tip the cooked rice into a wide bowl and pour over the vinegar mixture. Fold gently with a spatula for 1–2 minutes, until the rice looks glossy and has cooled to just warm. Avoid stirring hard, which makes the rice mushy.
Mix the soy sauce and sesame oil in a small bowl, then toss the salmon cubes through it for 30 seconds, until evenly coated and glossy. Keep the salmon in the fridge until you serve.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the seasoned rice between two bowls.
Arrange the marinated salmon, avocado slices, cucumber slices, edamame and pickled ginger in sections on top of the rice.
Scatter over the nori strips and sesame seeds, spoon any leftover soy mixture over the salmon, and serve straight away with lemon wedges if you like.

tips: Buy fish labelled sashimi-grade from the fishmonger or the supermarket seafood counter, and keep it cold until you assemble the bowls.
Wet your spatula before folding the vinegar through the rice so the grains don't stick.
Cook the rice up to 2 hours ahead and keep it covered at room temperature, not in the fridge, where it turns hard.
variations: Swap the salmon for sashimi-grade tuna, or use 250 g of cooked prawns if you prefer cooked seafood.
For a vegetarian bowl, replace the fish with 200 g of firm tofu, cubed and pan-fried over medium heat for 5 minutes until golden.
Add heat by stirring 1 tsp of sriracha into the soy sauce and sesame oil mixture.
recipe.storage: Best eaten fresh, as the raw fish and avocado don't keep well. Leftover plain seasoned rice keeps covered in the fridge for 1 day, though it firms up as it cools.

recipe.title: Tofu poke bowl
recipe.summary: Soy and sesame marinated tofu over rice with edamame, cucumber, carrot and avocado, a fresh and filling lunch.
ingredients: 300 g firm tofu, cut into 2 cm cubes
method: Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, honey, ginger and garlic, then fold in the tofu and leave 10 minutes, until the edges darken.
Boil the edamame over high heat for 3 minutes, until bright green, then drain. Heat the rice until steaming.
Slice the cucumber, spring onions and avocado, and grate the carrot.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, until golden.
Divide the rice into bowls, top with everything, spoon over the leftover marinade and add lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Marinate the tofu
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice wine vinegar, honey, ginger and garlic until the honey dissolves.
Gently fold in the tofu cubes and leave for 10 minutes, turning once, until the edges look darker from the soy. Avoid stirring hard or the tofu will break up.

stages.title: Cook the rice and edamame
steps: Bring a small saucepan of water to the boil over high heat, add the edamame and cook for 3 minutes, until bright green and tender, then drain well.
Heat the rice following the packet directions, usually about 90 seconds in the microwave, until steaming hot and fluffy when broken up with a fork.

stages.title: Prepare the toppings
steps: Slice the cucumber and spring onions, grate the carrot and slice the avocado, keeping the avocado for last so it stays green.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden and nutty-smelling, then tip onto a plate straight away so they don't burn.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the rice between two bowls and arrange the tofu, edamame, cucumber, carrot and avocado on top.
Spoon the leftover marinade over the bowls, scatter with the spring onions and toasted sesame seeds, and serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Press the tofu between paper towels for 5 minutes before cubing so it soaks up more marinade.
Marinate the tofu up to a day ahead in the fridge for deeper flavour.
Squeeze lime over the avocado to stop it browning if you're packing the bowls for later.
variations: Swap the tofu for cooked shredded chicken or sashimi-grade salmon cubes.
Add a drizzle of sriracha mayo or a pinch of chilli flakes for heat.
Use sushi rice or quinoa in place of brown rice.
recipe.storage: Keep the tofu, rice and vegetables in separate containers in the fridge for up to 2 days. Add the avocado fresh and eat cold, or reheat the rice only.

recipe.title: Chicken burrito lunch bowl
recipe.summary: A meal-prep bowl of spiced chicken, brown rice, black beans, corn salsa and lettuce that is high in protein and keeps well for the week.
ingredients: 2 x 250 g pouches microwave brown rice
400 g can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cob corn, or 1 cup frozen corn kernels (about 150 g)
method: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally and rub with the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Mix the corn, tomatoes, red onion, lime juice and coriander into a salsa.
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 4–5 minutes, then 3–4 minutes on the other side, until golden and white through with clear juices.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then slice. Microwave the rice 2 minutes and the beans 1 minute, until hot.
Divide the rice, beans, chicken, salsa and lettuce among bowls, top with yoghurt, and add lime wedges if you like.

stages.title: Prepare the salsa and chicken
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to make 4 thinner pieces about 1.5 cm thick, so they cook evenly.
Combine the paprika, cumin, garlic powder, salt and black pepper in a small bowl, then rub the mix all over the chicken.
If using a fresh cob, cut the kernels off with a sharp knife; if using frozen corn, thaw it under hot water and drain well.
Mix the corn, diced tomatoes, red onion, lime juice and coriander in a bowl to make the corn salsa, and set aside so the flavours mingle.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until it shimmers.
Cook the chicken for 4–5 minutes on the first side, until deeply golden and releasing easily from the pan; don't move it early or it will stick and tear.
Flip and cook another 3–4 minutes, until the centre is white with no pink and the juices run clear (74°C on a thermometer).
Rest the chicken on a board for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it across the grain.

stages.title: Warm the rice and beans and assemble
steps: Microwave the brown rice pouches according to the packet, about 2 minutes, until hot and steaming.
Warm the black beans in a small bowl in the microwave for 1 minute, until hot through.
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and top with the beans, sliced chicken, corn salsa and shredded lettuce.
Finish each bowl with a spoonful of Greek yoghurt, and serve with lime wedges if you like.

tips: Slicing the chicken breasts thinner means they cook through quickly without drying out.
For meal prep, keep the lettuce, salsa and yoghurt in separate containers and add them after reheating the rest.
Use a meat thermometer if you have one; 74°C in the thickest part means the chicken is safely cooked.
variations: Swap the chicken for 600 g of firm tofu, pressed and cubed, for a vegetarian bowl.
Add sliced jalapeños or a pinch of chilli flakes to the spice mix for more heat.
recipe.storage: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days in airtight containers, with the lettuce and yoghurt stored separately. Reheat the chicken, rice and beans in the microwave until steaming hot.

recipe.title: Mediterranean chicken bowl
recipe.summary: Lemon and oregano chicken served over wholemeal couscous with hummus, cucumber, tomato and a parsley and mint salad, ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 1 small red onion (about 100 g), finely diced
1 bunch flat-leaf parsley, leaves finely chopped
method: Slice the chicken breasts in half horizontally, then toss with lemon zest, juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp oil, garlic, oregano, paprika, 1/2 tsp salt and pepper.
Cover the couscous with 1/4 tsp salt and the boiling water for 5 minutes, until all the water is absorbed, then fluff with a fork.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes, onion, parsley and mint with the second lemon's juice, the remaining oil and salt.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan over medium-high heat, 4–5 minutes each side, until golden with no pink and the juices run clear. Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Divide the couscous and salad among bowls, then top with hummus and the sliced chicken.

stages.title: Marinate the chicken
steps: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally so you have 4 even fillets about 2 cm thick, which cook through without drying out.
In a bowl, mix the lemon zest, the juice of 1 lemon, 1 tbsp of the olive oil, the garlic, oregano, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp of the salt and the black pepper.
Add the chicken and turn to coat well, then leave it to sit while you make the couscous and salad.

stages.title: Make the couscous and salad
steps: Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt, pour over the boiling water, then cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes, until all the water is absorbed and the grains are tender.
Fluff the couscous with a fork to break up any clumps, then set aside.
In a large bowl, combine the cucumber, cherry tomatoes, red onion, parsley and mint.
Squeeze in the juice of the second lemon, add the remaining 1 tbsp olive oil and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt, and toss. Dress it just before serving so the herbs stay bright green and don't go soggy.

stages.title: Cook the chicken
steps: Heat a large frying pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles straight away.
Lift the chicken out of the marinade, shaking off the excess, and lay it in the pan without crowding. Cook for 4–5 minutes, until the underside is golden and the edges look white.
Turn the chicken and cook another 4–5 minutes, until golden all over and the thickest part is white with no pink and the juices run clear, or reads 75°C on a thermometer.
Move the chicken to a board and rest for 5 minutes so the juices settle, then slice it across the grain. Slicing straight away lets the juices run out and the meat dries.

stages.title: Assemble the bowls
steps: Divide the couscous among 4 bowls and top with the herb and tomato salad.
Add a generous spoonful of hummus to each bowl, lay the sliced chicken on top and spoon over any juices from the board.

tips: Halving the chicken breasts horizontally gives thinner fillets that cook quickly and evenly.
Leave the salad undressed until just before serving so the cucumber stays crisp.
Swap the couscous for cooked quinoa or brown rice if you want it gluten-free.
Marinate the chicken in the fridge for up to 12 hours for deeper flavour.
variations: Use 600 g chicken thigh fillets instead of breast and cook for 5–6 minutes per side.
Make it vegetarian by swapping the chicken for thick slices of halloumi or a tin of drained, roasted chickpeas.
Add a pinch of chilli flakes to the marinade for some heat.
recipe.storage: Store the chicken, couscous and salad in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Eat the chicken cold or reheat it in the microwave for 1–2 minutes until steaming hot.
